# Scheduled Strengthening Log

An automated **daily feature audit** (Claude Code scheduled task `daily-feature-strengthening-audit`,
runs 6:00 AM Finnish time while the desktop app is open). Each run picks **two features** from the
Feature Registry below, scrutinizes their implementation, code quality, and test coverage, and
appends a dated entry here with findings and suggested improvements.

## Rules the audit follows

- **Rotation:** never audit a feature that appears in the **last 6 entries**. Because this repo
  lives on multiple machines, the last-6 check uses the **union** of this file and the origin copy
  (`git fetch` + `git show origin/master:docs/SCHEDULED_STRENGTHENING.md`). Among eligible
  features, prefer the least-recently-audited, tie-broken toward the **lowest coverage** in the
  Coverage Snapshot below.
- **Lap angles:** when every feature has been audited once, the rotation starts a new lap with a
  different lens, so repeat visits stay valuable instead of repetitive:
  - **Lap 1 — correctness & test depth** (bugs, edge cases, untested branches)
  - **Lap 2 — robustness against hostile input** (malformed LLM output, malformed/stale saves, imports)
  - **Lap 3 — performance & token budget** (prompt size, re-renders, IndexedDB churn, call counts)
  - **Lap 4 — simplification & design** (dead code, duplication, better structure)
  - then cycle back to Lap 1.
- **Report-only, but self-committing:** the audit changes no production code or tests. Findings
  land here; actionable items go to the Open Findings Queue (and genuinely new ideas to
  `docs/IDEAS.md` tagged `[strengthening]`). Fixes happen in normal sessions. Unlike a normal
  session, this task DOES commit and push its own output — this file (and `docs/IDEAS.md` when
  amended) go straight to `origin master` at the end of each run, so findings are readable
  remotely without a manual commit (2026-07-16: Vesa evaluates entries with a separate agent).
- **Severity tags:** every finding is tagged **P0** (live bug / data loss / broken invariant),
  **P1** (real gap likely to bite), or **P2** (polish, coverage, simplification).
- **Red suite = the finding of the day:** if `npm test` fails, the entry leads with that,
  diagnosis-only, still no fixes.
- **Respect `docs/DECISIONS.md`:** never recommend reversing a settled decision without flagging
  that it is one.
- **Newest entry first**, dated `YYYY-MM-DD`, features named in the heading, entry kept skimmable
  (aim under ~50 lines).

## Open Findings Queue

Actionable items distilled from audit entries, for normal sessions to pick up. The audit **adds**
items here (deduped against open *and* checked items) and may check one off `[x]` with a date when
it verifies the code has since been fixed. Normal sessions: skim this when picking hardening work,
fix, then tick with the date and a short note.

Format: `- [ ] **P1** (feature-id, YYYY-MM-DD): description — file:line`

- [x] **P2** (dice-engine, 2026-10-04): the roll ledger has no membership rule — an out-of-combat `spell_cast` heal (`handlers/spellcasting.js:183`) and a Short Rest's hit dice (`handlers/resources.js:266`) roll real hero dice that never reach `rollHistory` (no `appendRollHistory` import in either file), while the potion beside them does; state the rule once ("a die the HERO's action rolled enters the ledger"), append at both lanes, and delete `exchangeLedgerRolls`'s dead `payload.rolls` fallback (`handlers/combat.js:30-33` — every plan branch emits `heroRolls`, `combatExchange.js:1652,1749,1834`; only test payloads lack it) — `src/state/handlers/spellcasting.js`, `src/state/handlers/resources.js`, `src/state/handlers/combat.js` *Fixed 2026-10-04: the rule is stated once on `appendRollHistory(state, rolls)` (`handlers/shared.js`: a die the HERO's own action rolled enters the ledger; another actor's never does); an out-of-combat spell heal appends one entry per recipient and a Short Rest's hit dice ONE entry whose total is the healing rolled; `exchangeLedgerRolls` and its `payload.rolls` fallback are deleted (an exchange ledgers `heroRolls` only). ## 2026-10-04 — dice-engine + cloud-sync (Lap 4: simplification & design)

`npm test`: 3407 passing / 204 files (green — after `npm ci`; see Process notes).

Rotation: origin was two commits ahead (the 10-03 Sol playtest + the bake-off) — fast-forwarded first; the last-6 union excludes living-world, scene-art (10-03), progression, hidden-fronts (10-02), memory-journal, chat-orchestration (10-01), story-memory, prompt-building (09-30), providers-adapter, vector-memory-rag (09-29), response-parsing, scribe (09-28). Oldest eligible is **dice-engine** (09-21, Lap 3 done); roll-resolution and cloud-sync tie at 09-22, broken toward **cloud-sync** (`auth.js` 78.94† is the snapshot's lowest row). Both take **Lap 4 (simplification & design)** by the 10-02 method: every export's importers before its body, every persisted key's READERS, every lane diffed against the lane that does the same thing. Grep-and-read only; no repo file outside the two docs touched. Coverage snapshot is 4 days old — not refreshed. **Every open dice-engine (09-21) and cloud-sync (09-22, 09-26) queue line was already ticked** and verified in code: `newestRollMarker` (`turnOrchestrator.js:136`), `heroRolls` (`combatExchange.js:1624`), the known-key projection (`shared.js:55-86`), the on-demand SDK (`firebase.js:30`), the blob lanes (`cloudSync.js:49`), the chapter lane.

### dice-engine (`engine/dice.ts` (158); the ledger's eight append sites — six `ADD_ROLL` dispatches in `rollResolver.js:631,673,721,776,819,913` → `handlers/messages.js:181`, `START_COMBAT` `combat.js:133`, `APPLY_COMBAT_EXCHANGE` `:379` via `exchangeLedgerRolls` `:30`, Second Wind `resources.js:162`, the two potion lanes `inventory.js:226,292`; `appendRollHistory` / `ROLL_HISTORY_CAP` / `sanitizeRollHistoryEntry` `shared.js:31-86`, `MAX_SAVED_ROLLS` `persistence.js:218`, the load slice `session.js:393`; the readers — RECENT DICE ROLLS `promptBuilder.js:294`, `DicePanel.jsx` (64), the dossier's DICE tier `recallDossier.js:278-286`, the probe `turnOrchestrator.js:136,851,889`; the stamps `combatMath.js:97-110,152`; tests `dice.test.ts` (25), `gameReducer.rollHistory.test.js` (2), `gameReducer.load.rollHistory.test.js` (3)) — Lap 4
- **Scope examined:** every importer of `dice.ts` (11 modules), every writer and reader of `rollHistory`, every `rollNotation` / `rollDie` call that produces a HERO die, the ledger entry's keys against the consumers that read them. **Verified sound / good structure:** `dice.ts` is one fairness kernel with one alias (the 08-20 fold holds), three bounded notation axes, and the crit RULE kept out of it; every append goes through `appendRollHistory`; `newestRollMarker` compares an id, not a length; the load twin projects to known keys; `DicePanel` is a read-only log by decision (07-08).
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 (design) — the ledger has no membership rule; eight sites decide one at a time, and two hero lanes decided differently.** An out-of-combat `spell_cast` heal rolls real dice (`handlers/spellcasting.js:183`, `rollNotation` per recipient) and a Short Rest spends hit dice (`resources.js:266`, `rollDie` per die) — neither file imports `appendRollHistory`, so a Cure Wounds or a rest's d8s never reach the Dice Log, RECENT DICE ROLLS, or the recall dossier's DICE tier, while the potion drunk beside them does (`inventory.js:292`) and so does a potion poured into a companion (`:226`). "What did I roll to heal Tammo?" has an answer when it was a potion and none when it was a spell. One rule, stated once: a die the HERO's action rolled enters the ledger — `appendRollHistory` at the spell and rest lanes, or a documented exclusion. Beside it, `exchangeLedgerRolls`'s `payload.rolls` fallback (`combat.js:30-33`, "planned before the split") has no production producer: all three plan branches emit `heroRolls` (`combatExchange.js:1652,1749,1834` — the opening an empty list) and a plan is never persisted (APPLY commits synchronously). It is kept alive by test payloads built without the field (`gameReducer.combat.test.js` 5 `rolls:` keys / 3 `heroRolls`; `gameReducer.spellcasting.test.js` 1 / 0) — test-shaped production code; delete the fallback and give those payloads `heroRolls`.
  - **P2 (design) — the ledger's one time-stamp is the wrong one.** Every roll carries a wall-clock `timestamp` (`dice.ts:107`), typed and persisted by `sanitizeRollHistoryEntry` (`shared.js:80`), that NO consumer reads (`DicePanel`, RECENT DICE ROLLS, the dossier, the probe — none touches it; the two `.timestamp` sorts in `promptBuilder.js:1233,1282` are world facts). Meanwhile the dossier's DICE row is the one ledger row with no "N turns ago": `row('rolls', …)` at `recallDossier.js:286` gets no distance argument because a roll has no message index, where fights / quests / fronts carry `resolvedAtMessage` (`:275`). The product has measured time in conversational distance everywhere since 09-21 (`describeTurnsAgo`); the ledger is the shelf that never got the stamp. `appendRollHistory(state, rolls)` stamping `atMessage: state.messages.length` (every caller holds `state`), the dossier's `when(item.atMessage)`, and `timestamp` dropped from the projection (or kept read-nowhere, by decision). `subtotal` and `dice` are persisted and read by nothing outside dice/combatMath either.
  - **P2 (duplication) — two constants for one cap, and one faces line written eleven times with three sign conventions.** `MAX_SAVED_ROLLS` (`persistence.js:218`) and `ROLL_HISTORY_CAP` (`shared.js:34`) are both 50 and equal by COMMENT ("matching persistence's MAX_SAVED_ROLLS"); `serializeGameState` re-slices an array that append AND load already cap — import the one constant and the belt costs nothing to keep. The dice-faces fragment `${roll.rolls.join(', ')}${modifier…}` is assembled at 11 sites in 7 files (`combatExchange.js`, `rollResolver.js` ×3, `promptBuilder.js`, `combat.js`, `inventory.js` ×2, `resources.js`, `spellcasting.js` ×2) under three conventions: `(+${mod})` (`inventory.js:230,296`, `spellcasting.js:192,200` — a NEGATIVE modifier renders "(+-1)": a WIS 8 cleric's Cure Wounds), `${mod >= 0 ? '+' : ''}${mod}` (`promptBuilder.js`, `rollResolver.js`), and a bare `+${bonus}` (`resources.js:165`). Around it, three heal lanes write one shape — roll → clamp to max → `gained` → `reviveCharacter` when > 0 → `bonusActionUsed` in combat → ledger → a system line + a `player_mechanic` `narrationCue` (`resources.js:149-175`, `inventory.js:205-235`, `:280-300`; the spell heal is the fourth without the cue or the ledger). One `describeFaces(roll)` beside the kernel and one `applyHealingRoll(state, target, roll)` in `handlers/shared.js`.
  - **P2 (nits).** `sanitizeRollHistoryEntry`'s id fallback is `String(entry.id ?? …)` (`shared.js:72`) — the `String(x)` idiom the 09-18 sweep banned at persistence boundaries: an object id loads as `"[object Object]"`, one React key shared by every such row (`DicePanel.jsx:46`); string-or-mint. `stampCriticalRoll` (`combatMath.js:97-110`) and the crit doubling (`:152-153`) MUTATE the minted `DiceRollResult` in place — the two mutations in a pipeline that otherwise treats a roll as a value — and `advantageDetail` (`rollResolver.js:585,590`) / `fightingStyleDetail` are display fields stamped onto the dice type by other modules, absent from the interface, dropped by the load projection (a loaded roll is a different shape from a live one; nothing renders them from the ledger, so it is harmless and undocumented). `rollWithModifier` calls `Date.now()` twice (`dice.ts:106-107`).
  - **Test depth:** ledger MEMBERSHIP is unpinned in both directions (no test says a spell heal or a rest d8 does / does not reach `rollHistory`); the `payload.rolls` fallback is exercised only by payloads no engine path mints; nothing pins `MAX_SAVED_ROLLS === ROLL_HISTORY_CAP`; nothing renders a negative healing modifier; the dossier's DICE row has no distance case because there is no distance.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) the membership rule + the two missing appends + the dead fallback; (2) `atMessage` on the ledger, `when()` on the DICE row; (3) one cap constant, `describeFaces`, `applyHealingRoll`; (4) the nits.

### cloud-sync (`state/cloudSync.js` (508), `state/auth.js` (46), `config/firebase.js` (94); the two callers `App.jsx:50-110` + `SettingsModal.jsx:50-130,148-240,340-370`; the local twin — `saveGame` `persistence.js:408-475`, `loadGame` `:508-545`, `BLOB_STORES` `:44-47`, `buildSaveMetadata` / `projectSaveMetadata` `:260-328`; `deriveSessionBoundaries` `migrations.js:509-513` as the reader of what both saves write; `firestore.rules`; tests `cloudSync.test.js` (36), `cloudSync.lanes.test.js` (10), `cloudSync.nodb.test.js` (1), `auth.test.js` (9), `gameReducer.auth.test.js` (3)) — Lap 4
- **Scope examined:** the four exports and their two callers, the save path diffed line by line against `persistence.saveGame`, the load path against `loadGame`, the lane table against `BLOB_STORES`, every key the save writes against its reader at load, the error contract per export. **Verified good structure:** the SDK is loaded once and read through `firestoreSdk` / `authSdk` (the 09-22 fix is clean — `!db` IS the module guard); the chunk count is read INSIDE the transaction; blobs are written before the metadata that names them and swept after the commit that releases them; `typedLaneRefs` bounds and types every claim; `projectSaveMetadata` is the one list projection; `auth.js` is three functions with every branch pinned.
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 (duplication) — the save prologue and the load epilogue are each written twice, and the field both prologues write is DEAD.** `saveGame` (`persistence.js:413-432,465-471`) and `saveGameToCloud` (`cloudSync.js:261-283`) each count `prunedMessageCount`, spread `serializeGameState` + `session`, fold the lanes' `extract`, and assemble `{ slotId, ...buildSaveMetadata, savedAt, messageCount, [refsField]: refs }`; `rehydrateBlobs` (`cloudSync.js:383-399`) and `hydrate` (`persistence.js:515-531`) are the same `collect` → fetch → `lanes.reduce(restore)` fold with a different fetch. And `prunedMessageCount` is overwritten on EVERY load by `deriveSessionBoundaries` (`migrations.js:509-513`, recomputed from the loaded messages) — neither save-time write has a reader; the cloud copy's comment ("indexes into the array we actually persist") dates from the trimmed-cloud-save era. One `prepareSavePayload(gameState, lanes)` → `{ state, lanes, metadata }` and one `restoreLanes(state, lanes, fetchBlob)` in `portraitStore.js`; the dead write goes.
  - **P2 (design) — two lane tables for one split, and a test whose job is to keep the copies equal.** `BLOB_STORES` (`persistence.js:44-47`) and `CLOUD_BLOB_LANES` (`cloudSync.js:49-68`) each list `refsField` + the extract / collect / restore triple; the local copy adds `store`, the cloud copy adds `collection` / `keyPattern` / `label`, and `cloudSync.lanes.test.js:84` exists to pin that they agree lane for lane — a test that guards a duplication is the duplication's running cost (09-26 is the day the copies disagreed). `store` and `collection` are already the same two strings. One `BLOB_LANES` in `portraitStore.js` (`{ id, refsField, keyPattern, extract, collect, restore }`), both modules reading it, makes the agreement structural and the pin redundant. `CLOUD_RULES_HINT` (`:144-149`) hand-writes the same collection names and rule paths a third time — derive it from the table.
  - **P2 (design) — four exports, four error contracts.** `saveGameToCloud` returns `{ ok, reason, message }` (09-02); `loadGameFromCloud` swallows EVERY failure to `null` (`:440-443`) — a permission-denied, a missing chunk (`:426`, the module's own deliberately loud throw), a corrupt chunk's JSON error, and "no such doc" are one `null`, so both callers can only say "could not be loaded — details in the browser console" (`App.jsx:98`, `SettingsModal.jsx:162-166`); `listCloudSaves` rethrows (`:470`); `deleteGameFromCloud` collapses to `false` (`:504-506` — a permission-denied delete reads "Failed to delete" with no rules hint). The 09-02 fix typed the save's result; its three siblings kept their 07-09 shapes. One result shape across the four (`{ ok, reason, message, value }`, with `CLOUD_RULES_HINT` on every permission-denied, not only the save's), and the callers render `message`.
  - **P2 (nits).** `saveDocRef` is built three times (`:256-257`, `:406-407`, `:479-480` — `doc(collection(db, users/${uid}/saves), cloudDocId(slotId))`) while `chunksCollection` / `blobDoc` are shelves two lines above; `typedRefsByLane(null)` serves as "empty refs" twice (`:330`, `:487`); `MAX_LANE_REFS` 512 against its own comment ("≤ ~100 portraits / ~50 chapters"); the ok result hardcodes two lane names (`portraitsUploaded` / `chaptersUploaded`, `:320-321,356`) that `describePortraitsUploaded` (`SettingsModal.jsx:21-23`) re-reads by name — a third lane edits three places; the chunk reader trusts `payloadChunks` unbounded (`:415,424`; harmless — the loop throws at the first gap — but the module states its bound once and applies it to two of three readers); `initializeFirebase`'s `isSameConfig` compares the three fields `getFirebaseConfigError` validates (`firebase.js:49-51,75-77`) — one `CONFIG_KEYS` list. **Snapshot correction:** `auth.js` 78.94† is STALE — the 09-26 sweep added the rethrow pins (`auth.test.js:81-100`) and every branch of the 46-line file has a case; it should not steer the next tie-break.
  - **Test depth:** nothing pins the module's own first-line claim (`cloudSync.js:9-10`: both paths persist the SAME serialized state) — a test that runs one `gameState` through `saveGame`'s and `saveGameToCloud`'s prologues and diffs the `state` objects would have made the duplication's drift visible and would retire with the shared prologue; no test asserts a caller can tell "no save" from "permission denied" on load or delete; the lanes test pins the copy's agreement rather than one source.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) `prepareSavePayload` + `restoreLanes` and the dead `prunedMessageCount` write; (2) one `BLOB_LANES` table, the hint derived; (3) one result shape for the four exports; (4) the nits; (5) the snapshot's `auth.js` row.

### Process notes
- Queue had 10 open items at run start (all 10-03, living-world + scene-art); eight lines added (0 P1, 8 P2). Coverage snapshot not refreshed (4 days; `auth.js` row flagged stale above for the next refresh).
- **Hosted-run lesson: a fresh container has no `node_modules`.** The first `npx vitest run` downloaded `vitest@5` on the fly, failed to load `vite.config.js` ("Cannot find package 'vite'"), and EXITED 0 with no tests run — a background task that reports "completed" is not a green suite. `npm ci` first, then grep the log for the `Tests` line, never only the exit code.
- **Lap-4 lessons, third pair.** (1) **A persisted key is found dead by grepping its READERS, not its writers** — `prunedMessageCount` has two writers and a load heal that overwrites both; `rollHistory[].timestamp` has one writer, a typed projection, and no reader. (2) **A test that pins two tables agree is a duplication with a maintenance contract** — the fix is one table, after which the test has nothing to compare. (3) **A ledger needs a membership rule stated once** — eight append sites each deciding "does this die count" is how two hero lanes decided differently. (4) **A module's first-line doc claim is a test to write** — "both paths persist the SAME state" is checked by nothing.
- Registry amendments: cloud-sync's scope drops `fitPortraitsToBudget` (retired 2026-09-24; it names `CLOUD_BLOB_LANES` as the twin of `BLOB_STORES` instead) and names the error contract per export; dice-engine's scope names the ledger's MEMBERSHIP (which hero dice reach it) and the hero-die lanes outside it.
- Session ran on a `claude/*` working branch; per the master-only convention the result lands on `origin master` directly.

(2) **A boundary that lands in one lane is copied by the next unless the copy is DELETED** — the 10-02 `normalizeFrontProposal` was adopted by the two lanes that were read that day; the aftermath lane's shaper, one import away, kept its weaker gate. When a boundary is unified, grep every function whose name starts with `sanitize` / `normalize` / `shape` in the family and delete the ones the boundary subsumes. (3) **A reason string two modules share is a contract with no test** — `fallbackReason` is written as prose in one module and parsed with `===` / `includes` in another; name the reasons once. (4) **One stamp, one owner** — a timestamp written by a component for the hero and by a reducer for the NPC is two owners of one field.

- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — XP receipts are invisible to the DM.** Every progression row — the XP line and the level-up line (`createSystemMessage` in `progression.js:70-77`), the cap note, the "Duplicate XP award ignored" line (`character.js:350-351,363,441,453-454,460`) — is a plain `system` row with no `dmVisible`, so `buildMessageWindow` drops it. Reproduced: window after a +300 XP / Level 2 award = the two fiction rows only; after a suppressed replay, likewise. Yet the cached prefix tells the DM at `promptBuilder.js:757` "the engine shows every award as a system line; if none appeared, it was not granted — award the missing amount ONCE" — a rule about lines the DM structurally cannot see. The 2026-08-26 live report (the DM promised the forgotten XP and awarded it on the two next turns) IS this blindness; the ledger became the belt, and the receipt is the fix the coin lanes got on 08-31 (`dmVisible`, folded into one window row). Cost: ~55–140 B per award, ONE window row (it folds with adjacent receipts), carried for ~10 turns; benefit: the DM stops re-emitting, and the level-up line is the one place the DM could learn "Astra just reached level 2" in the moment — the HERO SHEET shows the new number, never the event (a WOW-adjacent gain for the same bytes). `createSystemMessage` cannot import `systemMessage` (progression ⇄ handlers/shared cycle, the file says so) — give it an `extra` parameter instead.
  - **P2 — the prompt's promise and the L1–L2 cap disagree, and every disagreement costs two rows.** The prefix says a freeform bonus is "tens to low hundreds of XP" (`:756`) and that the engine "caps … at the quest-completion tier for the hero's level"; the tier is 38 XP at L1 and 75 at L2, so a DM obeying the prompt (50 XP for clever play) trips the cap note on EVERY award for the first two levels: 127 B + 53 B, two rows, both invisible to the DM, so it never learns the band either. The DM cannot know the tier (the prefix cannot carry a live number). One live number on the EXP line (`… to next level · freeform bonus cap 38`, ~25 B in the live block) closes the loop, and the note folds into the XP line (`+38 XP (capped from 50)`) — one row, not two.
  - **P2 — nits.** `getFrontResolutionMilestoneXp` / `getQuestCompletionXp` both re-coerce `Math.max(1, Number(level) || 1)` that `getExperienceThreshold` already does; `isMaxLevel` coerces a third way; three readers of one table — one `levelIndex(level)`. `applySingleLevelUp` computes `averageHp` only for the message while `perLevelHpGain` owns the number (one source, or the message reads the helper).

- **Suggested improvements:** (1) `dmVisible` on the four progression lines (an `extra` arg on `createSystemMessage`) + a pin "the window carries the XP receipt as ONE folded row"; (2) the live cap on the EXP line and the cap note folded into the XP line; (3) the level-up prefix pin (only `heroSheet` / `spellbook` differ between L1 and L2 parts); (4) the nits.

## 2026-10-01 — memory-journal + chat-orchestration (Lap 3: performance & token budget)

`npm test`: 3348 passing / 201 files (green; the hosted container shipped without `node_modules` again — `npm install` first).

Rotation: the last-6 union (origin == HEAD after fetch) excludes story-memory, prompt-building (09-30), providers-adapter, vector-memory-rag (09-29), response-parsing, scribe (09-28), quests, enemy-stats-conditions (09-27), chronicler, rules-math (09-26), inventory-economy, spellcasting (09-25). Oldest eligible is **memory-journal** (09-18); progression and chat-orchestration tie at 09-19 and the coverage tie-break picks **chat-orchestration** (`turnOrchestrator.js` 92.73 / `ChatPanel.jsx` 0 < `progression.js` 98.66). Both enter Lap 3 — they are also the two features that share the one seam the lens exists for: the journal boundary decides what the DM's next call carries. Every number below was **measured** with two throwaway vitest files (deleted, never committed; zero repo changes) against the real reducer, the real `maybeAutoSummarize` with a scripted Flash reply, the real `buildMessageWindow`, and the real turn runner with a React-shaped lagging `getState` (dispatch visible one macrotask later, the `postTurn.test.js` harness). Coverage snapshot is 1 day old — not refreshed. **All 09-18 / 09-19 findings for both features verified fixed in code** (the entry/mark commit order + the typed NPC list + the streak reset after the mark, `worldJournal.js:343-357`; the per-element row heal `session.js:400-420`; the Flash `location` clamp; `roleLabel`; the `combat_end` retirement, `applyFightOpeningChannels`, the `combat_start` roll strip `turnOrchestrator.js:456-459`, `clampInt` on the integer wires, the typed message rows + the window clamp, the `starting_items` opening gate).

### memory-journal (`engine/worldJournal.js` end to end — the trigger scan, `batchBoundary`, the batch as bytes, the commit, the secondary lanes, the reflection + verifier tail; `MARK_MESSAGES_SUMMARIZED` / `ADD_JOURNAL_ENTRY` in `handlers/worldMemory.js:271-310`; `runAutoSummarize` + `summarizedBoundary` in `turnOrchestrator.js:160-203`; the readers — SESSION HISTORY, the mount seed `ChatPanel.jsx:413`, the recall dossier, the Journal tab `JournalPanel.jsx:550`; tests `worldJournal.*.test.js` (46), `commitmentVerifier.test.js`) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** per-turn CPU of the cadence check, the batch per Flash call in bytes, the mark's churn, the journal's growth as save bytes / RAG rows / render rows, the cadence's network fan-out, and what the DM's next call carries after a cadence. **Verified cheap/sound (measured):** a typical 10-message batch is system 2,626 + user 3,200–4,466 chars (~2k tokens); the 40-weighted-row maximum is 49,835 user chars (~13k tokens, the 2k per-message clamp holding); `collectNarrativeEntries` walks from row 0 for the OOC pairing and costs 0.15 ms at 2,000 rows / 0.30 ms at 6,000, called 4× per turn (cadence check + presence ×3) — ~2 ms worst case; `MARK_MESSAGES_SUMMARIZED` re-allocates every row below the mark (2,000 of 2,000 when 10 were new) in 0.12 ms; a journal entry is 1,137 B typical / 7,187 B at every cap, so a 2,000-turn campaign's ~400 entries are 444 KB typical / 2.8 MB max in every autosave and cloud write, and 400 DURABLE RAG rows (never evicted, ~3.6 KB each on disk); a cadence turn's network is the journal Flash call + the reflection Flash call + the entry's own `addMemory` embed + the verifier (zero tokens); the 09-20 reflection projection and the 09-30 SESSION HISTORY diet hold.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — every cadence EMPTIES the DM's window.** `batchBoundary` returns `messages.length` whenever the backlog is under 40 weighted rows (`worldJournal.js:108-117`) and the mark flags every row below it; `buildMessageWindow` drops summarized rows. Reproduced: 14 narrative rows → window 14 rows before the cadence, **0 after**; the next turn's history is the player's new line alone. In production the newest DM row survives only because `runAutoSummarize` reads the LAGGING `stateRef` (the batch is one row behind the commit) — and not on every path: a post-roll outcome that awaited the nudge reads a flushed state and summarizes the outcome too (0 rows, reproduced with a fresh `getState`). `MESSAGE_WINDOW` = 20 is a ceiling the history never reaches: it saw-tooths 1 → ~11 → 1 every ~5 turns, and for the turn after each cadence the DM's immediate context is a 2–3-sentence summary + 3 clamped consequences — the merchant's exact offer two exchanges ago, the companion's last line, the player's previous three lines are gone from the call. The 2026-06-23 LOCATION TRANSITION HISTORY was built against this exact symptom ("the DM forgot events immediately prior to entering a location"); the root is the boundary, not retrieval. The standard shape keeps a TAIL: trigger at ≥ `SUMMARIZE_EVERY` + `KEEP_TAIL` narrative rows, summarize the oldest `SUMMARIZE_EVERY`, never the newest `KEEP_TAIL` (6 rows = 3 exchanges ≈ 4.5k chars ≈ 1.1k tokens per call; prompt-cache neutral — the history follows the dynamic half). Pushback noted for Vesa: the summary is the DESIGN's continuity carrier and tokens are the cost; but the cadence already pays those tokens on the ~4 turns before the next cadence, so the tail only removes the cliff. A decision item as much as a fix.
  - **P2 — the entry's live embed is a third embed request on a cadence turn.** `runAutoSummarize` awaits `addMemory` for the new entry (`turnOrchestrator.js:177-196`) after the turn's batch already flushed in `runPostTurnExtraction`; the 09-29 rule (one batch per turn) has `queueMemory` + flush for this. One round trip; also holds `summarizeInFlight` for its duration.
  - **P2 — the mark clones rows it did not change.** `idx < upTo ? { ...msg, summarized: true } : msg` (`worldMemory.js:271-281`) — 2,000 allocations and an identity change on every already-summarized row per cadence; the rendered 150 `ChatMessage` memos re-render once per cadence for nothing. `idx < upTo && !msg.summarized` keeps identity. 0.12 ms — polish.
  - **P2 — the journal has no growth projection and one unwindowed reader.** 444 KB at 400 entries in every save; 400 durable rows against the 1,500 cap that evicts TRANSIENTS only, so at ~1,000 durable rows (entries + active cards + facts + NPCs) the per-turn narrative/player rows get the remainder and the 09-29 overflow warning fires only past 1,500. No prune is possible by decision (the record lane reads every entry). The Journal tab renders ALL entries reversed (`[...journal].reverse().map`, no window, no virtualization) — 400 cards on open. Note the share in the Memory Inspector like the pool; window the tab like the chat (150).
  - **Test depth:** nothing asserts what the DM's next call carries after a cadence — the summarize tests pin the mark at `messages.length` as the CORRECT outcome (`worldJournal.summarize.test.js:91-113`); no test counts embed requests per cadence turn.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) `KEEP_TAIL` — the trigger, the boundary, and a pin "after a cadence the window still carries the last KEEP_TAIL narrative rows" (and the orchestrator reads ONE captured state, not the ref — see chat-orchestration); (2) `queueMemory` for the entry; (3) the mark's identity guard; (4) a journal count/bytes row in the inspector + a 150-entry window on the tab.

### chat-orchestration (`llm/turnOrchestrator.js` `sendToLLM` end to end as a call chain; `buildMessageWindow` in `turnVisibility.js:97-118` as bytes per lane; `submitPlayerMessage` `ChatPanel.jsx:688-826` and the providers' `formatMessages` (`gemini.js:129-147`, `openaiCompatible.js:29-45`) as the last consumer; the render path `ChatPanel.jsx:996-1011` + `ChatMessage`; tests `turnOrchestrator.*.test.js` (11 files)) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** the ordinary turn's network fan-out and blocking chain, the window as bytes per call and per lane, per-call CPU in `sendToLLM`, the render path under streaming. **Verified cheap/sound:** blocking before the first token = ONE awaited query embed (the machinery key is mandatory, so always) + ~1 ms CPU (presence 0.2 ms, curation, prompt build — measured 09-30); between the last token and the commit = the semantic detector only when the narration is request-shaped (the regex gate at `responseParser.js:285-290`), the arbiter only with rolls; after the commit = the nudge (a second DM call, blocks `isLoading`) on a contract cue only, then background Scribe + ONE batch embed; three embed requests per ordinary turn (query, the player line's own `addMemory` at `ChatPanel.jsx:724-731`, the batch); the chat renders the newest 150 rows through memoized `ChatMessage` with a stable `useCallback` delete handler, so a streaming paint re-renders one bubble; `buildMessageWindow` is O(N) with one regex per system row (sub-ms at 2,000); the stream's per-chunk `search(/```json/)` over the growing buffer is O(len) per chunk — trivial at narration length.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — the player's line reaches the provider TWICE on every ordinary turn.** `submitPlayerMessage` dispatches the user row (`ChatPanel.jsx:723-726`), then `sendToLLM` awaits the query embed (`turnOrchestrator.js:339`); by then React has flushed, `getState().messages` carries the row, `buildMessageWindow` keeps it as the window's LAST row (`:392`), and the same text is sent again as `userMessage` — both providers append `userMessage` after the history with no dedupe. Reproduced through the real runner with the React-shaped harness: last window row `===` userMessage on the ordinary turn and on table talk; the combat-intent and narration lanes are unaffected only because nothing is awaited before their window read (the stale ref hides the row) — the behavior depends on whether an `await` precedes the read. Cost is small (~100–500 chars per call: two consecutive `user` turns saying the same thing); the EFFECT is that the DM is told the action twice on every turn — and the 09-11 turn-grammar eval's one unmoved column is Gemini's echo-of-action (61 %, `docs/TURN_GRAMMAR_EVAL_2026-09-11.md:36`). The fix is a line (drop the trailing window row when it is the player's own line, or build the window from the state captured BEFORE the dispatch); the proof is `npm run eval:turns` before/after on the Echo column.
  - **P1 — the window after a cadence** — the memory-journal P1 above; the seam belongs to both features, and the orchestrator's half is that `runAutoSummarize` hands `maybeAutoSummarize` the lagging ref (`:177`) — the one reason the newest DM row survives today, load-bearing by accident.
  - **P2 — the nudge sends the narration twice.** `recoverMissingEvents` runs after awaits, so `buildMessageHistory()` carries the committed assistant row AND `buildNudgePrompt` quotes 1,500 chars of it (`missingEventsNudge.js:67`). Bytes only, on a rare lane.
  - **P2 — the cadence's own state is the header trap in reverse.** `runPostTurnExtraction` reads the committed-turn record precisely because `getState()` in the same task is pre-turn (the 09-07 P2); `runAutoSummarize` reads `getState()` for the cadence COUNT and the BATCH, so the count is one row behind on the sync path and current after an await — a cadence can fire one turn late or on time depending on whether the turn had a nudge. Benign today; brittle under any refactor that adds an await.
  - **Test depth:** no orchestrator test inspects the `messageHistory` handed to `streamMessage` (grep: zero hits across the 11 files) — the window's CONTENTS per lane are unpinned; no test counts network calls per turn.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) drop the duplicate + pin "the window never ends with the userMessage" on every lane; (2) capture ONE state at the top of `sendToLLM` / `runAutoSummarize` and read the window, the count, and the batch from it; (3) the nudge's quote OR the history row, not both; (4) a per-turn call-count pin (stream 1, query embed 1, player-line embed 1, batch flush 1; Flash ×2 + embed +1 on a cadence turn).

### Process notes
- Queue had ZERO open items at run start (the 09-30 build session cleared it); nine lines added (2 P1). Coverage snapshot not refreshed (1 day).
- **New Lap-3 sub-pattern: a budget nobody reaches is a budget nobody checked.** `MESSAGE_WINDOW` = 20 is tested as a CAP and documented as "the DM sees a 20-message sliding window"; the cadence drains it to 0–1 rows every five turns, so the typical fill is 1–11. For every "window of N" / "last N" constant, measure the TYPICAL fill across the cycle that empties it, not the ceiling — the cost lens asks what a block costs, and the answer can be "less than designed".
- **Second: a read after an `await` is a read of a different state.** `getState()` before the first await is pre-dispatch; after it, post-flush. The duplicated player line and the surviving DM row are the SAME mechanism with opposite signs, and the 09-07 header trap was its third face. Rule: a value a pipeline needs consistently (the window, the cadence's transcript, the count) is captured ONCE at a named point and threaded, never re-read through the ref wherever convenient.
- Registry amendment: memory-journal's scope now names the boundary's effect on the DM window and the cadence turn's network fan-out; chat-orchestration's names the window per lane, the providers' `formatMessages` as its last consumer, and the per-turn call count.

And `selectRelationshipBeatCandidate` reads the pool, so SOMEONE REACHES OUT can fire on a thread the line never carried. A lookup got a projection: the pool for the thread (0.3–0.5 ms per build over 1,000 cards, measured), the curated list for the callbacks.

## 2026-09-29 — providers-adapter + vector-memory-rag (Lap 3: performance & token budget)

`npm test`: 3214 passing / 187 files (green; the hosted container shipped without `node_modules` again — `npm install` first).

Rotation: the last-6 union (origin == HEAD after fetch) excludes response-parsing, scribe (09-28), quests, enemy-stats-conditions (09-27), chronicler, rules-math (09-26), inventory-economy, spellcasting (09-25), hero-tells, character-vault (09-24), combat-exchange, persistence (09-23). Oldest eligible is **providers-adapter** (09-16); story-memory and vector-memory-rag tie at 09-17 and the coverage tie-break picks **vector-memory-rag** (`vectorMemory.js` 96.12 < `storyMemory.js` 97.59). Both enter Lap 3. Lens: calls per turn and per mount, bytes per call and per row, IndexedDB churn, CPU per retrieval, and the stall budget each lane grants a call on the critical path. Every number below was **measured** with a throwaway vitest file (deleted, never committed; zero repo changes): the real `vectorMemory.js` with the provider mocked and `fake-indexeddb` counting `indexedDB.open`, the real `buildRetrievedMemoriesBlock`, and the real `sendMessage` + `getBackgroundConfig` under fake timers. Coverage snapshot 5 days old — not refreshed. **All 09-16 / 09-17 findings for both features verified fixed in code** (object-guarded bodies, the SSE event gate, `contentText`, `sanitizeSettings`, `isEmbeddingVector`, the stream idle guard; `MAX_EMBED_INPUT_CHARS`, the chunk bisection under its budget, `typeCachedRow`, the memory-unavailable line with its cause).

### vector-memory-rag (`engine/vectorMemory.js` end to end — the mount seed's load → prune → retag → embed → persist, the per-turn fan-out at `turnOrchestrator.js:191,335,602,747` and `ChatPanel.jsx:380-432,614,703`, `retrieveRelevant` at the cap, `buildRetrievedMemoriesBlock` as live prompt bytes; `embedText`/`embedTexts` in `providers/gemini.js` as the two embed budgets; tests `vectorMemory.test.js` (64), the embed cases of `gemini.test.js`) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** what one Continue costs (reads, opens, embeds), what one ordinary turn costs (embeds, opens, CPU), what a row costs (bytes in memory, on disk, through the read), and what retrieval costs the prompt. **Verified cheap/sound (measured):** retrieval over 1,500 rows 8.5 ms per call with every row scored + the diversity pass (the recall lane's 16 @ 0.45: 5.2 ms); `addMemory` at the cap 0.29 ms; the query-vector memo holds (09-22); a cold seed is ONE `batchEmbedContents` round trip per 100 items (300 items → 1 call) and an invalid key at a cold seed costs ≤ 13 requests through the bisection budget; the typical RETRIEVED MEMORIES block is ~4.6k chars (8 rows × a 2–3-sentence journal summary + the 658-char header); `enforceCampaignCap` evicts transients only (09-06 holds); the seed's mutable-category prune re-embeds only the rows whose text changed.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — the campaign cache read is device-wide.** `loadPersistedEmbeddings` calls `getAll()` on the whole store and filters by `sessionId` in JS (`vectorMemory.js:106-113`) although the store is keyed `[sessionId, text]` and `deleteCampaignMemories` already uses the exact campaign range (`IDBKeyRange.bound([sessionId, ''], [sessionId, []])`, `:637`). Measured: 4 campaigns × 500 rows → the active campaign's seed takes 217 ms vs 57 ms with one campaign (fake-indexeddb; in Chrome the cost is the structured-clone of every other campaign's 768-double vectors, ~6 KB per row): five mature campaigns at the cap read ~46 MB and materialize 7,500 vectors to keep 1,500, on EVERY ChatPanel mount — which remounts on every load. A device that plays several campaigns pays for all of them at every Continue; `getAll(range)` with the delete's own bound is the fix — same key, no schema bump.
  - **P2 — one IndexedDB connection per persisted row.** `storeMemoryEntry` → `persistEmbedding` opens the database and a transaction per row (`:60-72`, `:394`); the seed's retag loop persists per changed row too (`:469`). Measured: a cold seed of 300 items = 301 `indexedDB.open` calls (1,501 at the cap); a warm mount with 40 retagged rows = 41; an ordinary turn (player line + 3 facts + narrative) = 5; an add at the cap = 2 (persist + evict-delete). One readwrite transaction per seed (new rows + retags + stale deletes) is the shape; the row-level write stays for the live lane.
  - **P2 — the live-add fan-out is unbatched.** Per ordinary turn: 1 blocking query embed + N document embeds each on its own `embedContent` request (`turnOrchestrator.js:602` per world fact, `:747` narrative, `ChatPanel.jsx:703` player, `:614` terminal combat, `turnOrchestrator.js:191` on a cadence) — measured 6 embed HTTP calls on a turn with 3 facts, all counted against the same embedding RPM quota as the query embed the NEXT turn's memory depends on. `embedTexts` exists; a turn's facts + narrative are one batch.
  - **P2 — a vector costs 6,144 bytes as a `number[]`** (structured-cloned as 8-byte doubles): 8.8 MB in memory and on disk per campaign at the cap, and the same bytes through every read above. A `Float32Array` halves all three (3,072 B/row) at no retrieval cost at the 0.55 / 0.9 thresholds; the load filter's `Array.isArray(entry.vector)` (`:118`) must accept typed arrays and `cosineSimilarity` already indexes generically — a write-side narrow + read-side accept with the schema tag untouched (same vectors, narrower storage), no migration.
  - **P2 — the retrieved block has no ceiling.** `buildRetrievedMemoriesBlock` prints `m.text` whole (`:686`): 8 journal rows at `JOURNAL_SUMMARY_MAX` 2,000 = 16,963 chars; the recall lane's 16 rows = 33,275 chars (21 % of `PROMPT_CHAR_BUDGET`) of LIVE prompt bytes. Every other block got a ceiling constant in the 09-25/09-27 sweeps; this one is bounded only by its sources' clamps. A per-row clamp (~600, sentence-ended) or a block ceiling with a "+K more" tail, pinned.
  - **P2 — a 429 on the seed is a silent partial store.** `embedTexts` nulls a 429/5xx chunk without retry (`gemini.js:333` — right for the bisection, DECISIONS 2026-09-17: a retry per ITEM amplifies), the seed skips those rows, `retrieveRelevant` runs the whole SESSION against the partial store, and only the next mount retries — console-only. The query embed got its player line on 09-19; the seed never says anything. One Retry-After-bounded WHOLE-request retry per chunk (`parseRetryAfterMs` in `sse.js` is reusable) inside the 60 s guard, then a one-line notice when rows are still missing.
  - **Test depth:** nothing pins the read's SCOPE (`vectorMemory.test.js:342` checks the filter, not that other campaigns' rows are never read), the opens per seed, the embed calls per turn (the orchestrator harness still runs without a machinery key — the 09-22 note), or the retrieved block's ceiling; `gemini.test.js:511` pins the no-bisect on 429 but nothing pins what the seed does with the nulls beyond skipping.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) `getAll(IDBKeyRange.bound(…))` sharing the delete's bound, pinned with a two-campaign store whose `getAll` argument is asserted; (2) one transaction per seed and per turn's batch; (3) batch a turn's document embeds through `embedTexts`; (4) `Float32Array` on write, typed-array accept on load; (5) a retrieved-block ceiling; (6) one Retry-After retry per chunk + the notice; (7) the pins.

### providers-adapter (`llm/adapter.js` both lanes with their budgets; `providers/gemini.js` request shape + `embedText`/`embedTexts`; `providers/openaiCompatible.js` + `openai.js`; `providers/sse.js` per-chunk path; `llm/machinery.js` `getBackgroundConfig`; the pre-commit callers `outOfCombatRollPolicy.js:101` + `responseParser.js:315`; tests `adapter.test.js` (26), `gemini.test.js`, `openai.test.js`, `sse.test.js`, `machinery.test.js`) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** each request's bytes beyond the prompt, the retry/stall budget each lane grants a caller and what it costs a BLOCKING pre-commit call, the per-chunk work in the stream path, the embed endpoints' guards, and what the adapter observes about the provider (usage, cache). **Verified cheap/sound:** the per-call overhead beyond the prompt is ~400 bytes on Gemini (four safety rows + `generationConfig`) and ~60 on the compat body; the machinery config (thinking 0, 8k output, 60 s) rides every machinery call (pinned `machinery.test.js:113`) and the DM lane keeps the model's default thinking by decision (DECISIONS 2026-08-09); the stream's idle guard is one `clearTimeout` + `setTimeout` per chunk; `readSseStream` re-splits only the buffered tail; the OpenAI key probe fires only on a network-failure TypeError; `Retry-After` caps at 10 s and the adapter waits `max(backoff, retryAfter)`; the semantic-roll gate keeps the detector off ordinary turns (08-05, pinned `responseParser.test.js:1195,1225`) and its payload clamps at 4k (09-22); no lane retries a stream.
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — a blocking pre-commit machinery call can hold the turn for 183 s.** `sendMessage` retries a stall (`MAX_RETRIES` 2, `adapter.js:79-99`) with the SAME per-attempt guard: measured under fake timers, a never-answering provider fails the machinery lane after **183.3 s** virtual (60 + 1 + 60 + 2 + 60) and the default lane after 273.3 s. Right for the background Scribe / journal (a lost extraction costs the campaign); wrong for the two calls that sit BETWEEN the stream's last token and the commit — the roll arbiter (`outOfCombatRollPolicy.js:101`) and the semantic detector (`responseParser.js:315`) — where the player watches "waiting" for up to three minutes with the narration already fully received. `timeoutMs` is a per-call option nobody passes: a pre-commit lane gets one attempt at ~20 s, then the no-key fallback both callers already carry.
  - **P2 — the one BLOCKING embed has no retry at all.** `embedText` — the query embed, awaited before the prompt is built — is a single fetch under `AbortSignal.timeout(30_000)` with no 429 handling (`gemini.js:237`): one rate-limit reply = a memory-less turn with the 09-19 error line, on the lane whose quota the unbatched fan-out above is spending. A single Retry-After-bounded retry (≤ 10 s, inside the 30 s) keeps the turn's memory on the common transient. (Queued with the seed twin on the RAG side.)
  - **P2 (read-only, already queued) — the adapter observes nothing about cost.** No lane reads Gemini `usageMetadata` (`promptTokenCount` / `cachedContentTokenCount` / `thoughtsTokenCount`) or the compat `usage` (grep over `src/`: zero hits), so the byte-stable prefix (DECISIONS 2026-07-18) has never been observed to cache and the DM's thinking share is unknown; queued as M2 in `docs/MEMORY_RESEARCH.md` and `planned` in IDEAS ("Verify the prompt cache actually engages") — not re-queued. One addition for that item, recorded in IDEAS: the OpenAI-compatible STREAM lane returns no usage at all unless the request carries `stream_options: { include_usage: true }` (`openaiCompatible.js:131`), and OpenAI's cached share lives at `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` — the wiring is per lane, not per provider.
  - **Test depth:** `adapter.test.js:206` pins that a stall surfaces, not how long a caller waits or that `timeoutMs` shortens it; `gemini.test.js` pins the batch shape and chunk semantics but no request's byte overhead; `embedText` has no 429 case (there is nothing to cover yet).
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) a pre-commit budget (`timeoutMs` ~20 s, one attempt) on the arbiter and the detector, pinned as a number; (2) the query-embed retry; (3) the pins; (4) when M2 lands, the compat `stream_options` beside the Gemini `usageMetadata` read.

### Process notes
- Queue had ZERO open items at run start (the 09-28 sweep cleared it); eight lines added (1 P1). Coverage snapshot not refreshed (5 days).
- **New Lap-3 sub-pattern: a keyed store read without its key is a device-wide read.** The embedding store was campaign-keyed on 07-30 so a switch would load "only that campaign's rows" — and the write and the delete pass the key, while the READ still does `getAll()` and filters in JS, so the cost of every Continue scales with every campaign on the device. Rule for the lens: grep every `getAll()` / `openCursor()` on a keyed store and ask what range it passes.
- **Second: a retry budget belongs to the lane, not the call.** `sendMessage`'s 3 × guard is one policy for a background extraction (where it is right) and a pre-commit call the player is waiting on (where 183 s is three minutes of "waiting"). Check every `sendMessage` caller for whether it blocks a visible turn, and give the blocking ones their own attempt count and guard.
- **Third: fire-and-forget calls still spend the quota the blocking one needs.** Six embed requests per turn, five of them background, all on the RPM the next turn's query embed shares — a fan-out is only free until the one call that matters gets the 429.

### response-parsing (`llm/responseParser.js`, `llm/utils/jsonExtractor.js`, `llm/eventChannels.js` end to end; the orchestrator's stream path `turnOrchestrator.js:396-407` and its ChatPanel paint; the parsed object's commit `turnOrchestrator.js:558` → `serializeGameState` → `typeLoadedMessage`; `detectSemanticTextRolls` as the one machinery call; RESPONSE_FORMAT / FORMAT_REMINDER as the contract's bytes; tests `responseParser.test.js` (1,439 lines), `jsonExtractor.test.js`, `eventChannels.test.js` + `eventChannels.spellWire.test.js`) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** CPU per parse on realistic and hostile replies; the per-chunk stream path; the bytes the contract itself costs; the machinery call the parser can trigger and its gate; and the parsed object's life AFTER the turn — where it is stored and who reads it. **Verified cheap/sound (measured):** `parseResponse` on a 4k fenced reply 0.08 ms, 4k prose-only 0.31 ms (33 registry anchors × 2 needles of `lastIndexOf` + the text detector), 4k unfenced 0.11 ms, 20k fenced 0.02 ms, 20k prose 1.06 ms, a 5k prose reply with 40 bare wire-key mentions 0.93 ms (the 09-15 last-first walk and 4M budget hold); `normalizeEvents({})` 0.01 ms; the orchestrator's per-chunk `search(/```json/i)` over the accumulated buffer is O(n²) in principle but 0.46 ms for a 4.3k reply in 215 chunks, and ChatPanel coalesces the paint per animation frame; `FORMAT_REMINDER` is 352 chars of live tail; `RESPONSE_FORMAT` is 45,298 chars of cached prefix (43,724 on 09-27 — the combat-drama telegraph bullet and the two moved combat paragraphs are the growth; prompt-building's file); the semantic-roll lane is ONE gated Flash call with a ~1k system prompt and a ≤4k tail (the 09-22 clamp holds) — the gate opened on 0 of the 10 DM prose paragraphs the three playtest docs carry (too small a sample to rate the false-positive cost; recorded, not claimed).
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — the normalized events object rides every assistant row in the save, and nothing reads it after the turn.** `normalizeEvents` materializes all 35 channel keys (621 bytes of JSON for an EMPTY reply: `[]`s, `0`s, `null`s), the orchestrator commits it on the row (`payload: { id, role: 'assistant', content, events, hidden }`, `turnOrchestrator.js:558`), `serializeGameState` keeps it, the cloud path stringifies it, and `typeLoadedMessage` (`handlers/session.js:58`) spreads it back untyped — while both post-commit consumers (`runPostTurnExtraction`, `finalizeRoleplayTurn`) read the in-memory `lastCommittedTurn`, and no other module reads `message.events` (the only `.events` readers in `src/` are the exchange RESULT's, a different field). 300 assistant rows ≈ 190 KB per write in the immutable share the 09-23 entry watches, plus the populated turns' payloads, forever; a hostile save's `events` blob loads whole (inert, since nothing reads it — but bytes). The parser's output SHAPE became a save-bytes decision the moment the row kept it.
  - **P2 (nit) — `detectTextRollRequests` compiles up to 27 `RegExp`s per prose-only reply** (Pattern 2 builds one per skill inside the loop, `responseParser.js:96-99`): 0.12 ms; module-scope constants.
  - **P2 (nit) — the format spends prefix bytes on non-channels:** `combat_end` (retired 09-19) is still named once ("Never emit `combat_end`…", `promptBuilder.js:685`) and `resources_used` — a suppression signal the DM must never emit — twice (`:718`, `:721`); a "never emit X" line for a wire the registry does not carry is a rule about nothing, and the agreement test could assert that every wire the format names is a registry wire.
  - **Test depth:** nothing pins the assistant row's persisted shape (with or without `events`); `jsonExtractor.test.js:158` (the anchor budget < 200 ms) is the one perf pin in the family.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) keep `events` off the persisted row — commit without it (the in-memory record already serves both readers) and drop the key in `typeLoadedMessage` as the load twin, pinned; (2) hoist the skill regexes; (3) drop the two non-channel mentions + the agreement assertion; (4) the pins.

### scribe (`llm/scribe.js` `runScribe` + `runNpcFrontReflection` end to end with the adapter mocked; the `buildKnown*` builders + `namePresenceIn` at 10 and 200 NPCs; `projectNpcForReflection` / `projectFrontForReflection`; `scribeAudits.js` `describeOwnedInventory` / `describePartyGear` / `describeAppliedLoot` / `LOOT_AUDIT_RULES` / `CAST_AUDIT_RULES`; `shouldScribeCombatBeat`; the orchestrator's call assembly `turnOrchestrator.js:707-735` and the cadence's `worldJournal.js:412`; `getBackgroundConfig`; tests `scribe.test.js` (2,257 lines), `directorContexts.size.test.js`) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** calls per turn and per cadence; the exact bytes of the two machinery prompts (system + user) at a realistic and at a worst-case campaign, their cache-prefix stability, and the share that is repeated instruction; CPU of the builders and the projections at roster scale; the existing byte pins. **Verified cheap/sound (measured):** ONE Flash call per ordinary turn carries extraction AND every audit (loot / payment / loss / gear / cast are fields of the same reply), one reflection per journal cadence, combat beats gated by `shouldScribeCombatBeat` (0.34 ms at 200 roster NPCs), table talk none; thinking-free, 8,192 output cap, 60 s stall guard; the Scribe system prompt is 23,641 chars (414 preamble / 8,486 schema / 14,741 rules) + `LOOT_AUDIT_RULES` 8,409 + `CAST_AUDIT_RULES` 1,424 — three variants that all EXTEND the same base as a prefix, so implicit caching can hit the base whichever lane a turn takes; `buildKnown*` × 5 = 1.9 ms at 10 NPCs and 2.7 ms at 200 NPCs / 300 cards (`namePresenceIn` tokenizes the same turn text three times plus the orchestrator's own `findPresentNpcs` — ~0.5 ms each, a nit); `describeOwnedInventory` clamps at 800, party gear at 600; the reflection's NPC and front projections hold (12 NPCs at the caps 55.8k, 4 active fronts 16.0k, resolved fronts ship nothing — the 09-20 fix) and its CPU is 10 ms at 200 NPCs; the reflection reads the cadence's PRE-commit `state`, so `recentJournal` never duplicates the `cadence` block's fresh summary; KNOWN HERO TELLS is a constant ~3.4k at the 12-tell cap (every turn by design — a sighting may come from a new witness), KNOWN APPEARANCES 2.1k, STORY CARDS 1.9k, PLACES 0.4k at their caps.
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — the Scribe call has no byte ceiling, and its largest block carries its rules on every line.** Worst case measured: system 33,474 + user 29,677 = 63,151 chars (~16k tokens) per ordinary turn on Flash; the user half is 4.7k of turn text and 24k of KNOWN context, and KNOWN PLAYER-RELATIONSHIP STANCES alone is 14,233 chars for 8 present NPCs — of which 355 chars PER NPC (2,840 of the block) are the three instruction clauses repeated on every entry (`buildKnownStances` `scribe.js:257-269`: "open thread on record (emit openThread only if…)", "recent impressions (unconfirmed; carry one into the stance ONLY if…)", "moments already on record (do NOT re-report or paraphrase…)"). DECISIONS 2026-09-26 (9) and 2026-09-27 (2) both say: the rules go in the block's header once, the lines are data (`Name — thread: "…" | impressions: "…" | moments: "…" (promise)`). A realistic turn (2–3 present NPCs) is ~12k user chars; the 8-NPC ceiling is the scene the prompt's "only NPCs in this exchange" rule makes rare, not impossible (a feast, a council).
  - **P2 — the reflection context reaches 116,653 chars (~29k tokens) at a mature campaign, and two of its blocks ship raw.** `recentJournal` is the last 3 journal rows WHOLE (21,028 chars: each carries `summary` 2,000 + `keyDecisions` 8 × 300 + `consequences` 8 × 300 + the engine's `id` / `timestamp` / `messageRange` / `fallback` stamps), the `cadence` block adds the newest summary + decisions + consequences (6,928), `premise` rides at its 8,000 cap on every cadence, and `worldFacts` slice(-12) is 6.1k with `knownBy` / `id` / stamps (`scribe.js:788-806`). NPCs 55.8k + fronts 16.0k are projected already. Once per ~10 narrative rows, thinking-free — amortized ~3k tokens per turn, the biggest single machinery prompt in the app, for a lane that reasons over "what just happened", which the summaries carry.
  - **P2 (test depth) — the reflection NPC pin certifies half the true ceiling.** `scribe.test.js:556` asserts the 12-record payload < 30,000 with a fixture whose fields sit UNDER `projectNpcForReflection`'s own caps; 12 records AT the caps measure 55,831. Nothing pins the WHOLE reflection context, the Scribe user message's ceiling, or the Scribe system prompt's shared-prefix property (`systemPrompt.startsWith(BASE)` across the no-audit / loot / loot+cast variants — the cache-prefix contract), and `directorContexts.size.test.js` — the file that pins every director lane's worst case — covers neither machinery prompt.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) STANCES rules into the block header, lines as data, + a byte-ceiling pin on the Scribe user message at 8 NPCs / 10 cards / 12 tells; (2) project journal rows for the reflection (summary + 3 decisions + 3 consequences, no stamps) and consider a reflection premise clamp (~2k: the front proposal needs the premise's factions, not its whole scaffolding); (3) fixtures AT the caps + whole-context pins for both machinery prompts in `directorContexts.size.test.js`; (4) the shared-prefix pin.

### Process notes
- Queue was EMPTY at run start (the 09-27 sweep); six lines added (0 P1, 6 P2). Coverage Snapshot not refreshed (4 days).
- **Lap-3 sub-pattern: a parsed object kept on its row is a persisted field.** The parser's output shape (35 keys, every one materialized so consumers never null-check) became a save-bytes decision the moment the orchestrator kept it on the message — with no post-commit reader. Rule: when a transient result is attached to a persisted record, name its post-commit reader or leave it off; `grep '\.events'` outside the turn is the check.
- **Second: the 09-27 "rules in the header" pattern one level down.** A context-block LINE that carries its own instruction is the overflow tail's sibling — per-row constant bytes that scale with N — and the two machinery prompts still have it where the DM prompt no longer does (STANCES: 355 chars × present NPCs). Rule for every `buildKnown*` / director context: instruction in the block's header once, entries as data.
- **Third: a "worst-case" pin fixture is built AT the projection's caps.** A fixture under the caps certifies a ceiling well below the true one (30k pinned, 55.8k real) and passes forever; the pin's fixture and the projection's clamps should share constants.
- Environment: same as 09-25..27 — no `node_modules` in the container; measurement wrote to two scratch test files, deleted.
