## 2026-09-27 — quests + enemy-stats-conditions (Lap 3: performance & token budget)

`npm test`: 3153 passing / 179 files (green; `npm install` first — the hosted container ships without `node_modules`).

Rotation: origin/master (65e094b) == HEAD after fetch, one list — it excludes chronicler, rules-math (09-26), inventory-economy, spellcasting (09-25), hero-tells, character-vault (09-24), combat-exchange, persistence (09-23), roll-resolution, cloud-sync (09-22), dice-engine, scene-art (09-21). Least recently audited eligible: **quests** (09-14), then response-parsing and enemy-stats-conditions tied at 09-15 — the coverage tie-break picks **enemy-stats-conditions** (`enemyStats.js` 98.01 vs response-parsing's 98.07 / 99.30 / 98.91). Both are first Lap 3s (quests: Lap 1 09-04, Lap 2 09-14; enemy-stats: Lap 1 09-05, Lap 2 09-15). Every number below was **measured with a throwaway vitest file** against the real `buildSystemPrompt`, the live reducer (`ADD_QUEST` / `COMPLETE_QUEST`), `sanitizeQuestRecords`, `sanitizeLoadedEnemy`, `normalizeEnemyConditions`, `combatNarrationPrompt`, and `RESPONSE_FORMAT` (deleted, never committed; zero repo changes outside the two docs).

### quests (`buildQuestBlock` `promptBuilder.js:1040-1060` + its call site `:240`; `handlers/quests.js` end to end — ADD_QUEST dedupe, COMPLETE_QUEST's fuzzy fallback, `isSameResponse`, `sanitizeQuestRecords`; the four director projections `absenceDrift.js:130`, `frontAftermath.js:120`, `regionalFronts.js:95`, `frontMigration.js:85`; `QuestPanel.jsx`; the save's `questCount`; QUEST TRACKING INSTRUCTIONS in the prefix; tests `gameReducer.quests.test.js` (28), the quest cases in `promptBuilder.test.js`, `directorContexts.size.test.js`) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** the bytes the quest list puts on every DM call and where they sit; how the block and the reducer scale with a long campaign's quest count; what each machinery lane carries of the quest list; per-dispatch and per-load CPU; the panel's per-render work. **Verified cheap/sound (measured):** a typical 4-quest block is 1,343 chars (~330 tokens) and sits right after PLAYER CHARACTER at the head of the live tail; the narration lane skips it (the 09-23 `narrationOnly` pin holds); QUEST TRACKING INSTRUCTIONS (5 bullets) is prefix; `sanitizeQuestRecords` types 2,000 rows in 3.1 ms; `COMPLETE_QUEST` on a fuzzy miss over 1,000 rows 7.1 ms, `ADD_QUEST` 2.1 ms; the once-per-response instant-tier scan over 200 same-response rows 0.08 ms (`isSameResponse` returns at the first non-system row, so an old row costs one read); the three LIVE director lanes filter to active, clamp name 120 / description 240–400, cap 6–10 rows, and `directorContexts.size.test.js` pins their worst case at 12 × 160/800; `QuestPanel` filters the list twice per render — trivial.
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — the overflow tail is uncapped in COUNT.** `QUEST_PROMPT_CAP` (12) bounds the described rows; the "…plus N older active quest(s), tracked and still open: …" line names EVERY omitted quest at 160 chars. Measured: 52 active quests → an 11,958-char block, 6,119 of it the overflow line (~1.5k tokens), live on every turn. The prompt's own rule ("open the quest the moment they act on it") plus a DM that closes rarely make stale open quests the steady state of a long campaign, and nothing ages or prunes them (by design: the panel is the player's). The cap on the described rows moved the cost into the tail rather than bounding it.
  - **P2 (nit) — `questNamesFuzzyMatch` re-tokenizes the REF for every row** (`questTokens` of both sides per comparison inside both `.filter` fallbacks). 7 ms at 1,000 rows — nothing today; the ref side is a constant.
  - **P2 (nit) — `frontMigration` ships the last 20 quests INCLUDING completed/failed at 600-char descriptions** where its three live siblings filter to active and clamp 240–400 over 6–10 rows: 14k chars worst case on a one-shot, player-initiated call.
  - **P2 (metric) — terminal rows are forever.** `state.quests` never prunes completed/failed rows; they are never rendered to the DM, yet 500 of them are 159 KB in every autosave and cloud save and typed at every load. Cheap at a realistic 100 rows (~30 KB); the 15 s background lane already softens the write rate. Noted for the persistence file's immutable-share metric.
  - **Test depth:** nothing pins the block's or the tail's byte ceiling; the directors' active filter is unpinned (the DM block's is).
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) cap the overflow names (~8 + "and K more", or collapse by `openedAtMessage` age) + a byte-ceiling pin; (2) hoist `questTokens(refName)`; (3) status filter + clamp parity in `frontMigration`; (4) the pins.

### enemy-stats-conditions (`engine/enemyStats.js` end to end with every call site's RATE — `validateCombatStart` at the parser, START_COMBAT's `normalizeCombatEnemy`, `resolveEnemyAttack`'s per-swing re-validation `combatExchange.js:1338-1342`, `rollResolver.js:645`, `sanitizeLoadedEnemy` at LOAD; the three exchange condition lanes + `applyEnemyConditionDelta`; `buildCombatBlock` `promptBuilder.js:1265-1300` as bytes on BOTH DM calls per round; `combatNarrationPrompt` `combatExchange.js:1760` POST-EXCHANGE STATE; the condition bullets of RESPONSE_FORMAT_TAIL; `CombatPanel.jsx` enemy cards; tests `enemyStats.test.js` (37), `gameReducer.conditions.test.js` (8), `promptBuilder.combatPacing.test.js`) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** CPU per boundary, the per-round prompt bytes the enemy state produces on each of the two calls, what of them is constant, and whether the narration lane reads anything twice. **Verified cheap/sound (measured):** `sanitizeLoadedEnemy` × 40 foes 0.36 ms (with a console.warn per typed damage); `normalizeEnemyConditions` on a 30-element junk list 2.0 µs; the per-swing `validateEnemyAttackBonus` + `sanitizeEnemyDamage` run on the CLEANED stored notation, so the 09-15 damage-type warn fires once at the parser and never per attack; the condition rulebook is 7 bullets / 2,074 chars inside RESPONSE_FORMAT_TAIL — prefix, cached (the whole COMBAT NOTES tail is 24,501 of RESPONSE_FORMAT's 43,724 chars, every turn, cached — prompt-building's file, recorded for it); a per-foe row is ~250 chars (~60 tokens) of genuinely live state; the enemy card maps conditions per render — trivial.
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — the combat block's constant sentences are billed live twice per round.** `buildCombatBlock` at 0 foes is 694 chars and 550 of them never change: the "LIVE COMBAT STATE OVERRIDES…" paragraph (258) and the closing "The engine owns every combat die… If phase is opening or awaiting_narration, do not declare more actions." paragraph (292) — only `Action Surge: …` and the phase are live. Rendered on the intent call AND the narration call, every round: ~140 tokens × 2. The 09-26 rule (a builder's byte is prefix or live) and DECISIONS 2026-09-26 (9) ("a block's rules go in its header once; its lines are data") both point the same way: COMBAT NOTES (prefix) or a one-line header.
  - **P2 (flag — revisits DECISIONS 2026-09-26 (2), does not reverse it) — the narration call reads the same foes twice.** On `awaiting_narration` APPLY has already committed, so `## ACTIVE COMBAT` (2,191 chars at 6 foes) renders the post-exchange HP / health / conditions that `combatNarrationPrompt`'s POST-EXCHANGE STATE (1,147 chars) carries as the AUTHORITATIVE copy — plus AC / Atk / Dmg / the turn order / the "translate a committed player action into one combat_exchange intent envelope" instruction the narration lane cannot act on ("Do not … emit JSON"). ~550 tokens per round on the DM model. The 09-23 `narrationOnly` pin (`promptBuilder.test.js:1198`) deliberately "keeps combat"; the narrower shape is header + FLANKED state (the one thing the snapshot lacks), rows and turn order dropped.
  - **P2 (nit) — the FLANKED annotation is a 97-char instruction repeated per flanked row** (6 flanked = 582 chars); `FLANKED` on the row, the sentence once under the list.
  - **P2 (nit) — `normalizeConditionDelta(slot.on_success)` is evaluated twice per check slot** (`combatExchange.js:166-167`: truthiness gate, then value).
  - **Test depth:** no byte-ceiling or constant-share pin on `buildCombatBlock`; nothing pins its shape under `narrationOnly` beyond "present"; nothing pins that the damage-type warn fires once per fight and never per attack.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) the two paragraphs into COMBAT NOTES / a header once, surge + phase stay live; (2) `narrationOnly` combat block = header + flanks; (3) the flank footnote; (4) the pins.

### Process notes
- Queue was EMPTY at run start (the 09-26 sweep); nine lines added (0 P1, 9 P2). Coverage Snapshot not refreshed (3 days).
- **Lap-3 sub-pattern: a "…plus N more" tail is a cap on the DESCRIBED rows only** — the tail's own length scales with N when it names the omitted rows. `buildQuestBlock` is the one such tail in `promptBuilder.js` (`grep 'plus \${'`); rule for every `slice(-CAP)` block: the overflow line needs its own cap, and the byte-ceiling pin covers the block WITH the tail.
- **Second: a block that renders on two calls per round pays its constant bytes twice.** The combat block is the only builder that rides both the intent and the narration lane, so its constant sentences are the priciest constant bytes in the app per round — and the narration lane already carries an authoritative copy of the live half. Rule: when a lane gets a purpose-built user prompt (`combatNarrationPrompt`), the system prompt's matching block should render only what that prompt lacks.
- Environment: same as 09-25/26 — no `node_modules` in the container; measurement wrote to a scratch file, deleted.
- Session ran on a `claude/*` working branch; per the master-only convention the result lands on `origin master` directly.

## 2026-09-26 — chronicler + rules-math (Lap 3: performance & token budget)

`npm test`: 3107 passing / 174 files (green; `npm install` first — the hosted container ships without `node_modules`).

Rotation: origin/master (28556f1) == HEAD after fetch, so the last-6 union is one list — it excludes inventory-economy, spellcasting (09-25), hero-tells, character-vault (09-24), combat-exchange, persistence (09-23), roll-resolution, cloud-sync (09-22), dice-engine, scene-art (09-21), hidden-fronts, living-world (09-20). Least recently audited eligible: **chronicler** (09-13), then rules-math and quests tied at 09-14 — the coverage tie-break picks **rules-math** (`engine/rules.js` 98.51 vs `handlers/quests.js` 100). Chronicler's first Lap 3 (Lap 1 08-29 + 09-04, Lap 2 09-13); rules-math's second (first: 08-05). Every number below was **measured with a throwaway vitest file** against the real chronicler (adapter mocked), the narrative gate, the prompt builder, `rules.js`, `normalizeItem`, and `serializeGameState` (deleted, never committed; zero repo changes outside the two docs).

### chronicler (`llm/chronicler.js` end to end; `collectNarrativeEntries` as the eligibility walk; `handleWriteChapter` + `ChronicleTab` in `JournalPanel.jsx:138-171,366-441`; the chapter lanes — `CHAPTER_FIELD`/`chapterKey` in `portraitStore.js`, `BLOB_STORES` in `persistence.js:405-425`, and `saveGameToCloud`'s `extractPortraits` `cloudSync.js:211`; `sendMessage`'s stall guard + retry `adapter.js:74-105`; tests `chronicler.test.js` (21), `chronicler.budget.test.js` (7)) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** the bytes each passage call sends and what of them could cache; how a run's call count and per-call size scale with the backlog; the largest chunk against the 90s stall guard; the chronicle's share of the local and cloud payloads; the tab's per-render work; CPU of the eligibility walks. **Verified cheap/sound (measured):** `collectNarrativeEntries` walks 6,000 rows in 4.1 ms and the tab's per-render `pendingCount` walk is 0.5 ms (0.07 at 600 rows); `chapterKey` hashes 20 × 49k-char chapters in 2.2 ms once and 0.06 ms cached (the 09-24 memo works — an autosave moves zero chapter bytes); a 1,000-message backlog closes as 33 passages in 4 parts (36k / 36k / 36k / 11k chars), every part under the 50k budget, nothing lost, the tail (700) threading each boundary; the premise clip is 1,200 of the 8,000 allowance; salvage keeps paid-for parts. Nothing to cache: a passage's constant prefix (system prompt ≈ 1.6k chars + HERO + premise) is ~700 tokens — under Gemini's implicit-cache minimum — and the transcript is 93 % of the call, unique per passage.
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — a chunk is sized in MESSAGES; its bytes are bounded only by the per-message clip.** `CHUNK_SIZE` 30 × `MESSAGE_CLIP` 4,000 puts one call's transcript anywhere between 740 chars (30 curt rows) and 122k chars (30 clipped narrations; both measured) — a 165× spread against ONE fixed ask ("300–700 words"): the curt chunk must be inflated (the contract forbids invention, so the model pads), the fat one compressed 40:1 at ~30k input tokens. Realistic play is 21k chars ≈ 5.3k tokens per passage, 33 passages ≈ 174k input tokens for a 1,000-message backlog — before Pro's default dynamic thinking on every passage (no DM-model director passes `thinkingBudget`; a retelling is closer to transcription than reasoning, so a bounded budget is the one cost lever left, and the file header's "runs on the DM model" precedent stands). The fat chunk is also the app's largest non-streaming payload against the 90s stall guard, and a stall re-sends the identical call twice more (adapter-wide) before the salvage: 4.5 minutes and 3× billing for one passage. The 09-13 "budget in one unit, clamp in another" family, on the INPUT side.
  - **P2 — the chronicle rides every CLOUD save inline.** `saveGameToCloud` extracts portraits only (`extractPortraits` is portrait-only by construction), so the IndexedDB v5 chapter split has no cloud twin: 18.3 % of a 1,000-message payload with 3 chapters (149k of 815k chars; the 09-23 audit measured 23–25 % of autosaves), re-uploaded on every manual cloud save and counted against the 9 MiB pre-flight although chapters never change. Manual only (three Settings callers) — per upload, not per turn. CLAUDE.md's "cloud saves keep the same split" sentence reads as if chapters had it.
  - **P2 (nit) — every chapter body is in the DOM.** `ChronicleTab` splits and renders all chapters' paragraphs (0.5 ms and 2,400 `<p>` for 20 × 49k chars) on every keystroke of the title input and every progress tick of a write; only the newest `<details>` is open. JS side cheap; the DOM reconcile per keystroke is unmeasured here.
  - **Test depth:** nothing pins a chunk's byte ceiling, the premise clip, or that the cloud payload carries chapter text (by design or not).
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) character-sized chunks (~20k chars, message count as the belt) + a pin on the per-passage ceiling; (2) a chapter lane in `saveGameToCloud` mirroring the portrait docs, or a recorded decision that cloud chapters stay inline; (3) a memoized chapter card; (4) the pins.

### rules-math (`engine/rules.js` end to end; every consumer's call rate — `computeACFromInventory` at its eight write sites, the exchange's `playerAc`, the resolver; `getAllSkills` in the two sheets; `findSkillInText` at the parser boundary; `describeCheckOdds` on the card — and the bytes the rules render into PLAYER CHARACTER (`buildCharacterBlock` `promptBuilder.js:759-867`) and INVENTORY (`:948-953`); tests `rules.test.js` (56), `rules.checkOdds.test.js` (17), `rules.queue0914.test.js` (6)) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** CPU per call at scale, call rates per dispatch / render / prompt build, the prompt bytes the rules produce and where they sit relative to the cached prefix, and whether any consumer renders a rules number through a formula other than the engine's. **Verified cheap (measured, per call):** `computeACFromInventory` 0.66 µs at 300 rows; `getAllSkills` 2.2 µs; `findSkillInText` 0.24 µs on an 80-char description and 3.4 µs on 1,000 chars of no-skill text (18 regexes built once at module load); `isProficientWithWeapon` 0.46 µs (it re-lowercases the class list per call, per weapon row per prompt build — still nothing); `describeCheckOdds` 0.78 µs; `d20SuccessChance` 0.07 µs; `normalizeProficiencyLists` 0.54 µs. No memoization is warranted anywhere in the file; the AC recompute on every inventory write is free.
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — the sheet's level-constant lines are billed as live: the fourth sighting.** PLAYER CHARACTER is 833–1,030 chars at L5 across the four classes, and 549–754 of them (57–75 %) are lines that change only at level-up or an ASI: Race, Class (Level), Proficiency Bonus, Stats (94), Saving Throws (123), Skill Proficiencies (48–72), Speed, Fighting Style (94) / Martial Archetype (98), Traits (58), Features (126–177). They sit at byte 60,325–64,627 — the very start of the dynamic tail — so ~140–190 tokens are re-billed uncached on every DM call for every class (two per combat round). The premise (07-18), the identity (09-24), and the spellbook (09-25) each moved for the same reason; a `## HERO SHEET` block ending the prefix after SPELLBOOK, with HP / EXP / AC / Wealth / Conditions / Resources / Hit Dice / Appearance / slots staying live, costs one cache miss per level-up or ASI. Extends DECISIONS 2026-07-18; smaller than the spellbook per campaign, but every campaign pays it.
  - **P2 (Lap-1/4 spill, reproduced) — the INVENTORY annotation computes armor AC with a second formula that skips the engine's magic-bonus read.** `buildInventoryBlock` prints `[AC ${baseAC + (acBonus || 0)}]` (`promptBuilder.js:951`) while `getArmorClass` reads `clampItemBonus(acBonus) || clampItemBonus(magicBonus)` (`rules.js:102`). `normalizeItem` folds `magicBonus` into `acBonus` for CATALOG armor only (`items.js:433`); a non-catalog armor the DM grants with `magicBonus: 2` — the channel the prompt advertises — keeps `acBonus: 0`. Measured "Elven mail" (baseAC 15, medium, +2): the DM's INVENTORY row says `[AC 15, medium armor]`, the hero's AC line says 17 + DEX — one prompt, two numbers, and the Scribe's gear audit reads the same row. The 08-28 Lap-4 rule (getAllSkills: "never a second inline formula that could drift") applied to AC. Belts hold elsewhere: `baseAC: 25` and `shieldAC: 5` are clamped by `normalizeItem` before either reader, so both agree at 18 / +2.
  - **Nit:** the character block's proficiency star reads `savingThrowProficiencies?.includes` directly (`:767`) while every rules read goes through `hasListEntry` (array-only) — safe now that the load heal types the list, one belt short of the rule.
  - **Test depth:** nothing pins the character block's constant/live split or its position; nothing pins prompt-vs-engine armor annotation parity for a non-catalog magic armor.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) the sheet's constant lines into a prefix block, split ONCE along its event lines, + a position pin; (2) one shared `describeArmorAc(item)` (or `getArmorClass(0, item) − 10`) behind the annotation; (3) `hasListEntry` at the star; (4) the pins.

- **Scope examined:** every byte the feature adds to a DM call and where it lands relative to the cached prefix; CPU per cast at scale; the Scribe's per-call spell context; what the DM window carries back after a cast. **Verified cheap/sound (measured):** CAST_SPELL 0.12 ms at 6,000 messages (`recentSpellCasts` cap 8, `findNearbyReplay` walks are nothing); `getKnownSpells` is one filter over 29 entries and `findSpell` a Map; the slot renders are one join each; HERO'S KNOWN SPELLS costs the Scribe 71–216 chars and only on cast-audit turns; the exchange lane resolves a cast slot twice per slot (`combatExchange.js:644,1022`) — trivial.
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — the spellbook is level-constant but billed uncached on every DM call.** The block is 778 chars at L1 → 1,833 at L10 (wizard; cleric 862 → 1,832), of which the catalog lines are 712 → 1,731 and only the "Spell slots remaining … DC … attack" line (65–101 chars) is live. It sits at byte 66,268 of the wizard prompt, past the dynamic start at 65,652, inside PLAYER CHARACTER behind HP / XP / wealth — ~430 tokens re-billed per call at L10, two calls per combat round. The 09-24 identity-block pattern applies exactly: the catalog lines change only at level-up (one cache miss each), so a `## SPELLBOOK` block ending the prefix after HERO IDENTITY, the slots line staying live. Extends DECISIONS 2026-07-18; does not reverse it.
  - **P2 — a Fighter's prefix carries the caster's rulebook.** `SPELLCASTING INSTRUCTIONS (Wizard / Cleric only)` is 12,373 chars (~3.1k tokens) of `CORE_INSTRUCTIONS` — 19 % of a Fighter's 65.7k-char prefix, cached but still billed at the cached rate on every call and still walked by the provider before the first token. Class is campaign-constant (`healUnknownClassRace` is the one load-time exception), so a class-gated static block keeps the prefix byte-stable per campaign. Same shape as the P2 above, the other half of the roster.
  - **P2 — the DM never sees a cast's receipt.** The success line (109 chars: the healing rolled, slots left) and all four rejections (not on the list, combat-only, incapacitated caster, "no level N+ spell slot remains") are plain `systemMessage`s — not `dmVisible`, not matching the `rolled **` regex — so `buildMessageWindow` drops them (measured: no "casts" row in the window after a CAST_SPELL). The coin lane made its rejections receipts for exactly this reason (2026-08-31 P1: "the DM must learn its re-emission was suppressed"). A "no slot remains" refusal after the DM narrated the cure leaves the fiction and the sheet disagreeing until the next turn's HP line, and a rejected cast is never ledgered, so a re-emission fails again the same way, silently to the DM.

- **Scope examined:** the per-turn prompt bytes (INVENTORY dynamic, ITEM CATALOG + ECONOMY prefix), the receipt lines' place in the DM window, reducer CPU at scale with every ledger at cap, LOAD_GAME's inventory heals at scale, the ledgers' save bytes, the Scribe's context, the panel's render inputs. **Verified cheap/sound (measured):** ADD_COIN_GRANT 0.64 ms / APPLY_COIN_LOSS 0.47 / PURCHASE_ITEM 0.13 / ADD_ITEM 0.04 ms per dispatch at 6,000 messages with all four ledgers at cap 20 and decade-old indexes (the `conversationalDistance` walk is O(entries × rows) but 20 × 6k is nothing; 0.03 ms at 40 messages); LOAD_GAME 3.0 → 4.7 → 12.3 ms at 48 / 128 / 328 rows (the O(n²) shadow-row fold included); the four ledgers are 12 KB in a save at cap; ITEM CATALOG (1,480) and ECONOMY & HEALING (7,012 chars) are prefix; the Scribe's inventory context caps at 800; the streamed reply is ChatPanel-local state (no per-chunk global re-render); the Carried cap holds (63 rows → 1,239 chars).
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — receipts are window ROWS, and each is a `user` turn.** A six-purchase + reward response posts 7 `dmVisible` lines (227 chars) and `buildMessageWindow(…, 20)` then holds 7 receipts and 13 rows of fiction — the DM's history shrinks by a third for the next ~3 turns, and the provider sees seven consecutive `user` rows between two assistant turns. The purchase line also lacks the purse total the coin line carries ("Bought Dagger for 2 gp." vs "**+5 gp** received — purse: 98 gp, 4 sp, 5 cp."). One receipt line per response (the purse once at its end), or receipts that ride the window without consuming its 20 slots.
  - **P2 — the INVENTORY block is 72 % annotations the DM does no math with.** 1,165 chars for 3 equipped + 25 carried catalog rows: `[value …]` 379 + `[AC …]`/`[1d8 slashing, …]` 455; names and counts alone ≈ 300. AC / attack / damage are engine-owned on every lane (the prompt says so), and value matters only when the DM prices a sale. Stat annotations on Equipped only, value kept, would save ~110 tokens per call.
  - **P2 (Lap-2 spill, reproduced) — an unrecognized `itemKey` with no `name` buys "Unknown item".** `normalizeItem({ itemKey: 'healingPotion' })` keeps the unknown key and names the row "Unknown item" (type gear, no value), `buildPurchaseTransaction`'s `nameless` test is `!item.itemKey && !nameRef` (`economy.js:80`) so the key alone passes it, and the purchase charges the DM's price: three of six purchases in one measured response bought "Unknown item" (two of them for 100 gp — the potion), rows the player cannot use or sell by name; `items_found: [{ itemKey }]` mints the same row. The key typo is the LLM-plausible shape — the prompt says "use itemKey when possible" and the catalog's `potionHealing` / `ropeHempen` invert natural word order. The 09-12 fix covered the no-key-no-name shape only.
  - **P2 (Lap-1 spill) — the stack has no ceiling.** `addOrStackItem` sums quantities with no `MAX_ITEM_QUANTITY` (12 × ADD_ITEM torch ×999 → one row of 11,988; `healStackedInventoryRows` sums the same way), and only `healEquippedSlots`' `normalizeItem` clamps it back to 999 on the NEXT load — a silent loss in the other direction. The prompt and panel show the live number; `MAX_SALE_PROCEEDS_CP` bounds the coin.
  - **Test depth:** nothing pins receipts-per-response or their window share, the block's byte composition, the unknown-key purchase, or the stack ceiling.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) one receipt per response; (2) annotate Equipped only; (3) an unknown key with no name is nameless (refuse visibly) — or humanize the key into the name so the fuzzy lookup gets a second chance; (4) clamp in `addOrStackItem` and the load fold with a visible line; (5) the pins.

### hero-tells (`engine/heroTells.js` end to end; `state/handlers/heroTells.js`; the cadence tick `worldMemory.js:265`; the Scribe schema / rule / context / dispatch `scribe.js:89,124,248-262,481-487`; the two prompt blocks `promptBuilder.js:237-262`; `regionalHearsay.js:201-216`; the load twins `livingWorldSession.js:150-166` + `session.js:376`; `CharacterSheet.jsx:22,590`; tests `heroTells.test.js` (16), `gameReducer.heroTells.test.js` (7)) — Lap 1
- **Scope examined:** the record's typing boundary and load twin, sighting/scene semantics, establishment and fade, the witness rule on both blocks, the beat's mint / open / close / voice / expiry lifecycle, the Scribe lane's shapes into the reducer, the hearsay path, the sheet. **Verified sound:** the Scribe shapes the registry row named all type correctly (a `witnesses` object → `[]`, a `voiced` string → a plain sighting, a `voicedBy` string → one name, `public: "yes"` → false, a 500-char text → 160, an array text → dropped); `sanitizeHeroTells` types every field and re-mints a duplicate id; both blocks are silent in combat, an unestablished tell never renders, an intimate tell renders only for its partner with the private-only rule, a dormant tell is never live and never travels, `isSameTell`'s opposite-manner guard holds, eviction ranks unestablished-first, a fiction voice inside the window closes the beat without a double stamp.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — the scene window slides with every report, so the most consistent habit never becomes a pattern.** A sighting joins only when `now - held.lastSeenMessage > 16`, and `lastSeenMessage` advances on every sighted report (`heroTells.js:253-265`). Measured: 13 reports at 2 / 4 / 8 / 12 / 16-row spacing → ONE sighting, never established; 17+ → 8. A turn is 2–6 raw rows and the Scribe is asked for one sighting per scene per pattern — the pipe the DM shows every serious turn is the tell that never reaches three scenes, while one reported a fortnight apart does. The sibling rule (`appendBondMoments`, `npcRoster.js:275`) measures from the held moment. Every fixture in both suites is ≥ 30 rows apart, which is why the suite cannot see it — and the pending playtest would have read it as "the Scribe never re-reports".
  - **P2 — the expiry fallback lands on the sheet as a line someone said.** `stampTellVoiced` increments `voicedCount` when a window closes unvoiced (the rotation stamp, by design) and `listVoicedTells` shows any `voicedCount > 0` with `saidBy` = `witnesses[0]` — measured: an unvoiced window puts "…pipe… — said by Maren" under "How others see you".
  - **P2 — the window's edges.** The cooldown is stamped at the MINT and a delayed window can close after it expires: with one tell on record the same tell got a fresh window on the tick after its first closed (`sinceVoiced` 40 is not `< 40`) — the same remark cued back to back; and a `voiced` report before a delayed window opens (110 < opens 124) is not `beatVoicedByFiction`, so the cue still renders at 126 and expiry stamps `voicedCount` 2.
  - **P2 — a Scribe `id` from another tell attaches the sighting to the wrong record** (`findHeroTellMatch` id-first, no kind/text check): "pays the poor double" under the jokes tell's id added a scene and Brother Anselm — who may now voice it — to "jokes the moment things get serious".
  - **P2 — witness-less tells are dead weight; companions are present but never witnesses.** A report with no witnesses establishes (3 scenes) yet can never render, mint, or travel — it spends a `MAX_HERO_TELLS` slot and a KNOWN slot ("seen by: nobody named"); the party is "always present" for voicing but must be named per sighting to witness.
  - **P2 — the three beat cooldowns load unclamped** (`lastHeroTellBeatMessage` / `lastRelationshipBeatMessage` / `lastWonderMessage`, `livingWorldSession.js:155-166`): `1e9` survives LOAD_GAME on all three and every beat is silenced forever. Minor twin: `normalizeSightings` clamps `[900, -2]` to two sightings (50, 0) instead of dropping them — a count is semantic.
  - **Test depth:** none of the above is pinned. Token note for the Lap-3 visit: one tell's standing block is 925 chars (2,061 at the ceiling), ~860 of it a fixed paragraph in the dynamic half on every turn a witness is present; beat block 712; KNOWN HERO TELLS up to 3.7k chars per Scribe call.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) new-scene judged against the last accepted SIGHTING, `lastSeenMessage` sliding for the fade only, a 4-row-cadence pin; (2) engine stamp and fiction stamp on separate keys, the sheet reading the fiction's; (3) cooldown from the close, a voice at or after the mint spends the beat; (4) id + kind + containment floor; (5) party names unioned into witnesses at ADD_HERO_TELLS, no-witness reports dropped; (6) `finiteStamp(…, maxMessageCount)` on the three stamps; (7) the instruction paragraph into the cached prefix.

- **First-audit lessons (a new feature's Lap 1 before its first playtest):** (1) **a scene window measured from the last REPORT never closes under continuous reporting** — measure it from the last accepted event, as the sibling module already does; (2) **an engine assumption must not share a key with a fiction fact** — the rotation stamp and "who said it" were one counter, and the player-facing view read the assumption; (3) **a cooldown that starts at the mint can expire before a delayed window closes** — start it at the close; (4) **"always present" must mean the same on both sides of a rule** — companions are present for voicing but not for witnessing; (5) audit a new feature BEFORE its playtest: the P1 would have read as a provider failure ("the Scribe never re-reports") and cost a playtest day.

`npm test`: 2958 passing / 162 files (green; `npm install` first — the hosted container ships without `node_modules`).

Rotation: origin was AHEAD of the session's working branch by one commit (the 09-22 audit) — master reset to `origin/master` first; the last-6 union excludes roll-resolution, cloud-sync (09-22), dice-engine, scene-art (09-21), hidden-fronts, living-world (09-20), progression, chat-orchestration (09-19), memory-journal, prompt-building (09-18), story-memory, vector-memory-rag (09-17). **combat-exchange** and **persistence** (both 09-11) are the oldest eligible, and also the two weakest coverage spots of the eligible set (`combatExchange.js` 85.36, `persistence.js` 88.68) — the pair's second Lap-3 pass (first: 08-03 / 08-04). Lens: DM and Flash calls per combat round and per fight, prompt bytes the combat subsystem adds (static prefix vs dynamic half vs window), the message rows a fight leaves behind and who reads them, save bytes per write, writes per TURN, and the payload's immutable share. Every number below was **measured with a throwaway vitest file** against the real reducer, the real exchange planner with real crypto dice, the real prompt builder, the real narrative predicate, `serializeGameState` + `extractPortraits`, and `createAutosaveRuntime` under fake timers (deleted, never committed; zero repo changes). Coverage snapshot (09-17) is 6 days old — inside the 7-day rule, not refreshed. **Both features' 08-03 / 08-04 Lap-3 and 09-11 Lap-2 findings verified in code:** exchange lines are out of the DM window (20 rows of prose, zero exchange rows, every round), the result stores events only, the hero's AC is computed once per enemy phase, the flush cover and the dirty-gated hide flush hold, listing is metadata-only, and the 09-21 portrait split leaves zero portrait bytes in the payload.

### combat-exchange (`engine/combatExchange.js`, `state/handlers/combat.js`, the two DM calls per round — intent in `turnOrchestrator.js:364-366`, narration in `ChatPanel.jsx:527-624` — the per-beat Scribe, and the `exchangeLine` rows' downstream readers: `buildMessageWindow`, `collectNarrativeEntries` → journal cadence / `buildPresenceText` / chronicler) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** per-exchange CPU and payload; the message rows APPLY mints and every reader of them; the narration prompt's size; the combat block's size; what the intent call and the narration call each send (prefix / dynamic / window); the Scribe on combat beats; the save delta per fight. **Verified cheap/sound:** `planCombatExchange` 0.11 ms at the 6-foe ceiling; `lastExchangeResult` ≤ 2.9 KB and the combat envelope ≤ 5.2 KB (autosaved during `awaiting_narration` — trivial); `combatNarrationPrompt` 1.5–2.5 KB (10 events); the combat block 1.4 KB for 4 foes; `heroRolls` ledgers 3–4 rolls per exchange (12 for a 3-exchange fight — the 09-21 fix holds); the window stays 20 rows of prose through every round (the 08-04 fix holds); a 3-exchange fight adds 11 KB to the save; `resolvedExchangeIds` resets at END_COMBAT.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — the `exchangeLine` tag has one reader; the narrative predicate is not it.** `collectNarrativeEntries` (2026-09-01, THE "transcript as story" rule) admits every `system` row that is not `error`/`record`, so the dice lines a fight mints are narrative to the journal cadence, the presence window, and the chronicler. A realistic 9-exchange fight (4 foes at 34 HP vs a L5 fighter + 2 companions) mints 64 exchange lines (5.6k chars; 76 rows in all). Simulated on the real cadence rule: the first post-fight turn fires the journal cadence TWICE in a row (40 rows / 34 dice lines, then 36 / 30) — two Flash calls, two journal entries for one fight holding two of SESSION HISTORY's three slots and two journal RAG rows — the exact inflation the 2026-09-06 "count narrative, not raw" fix set out to end, one layer over. `buildPresenceText` is dice lines after every commit and after the victory narration, so scene presence (KNOWN NPCs slots, `findPresentNpcs`, the RAG gate) is judged from `**Oda attacks Marsh bandit 4** — Rolled **20**…` for the fight and the turn after. The lines have exactly two readers that need them: the chat and the narration prompt's RESOLVED EVENTS. Fix: exclude `exchangeLine` in the ONE predicate (out-of-combat roll lines keep their seat — no second carrier there; narrow DECISIONS 2026-09-06's "engine lines still ride it" explicitly), plus a pin that a 9-exchange fight fires one cadence at most.
  - **P2 — a combat round is the token-hottest turn, and the narration call pays the whole dynamic half.** Combat-time system prompt 86.6k chars = 66.6k cached prefix + ~20k dynamic (≈5k uncached tokens; 12 NPCs / 30 facts / 8 journal / 6 quests fixture) + a 16k-char window (≈4k tokens), twice per round; a 9-exchange fight = 19 DM stream calls ≈ 170k uncached + 320k cached input tokens to narrate 2 KB RESOLVED EVENTS blocks. The narration call re-sends ACTIVE QUESTS / WORLD FACTS / SESSION HISTORY / LOCATION TRANSITION HISTORY / INVENTORY (10k+ chars) it cannot use. A `narrationOnly` prompt variant that drops those blocks (prefix untouched) halves the uncached tokens on half the fight's calls.
  - **P2 — the Scribe runs on every beat.** ~10 Flash calls per 9-exchange fight (20.8k-char system prompt + narrative + four KNOWN blocks each), extracting from prose the engine snapshot owns and that is deliberately not embedded; the ≤2-facts budget is per beat. Gate to terminal narration + beats that name an out-of-party roster NPC.
  - **Test depth:** the 08-04 pins cover the window and the message count; nothing pins the lines out of the predicate / cadence / presence, counts calls per round, or pins the narration prompt's ceiling.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) `exchangeLine` → predicate exclusion + cadence pin; (2) the narration-only prompt slimming; (3) the Scribe gate; (4) the pins.

### persistence (`state/persistence.js`, `state/portraitStore.js`, `state/autosaveRuntime.js` + `autosavePolicy.js`, the GameContext wiring, the LOAD_GAME heal at scale) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** bytes per write and their composition at three campaign scales; UI-thread cost of serialize / clone / stringify / load-heal; writes per TURN on a realistic dispatch timeline; IDB requests per write; `persistence.test.js` (60), `autosaveRuntime.test.js` (20), `autosavePolicy.test.js`. **Verified cheap/sound (measured):** mature campaign (600 messages / 560 summarized, 40 NPCs at the dossier caps, 80 cards, 120 facts, 60 journal, 8 chapters × 45k, 30 places, 20 quests, 50 rolls) = 1.56 MB; `serializeGameState` + `extractPortraits` 0.12 ms, `structuredClone` 3.0 ms, stringify 6.5 ms, LOAD_GAME heal 20 ms (and it accepted the synthetic save whole); epic (1,500 messages, 20 chapters, 80 NPCs) = 3.55 MB / 5.5 / 15 / 35 ms — phones 3–5×, still ms-level: the portrait split did its job; `getKey` probes move zero portrait bytes; listing is metadata-only; `loadGame` hydrates refs in one readonly transaction; the hide flush is dirty-gated; the flush cover holds.
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — five full-snapshot writes per ordinary turn, four per combat round.** Fake-timer run of the real runtime on a realistic timeline (player line 0 s; DM reply + events 7 s; Scribe wave 11.5 s; cadence 15 s; reflection 19 s) → writes at 2.0 / 9.0 / 13.8 / 17.0 / 21.0 s. The 2 s debounce collapses bursts, not the turn's phases, which sit 3–5 s apart: 7.8 MB cloned and written per mature turn (17.8 MB epic) for a few KB of change after the DM reply. A two-tier debounce (2 s for messages/character/combat/inventory; ~15 s for the background lanes, hide flush still protecting) → 2 writes per turn.
  - **P2 — 55–62 % of every write never changes.** Summarized messages 497 KB + chronicle 361 KB of 1.56 MB (mature); 1.30 + 0.90 MB of 3.55 MB (epic). The chronicle is the portrait case exactly — a `chronicleChapters` store with refs, the `extractPortraits`/`restorePortraits`/sweep trio generalized by field. The summarized prefix is the harder half (IDEAS.md already holds the append-only messages idea).
  - **P2 (minor) —** `saveGame` probes every portrait ref on every write although the previous metadata record it reads three lines later already proves them present — probe only new refs.
  - **Test depth:** no writes-per-turn pin, no payload-composition pin (08-04 (4) still open), no zero-probe pin.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) two-tier debounce + timeline pin; (2) the chronicle store; (3) probe-skip; (4) the composition pin.

## 2026-09-22 — roll-resolution + cloud-sync (Lap 3: performance & token budget)

`npm test`: 2958 passing / 162 files (green; `npm install` first — the hosted container ships without `node_modules`).

Rotation: origin was AHEAD of the session's working branch by three commits (the 09-21 audit, its queue sweep, the live-play report) — master reset to `origin/master` first; the last-6 union excludes dice-engine, scene-art (09-21), hidden-fronts, living-world (09-20), progression, chat-orchestration (09-19), memory-journal, prompt-building (09-18), story-memory, vector-memory-rag (09-17), scribe, providers-adapter (09-16). **roll-resolution** and **cloud-sync** (both 09-10) are the oldest eligible, coverage tie-break `rollResolver.js` 87.69 / `auth.js` 78.94 — the pair's second Lap-3 pass (first: 08-03 / 08-04). Lens: machinery calls per check turn, prompt bytes the check subsystem adds, save bytes it holds, UI-thread CPU per cloud save, and bytes on the wire and in the bundle. Every number below was **measured** — call counts with a throwaway harness against the REAL orchestrator/parser/reducer (a Gemini machinery key present so the arbiter, detector, and retrieval actually run; adapter + vector store mocked), bytes with `serializeGameState`/`buildSystemPrompt`, and the bundle with `npm run build` (throwaway test deleted, never committed; zero repo changes). Coverage snapshot (09-17) is 5 days old — not refreshed.

### roll-resolution (`engine/rollResolver.js`, `engine/outOfCombatRollPolicy.js`, `engine/roleplayCheck.js`, the accept / challenge / change-approach hops in `turnOrchestrator.js:744-907`, the check turn's machinery calls, `## RECENT TABLE RULINGS`, `checkOdds.js`) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** every LLM/embed call one check turn makes from the player's line to the outcome; what each hop sends and what it persists; the bytes the subsystem adds to the prompt and to the save; dispatches per roll; the card's render cost. **Verified cheap/sound:** a JSON-declared check costs hop 1 = 1 query embed + 1 DM stream + 1 arbiter (Flash, thinking-free, pinned `< 6000` chars); accept = 1 query embed + 1 DM stream + the Scribe + 1 narrative embed — the semantic detector's gate stayed CLOSED on the outcome narration (no second detector call), and the 08-03 fixes hold: the [ROLL RESULT] user prompt (1,406 chars typical, ≤ ~5.3k with a 4k withheld setup) is sent but never persisted, the hidden setup is out of the DM window, and no hidden summary row is written. Dispatches: 2 per skill check (`ADD_ROLL` + line; +2 per damage), batched into one render. `pendingRoleplayCheck` is 31 KB at its ceiling (6 rolls, 4k action, 4k setup) and transient. The card's `describeCheckOdds` is pure arithmetic per render. `pruneRecentRulings` re-normalizes ≤ 5 rows per prompt build — µs.
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — the outcome hop and the challenge hop re-embed a byte-identical query.** Hop 2 is a first-class turn since 09-02 (correct), and it passes the proposal's `playerAction`; `sceneContext` is that text + `Location:` (`turnOrchestrator.js:318-323`), so `retrieveRelevant` was called with the SAME string on hop 1, on accept, and on a challenge — reproduced in the harness (`identical=true` both times). One blocking Gemini round trip per check turn — two on a challenged one — for a vector the previous hop already held; the results are then re-gated by presence, which is right, but the network hop is pure repeat. A per-session query memo (text→vector, cap ~16, cleared with the store) removes it.
  - **P2 — the detector's payload has no clamp.** `detectSemanticTextRolls` sends `DM narrative: ${narrative}` raw (`responseParser.js:301`); the arbiter one call later clamps action and narrative to 2k each. The gate keeps ordinary turns free, but when it opens on a long narration the detector pays the whole thing (up to `MESSAGE_CONTENT_MAX` 20,000 ≈ 5k tokens). Clamp from the end (the request sits in the tail) and pin it.
  - **P2 — RECENT TABLE RULINGS pays its rule text per ruling.** +3,157 chars at the ceiling (5 rulings) in the dynamic prompt half for up to 24 messages, +558 for the typical single ruling; ~250 of every line is the same binding instruction repeated. Hoist the three rules into the header, render rulings as data lines → ~1.2k at the ceiling.
  - **Test depth:** the orchestrator harness runs without a machinery key, so nothing counts calls or embeds on a check turn; no size pin on the detector payload or the rulings block.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) the query-vector memo; (2) clamp + pin the detector; (3) the rulings-block rewrite; (4) a machinery-keyed harness case that pins "one arbiter, one Scribe, N embeds" per check turn.

### cloud-sync (`state/cloudSync.js`, `state/auth.js`, `config/firebase.js`, `fitPortraitsToBudget`, the list/save callers in `App.jsx:49-66` and `SettingsModal.jsx:80-125,204-232,319-345`, the SDK in the bundle) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** bytes on the wire per manual save and per list; UI-thread passes per save; Firestore reads per UI action; what every player downloads for a feature most never configure. **Verified cheap/sound:** the 08-04 metadata-only parent docs hold (`listCloudSaves` never downloads payload bytes; the transaction's previous-doc read is metadata too); the stale-chunk sweep is bounded (64); the UI-thread cost of a save is a click-time one-off — stringify 11 / 30 / 50 ms + TextEncoder 2 / 4 / 5 ms at 12 / 40 / 100 portraits on this CPU (phones ~3–5×); `listCloudSaves` runs once per uid at boot and once per Saves-tab open; `auth.js` is a 3-function wrapper with nothing to measure.
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — the Firebase SDK ships to everyone, preloaded.** Build: `vendor-firebase` 330 KB / 102.5 KB gzip, `modulepreload`ed by `dist/index.html` beside React — 23 % of all shipped JS (447 KB gzip total) — because the three SDK importers are static and `App.jsx`/`GameContext.jsx` import them statically; `initializeFirebase` is only CALLED with a config. Cloud sync is bring-your-own and opt-in; a dynamic `import()` behind the config check turns the chunk into an on-demand load (returning players have it cached, but every first load and every phone pays it).
  - **P2 — a manual cloud save re-uploads every portrait and every chunk.** Measured: 12 NPC portraits → 2.38 MiB per save (47 % portraits, 9 chunk docs); 40 → 4.78 MiB (74 %, 17 chunks); 100 → 9.94 MiB, over budget, so `fitPortraitsToBudget` drops 11 and the payload is stringified + encoded AGAIN (+57 ms) → 9.00 MiB in 32 chunks. The 09-21 local split (content-addressed `portraits` store, refs in the payload, write-when-absent) stops exactly at the cloud boundary — the pure helpers (`extractPortraits`/`restorePortraits`) already exist; a `users/{uid}/portraits/{key}` collection + a rules match + `portraitRefs` on the metadata doc is the twin, and the budget dropper retires.
  - **P2 (minor, not queued) —** `handleSave` refreshes the save lists TWICE per manual save (after the local write and again after the cloud write: 2 `getDocs` over `users/{uid}/saves` + 2 IDB scans) — metadata-only, so bytes are small, but one refresh after both writes is the same UI.
  - **Test depth:** no test asserts the byte share or chunk count of a cloud save with N portraits; nothing guards the entry HTML against a preloaded `vendor-firebase` chunk.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) lazy-load the SDK behind the config; (2) the cloud portrait collection; (3) one list refresh per save; (4) a post-build check script + a chunk-count pin.

### Process notes
- Queue had ZERO open items at run start (the 09-21 sweep cleared it); six lines added (0 P1 — the pair's Lap-2 P1s from 09-10 are all fixed and its remaining costs are click-time or first-load one-offs).
- **Lap-3 lessons, third pair.** (1) **A promoted lane repeats its sibling's calls:** making the outcome hop a first-class turn (09-02, correct) silently doubled the query embed because the pipeline was copied whole — when a lane is promoted, diff the calls it now makes against the hop before it and memoize what is identical. (2) **Opt-in feature, opt-out bytes:** a bring-your-own integration's SDK should load when it is configured, not because a module that might use it is imported. (3) **A storage fix on one of two "same snapshot" paths has a twin on the other:** the local portrait split (09-21) left the cloud path carrying the same bytes it removed locally — `serializeGameState`'s "both paths persist the SAME snapshot" rule cuts both ways.
- Registry amendment: roll-resolution's scope now names the three hops, the check turn's machinery calls, the rulings block, and the card; cloud-sync's names `config/firebase.js`, the budget dropper, the list/save callers, and the SDK's place in the bundle — today's findings live there.

## 2026-09-21 — dice-engine + scene-art (Lap 3: performance & token budget)

`npm test`: 2940 passing / 162 files (green; `npm install` first — the hosted container ships without `node_modules`).

Rotation: origin was AHEAD of the working branch by four commits (the 09-20 audit, its same-day queue sweep, the Flash playtest) — master reset to `origin/master` first; the last-6 union excludes hidden-fronts, living-world (09-20), progression, chat-orchestration (09-19), memory-journal, prompt-building (09-18), story-memory, vector-memory-rag (09-17), scribe, providers-adapter (09-16), response-parsing, enemy-stats-conditions (09-15). **dice-engine** and **scene-art** (both 09-09) are the oldest eligible — the pair that has opened every lap since 08-20, now on **Lap 3 (performance & token budget)**: bytes on the save and on the wire, per-turn CPU, tab memory, call counts. Every number below was **measured with a throwaway vitest file** against the real reducer / exchange planner / prompt builder / serializer (deleted, never committed; zero repo changes). Coverage snapshot (09-17) is 4 days old — not refreshed. **Both features' 08-01 Lap-3 and 09-09 Lap-2 findings verified fixed in code:** the reducer-level `ROLL_HISTORY_CAP`, DicePanel slicing before it reverses, `MAX_DIE_SIDES` + `MAX_ROLL_MODIFIER`, the Sneak Attack pool drawn as ONE `rollDice`, `boundCompanionDamage`, `sanitizeRollHistoryEntry`; the input-keyed scene cache + `peekCachedImage`, `PROVIDER_PROMPT_MAX` 4000, the LRU eviction pin, filter-before-slice in the cast, typed provider payloads + `<img onError>`, the ONE portrait allowlist at every write, typed hero identity fields, the `fallback`-skipping situation picker.

### dice-engine (`engine/dice.ts`; the `rollHistory` ledger end to end — six append sites → `appendRollHistory`, `MAX_SAVED_ROLLS`, the load slice; its consumers: RECENT DICE ROLLS `promptBuilder.js:200-201,953-957`, `DicePanel.jsx:44`, the recall dossier's DICE tier `recallDossier.js:274-283`, and the orchestrator's dice-landed probe `turnOrchestrator.js:746,784`) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** per-roll CPU and allocation; bytes per stored roll and per prompt block; rolls per combat exchange; what each consumer reads and how far back. **Verified cheap:** one `Uint32Array(count)` + one `getRandomValues` per pool (µs), ~232 B per stored roll → the whole 50-roll ledger is ≤ 12 KB on the save, RECENT DICE ROLLS is 215 chars a turn (≈ 60 tokens, dynamic half of the prompt). Token cost of this feature stays negligible.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — the 08-01 cap broke the orchestrator's "did dice land" probe.** `acceptRoleplayCheck` snapshots `rollHistory.length` before `handleRequestedRolls` and compares after; `appendRollHistory` slices to 50 and LOAD_GAME slices to 50 too, so once the ledger is full the length never moves — reproduced: 50 rolls → `ADD_ROLL` → still 50, `diceRolled === false`. Full is the NORMAL state of an established campaign: one fight fills it (10 rolls per exchange measured with hero + 2 companions + 3 foes → 5 exchanges), 50 checks fill it, and any save that once held 50 loads full. Post-dice consequences: a Stop during the outcome narration RESTORES the proposal (`:792` — "the dice are final: restoring would reopen the reroll-bargaining door" says the comment right above it), and an outcome-call failure posts "Error resolving check" and RE-PROPOSES the check (`:797-799`) instead of the "dice landed… say continue" line — the player rolls again while the first die already sits in the ledger, the heat ledger, and the visible [ROLL RESULT] line. `turnOrchestrator.test.js:224` and `.abort.test.js:67` both start from an EMPTY ledger, which is exactly why the suite passes. The 09-09 lesson one layer over: a guard that becomes a throw moves the failure; **a cap that becomes a slice moves the counter** — every consumer that watches a capped collection's LENGTH must be re-read when the cap lands. Fix is one line: compare the newest roll's `id` (or return the resolved rolls from `handleRequestedRolls`, which already knows them).
  - **P2 — the ledger's 50 is counted in dice, not in moments.** An exchange appends every actor's attack AND damage (saves/heals extra): a 5-exchange fight evicts every out-of-combat check the campaign ever rolled, `MAX_SAVED_ROLLS` mirrors it, and the recall lane's DICE tier — "what did I roll to…" — answers from a ledger one fight flushes. RECENT DICE ROLLS after an exchange is the enemy tail (`- A attacks Vesa: **15** (11 +4)`, `- B damage: **3**`): engine internals the narration prompt already carries as RESOLVED EVENTS. Suggest one summary row per exchange (the hero's own d20s) or a separate combat lane, and skip the block while `combat.active`.
  - **P2 (minor) —** `sanitizeRollHistoryEntry` spreads `...entry` (`shared.js:65`), so unknown keys on a roll ride every save (the 09-16 project-to-known-keys rule); 50 rows bound the blast radius.
  - **Test depth:** no test feeds the accept path a full ledger; no test pins the cap against a consumer that counts.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) id-based probe + a 50-deep pin; (2) per-exchange summary rows / a combat lane + no block in combat; (3) project the loaded roll to known keys.

### scene-art (`llm/providers/imageGen.js` chain + cache; `llm/sceneDirector.js`; `SceneArt.jsx` memo/effects; portrait persistence — `applyNpcPortrait` `handlers/npcs.js:59-80`, the hero write `handlers/character.js:104-120`, `serializeGameState` → `saveGame` `persistence.js:296-330` and the cloud pre-flight; every machinery/director lane that `JSON.stringify`s an NPC or character record) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** compose-call bytes at the ceiling; whether any of the 11 JSON director payloads ships `portraitUrl`; save bytes and serialization CPU as portraits accumulate; the render sizes the stored pixels serve; tab memory held by the cache; the load-side regex cost. **Verified cheap/sound:** `composeScenePrompt` at its ceiling (6k-char situation, hero + 3 companions + 4 NPCs with 600-char looks and identity locks, 6 foes) is 9,573 chars + 2,747 system ≈ 3k tokens on Flash, on demand only; NO lane ships a portrait — `frontAftermath`/`frontMigration`/`npcFodderReview`/`npcEnrichment`/`projectNpcForReflection`/`premiseDrafter`/`frontDirector` all project (the 08-02 reflection fix held); `visualTargets` and the `<img src>` re-render are reference-equal cheap; `sanitizePortraitUrl` × 40 at 300k = 0.3 ms at load; portraits downscale at all three call sites.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — portraits are ~96 % of every save and have no aggregate budget.** Measured through `serializeGameState` at the downscale's ~90k chars each (vault comment: 60–110k): 12 NPC portraits → 1.19 MB payload (1.14 MB portraits), 40 → 3.7 MB, 100 → 9.2 MB (over `CLOUD_SAVE_BYTE_LIMIT` — cloud saves refused on portraits alone), 40 at the 300k per-portrait ceiling → 11.9 MB. Every autosave (2 s debounce after ANY persisted change — the DM turn, each Scribe upsert wave, the cadence; several per turn) structured-clones the whole payload OBJECT into `savePayloads` and the cloud path stringifies it (16 ms at 40 portraits on this CPU; 62 ms at the ceiling; phones 3–5×), and each manual slot duplicates the set — for an image the Journal card renders at **84 px wide** (`Journal.css:655`; the hero 108×138). The hero export ceiling bounds ONE portrait; nothing bounds the roster's. Rule: **bytes that never change must not ride the record that changes every turn** — the DB-v3 messages/payload split is the house pattern: a `portraits` store keyed `${sessionId}:${npcId|hero}` with the record carrying a reference (and the cloud payload stripped or budgeted), or at minimum a per-campaign portrait budget with a visible "oldest portrait dropped" line.
  - **P2 — `portraitPrompt` is write-only ballast.** ≤ 2,000 chars per NPC (`npcs.js:76`) and on the hero (`migrations.js:395`), read only as the `<img title>` tooltip at `JournalPanel.jsx:721` (the hero's is never read): 59 KB at 40 portraits, 146 KB at 100 — the 08-27 settings-copy class.
  - **P2 — the scene cache holds up to 10 FULL-resolution renders in tab memory by design** (`imageGen.test.js:350` pins "scene renders skip downscaling"). Unmeasured here (no provider in the container): an xAI 1k JPEG is a few hundred KB base64, a Gemini inline PNG several MB — the fallback tier can pin tens of MB on the phone target. Keep the CURRENT picture full-res; cache a display-sized re-encode.
  - **P2 — store at the size you render:** 480×640 for an 84-px card is 5.7× the pixels a 3×-DPR phone draws; a 256×341 NPC tier cuts the P1 bytes ~3× with no visible loss (the hero's 108×138 and the wizard reveal are the only larger consumers).
  - **Test depth:** nothing asserts a portrait byte share or budget on a save, nor that a stored portrait is sized to its render.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) the portrait store / budget; (2) drop or clamp `portraitPrompt`; (3) a 256×341 NPC tier; (4) display-sized scene cache entries; (5) pins.

- Queue had ZERO open items at run start (the 09-20 sweep cleared it); seven lines added (2 P1).

### living-world (`engine/regionalHearsay.js`, `llm/absenceDrift.js`, `llm/frontAftermath.js`, `llm/regionalFronts.js`, the SET_LOCATION arrival tail + INSTALL_* in `handlers/npcs.js`/`handlers/fronts.js`, the `BACKGROUND_DIRECTORS` effect `ChatPanel.jsx:58-104,334-368`, the `pending*` markers) — Lap 3
- **Scope examined:** every background director's call count, context bytes and retry path; the two private blocks at their ceilings (HEARSAY 1,485 / AWAY 1,883 chars — bounded, windowed, fine); the hearsay slot allocation across consecutive arrivals; the ledger cap; marker lifetimes across turns, departures and reloads.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — a failed background director retries on EVERY message with no cap, no backoff, and no give-up, and its stuck marker blocks the whole lane for the rest of the campaign.** The effect parks the key while a call is in flight and NULLS it on failure (`ChatPanel.jsx:350-355`); its deps include `state.messages.length` and `combat.active` (`:365-366`), so the next message re-fires. The markers never expire: reproduced — `pendingFrontAftermath` still `shouldGenerate` after 30 `ADD_MESSAGE`s AND after a LOAD_GAME round-trip; `pendingAbsenceDrift` still pending after the hero LEFT the place and 40 messages passed. Per attempt the aftermath context is up to **85 KB (~21k tokens) on the DM model with default thinking** (remainingActiveFronts 17 KB, worldFacts 16 KB, knownNpcs 15 KB, recentEvents 11 KB, premise 8 KB; drift 31 KB, regional 28 KB), ×3 inside the adapter on a transient. A PERSISTENT failure — a Gemini `promptFeedback.blockReason` on the 12 raw narrative messages the context ships (non-retryable since 09-06, so it fails fast and re-fires on the very next row), a prose-answering DM (Grok), an exhausted quota, a bad key — costs one hidden DM-model call per turn indefinitely, surfaced only as a console.warn "will retry". And the markers are EXCLUSIVE gates: `!state.session?.pendingAbsenceDrift` (`npcs.js:394`) and `if (state.session?.pendingRegionalFronts) return next` (`:617`) — a stuck drift means no return is ever drifted again and a stuck region seed means no land is ever seeded again. This is the 08-18 memory-journal P1 class ("no escape hatch"), fixed there with a failure streak; the four director markers never got one.
  - **P1 — the two hearsay slots go to the two OLDEST resolved fronts at every new place, forever; fresh deeds never travel.** `selectRegionalHearsay` walks resolved fronts first in ARRAY order (`regionalHearsay.js:129-144`), `consider` stops at `HEARSAY_MAX_ITEMS` = 2 (`:121-125`), a resolved front never ages out as a source, and the ledger is keyed per (deed, place) so every new place is a fresh key. Reproduced: three resolved fronts (two from message 20/40, one from 380) + a salience-5 witnessed card + a fight five scenes old → **five consecutive new towns all offered the same two ancient victories as `legend`**; the fresh victory, the card and the fight were never offered anywhere. The block's whole budget is spent on the stalest content the system holds. (The ledger's 30-entry cap = 15 arrivals: after that a burned pair re-offers at the SAME place; secondary once sources age out.)
  - **P2 — a drift keeps generating for a place the hero has left.** The marker survives departure (above); the call fires (or keeps retrying) and `INSTALL_ABSENCE_DRIFT` writes `agenda`/`lastNotes` + a world fact under a now-stale `awayDistance`, while the away block never renders (location-gated) — canon without payoff. `hearsayOfferSurvivesArrival` already decides "unrelated arrival drops the offer"; the marker needs the same rule.
  - **P2 — the aftermath context ships full dossiers of the OTHER fronts.** `remainingActiveFronts` → `compactFront` (`frontAftermath.js:53-69,87-90`) carries every portent, hint, note and relationship of up to 3 fronts (17 KB at the ceiling) where the prompt needs only "faction, flavor, territory" for divergence — the 3-field projection `regionalFronts.js:76-83` already uses for the same rule.
  - **Test depth:** no reducer test pins that a `pending*` marker survives departure or reload (the retry surface), no test asserts a fight or card ever wins a slot beside resolved fronts, no size pin on any director context, and the director table is inside the 0% ChatPanel.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) a reducer-owned failure count per marker (`DIRECTOR_ATTEMPT_FAILED { name, key }` → `attempts`), re-fire only after ≥ 6 conversational messages, give up at 3 and CONSUME the marker as the quiet answer with a console line — the journal's failure-streak pattern; (2) rank hearsay candidates newest-first across sources, at most ONE front slot per arrival, and retire a deed as a source after it has traveled ~3 times or past ~200 conversational messages unless local; (3) clear `pendingAbsenceDrift` on an unrelated arrival; (4) project `remainingActiveFronts` like `existingCampaignFronts`; (5) the pins above.

### Process notes
- Queue had ZERO open items at run start (the 09-19 sweep cleared it); seven lines added (2 P1).
- **Lap 3 opened.** Its first lesson: **a one-shot marker needs a give-up rule** — every fire-and-forget lane keyed on a persisted marker must count its failures and consume the marker, or a deterministic failure becomes a per-turn tax plus a permanently blocked lane. Second: **a slot budget's priority order is a design decision** — when a bounded block picks N items from several sources, walking the sources in declaration/array order silently makes the oldest source the only one that ever renders; rank by freshness unless the design says otherwise. Third: a private block's "cheap" verdict expires — re-measure at the ceiling whenever a line is added (the tempo block grew 8× since 08-02 through four good additions).

Lens: the journal cadence as a Flash-lane AND save-lane payload (every summary field and every stored row against null / scalar / object / oversized values, and the pipeline's dispatch ORDER under a throw), and the prompt as the one reader of every persisted field — which state fields still reach a block builder untyped after the 09-09 → 09-17 load-heal sweeps. Every finding below was **reproduced empirically** with throwaway vitest files (deleted, never committed; zero repo changes) unless marked read-only. ### memory-journal (`engine/worldJournal.js` end to end; `ADD_JOURNAL_ENTRY` / `MARK_MESSAGES_SUMMARIZED` in `handlers/worldMemory.js:216-249`; the journal rows' LOAD_GAME heal `handlers/session.js:284-299`; the readers — SESSION HISTORY / LOCATION TRANSITION HISTORY, `applyStoryMemoryDormancy`, the Journal panel, the return card, the RAG mount seed) — Lap 2
- **Scope examined:** the Flash reply's every field through `normalizeJournalSummary` and the dispatch loop; the stored row's every field through the load heal into the prompt and the panel; the cadence's own failure escape under each throw site. **Verified sound:** `normalizeJournalSummary` (non-object → null; `key_decisions`/`consequences` string-or-drop, 300 × 8; the literal `"null"` location dropped); string / number / object-name elements in `npcs_encountered` (skipped or sanitized by `sanitizeNpcLanePayload`); a non-array `world_facts` (ignored); the summary `.slice` on non-arrays; `SET_LOCATION fillOnly` clamping its own write; the 09-17 `summary` clamp at load; an object entry `location` in the transition scan (`isSameLocation` tokenizes it to nothing — no throw).
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — one `null` in `npcs_encountered` makes the cadence a runaway duplicator.** The entry is dispatched, THEN the NPC loop reads `npc.name` on the null and throws; the catch returns without the MARK, and the successful parse already reset the failure streak — so the `MAX_BATCH_FAILURES` hatch can never fire. Reproduced: three cadence calls → three `ADD_JOURNAL_ENTRY`, zero MARK, index pinned; one Flash call and one duplicate entry per turn forever; the unsummarized stretch never leaves the DM window. Worse, each duplicate is stamped `now`, so on the third `applyStoryMemoryDormancy`'s cutoff is seconds ago and every active salience-≤2 card went dormant (reproduced through the reducer). The fix is ordering as much as typing: validate, commit entry + mark together, then the side dispatches; reset the streak after the mark.
  - **P2 — the row heal types the containers, not the contents.** `consequences: [{…}, <100k>]` → `[object Object]` in SESSION HISTORY and a 167,115-char prompt from one entry (over the 160k budget; the live write clamps, the load twin does not); an object `keyDecisions` element reaches the Journal panel's `<li>` (the 07-25 React-child class, read-only); `timestamp: "junk"` persists and silently switches dormancy off while the entry is in the last-3 window; `fallback: "false"` is truthy; an object `id` is a React key.

### Process notes
- Queue had ZERO open items at run start (the 09-17 sweep cleared it); nine lines added (3 P1).
- **New Lap-2 sub-pattern: commit order is a hostile-input surface.** A pipeline that dispatches its durable record FIRST and its side effects AFTER, with one catch around both, turns any throw in the side effects into a replay of the record — and a failure counter reset before the commit makes the replay unbounded. Rule for the lens: for every LLM-lane pipeline, list the dispatches in order, throw at each one, and ask what the retry does. (`maybeAutoSummarize` is the one found today; `runScribe`'s queued dispatches were checked on 09-16 from the "what is lost" side, not the "what is duplicated" side.)
- **Second: a typed CONTAINER is not a typed field.** `Array.isArray(x) ? x : []` is a presence heal for the list — the 09-17 "a list element is a text field too" rule applies to every load heal that stops at the container (journal rows today; the 09-14 proficiency lists and 09-17 card lists were the same fix).
- **Third: the load heal's spread is the un-audited half.** `healLoadedCharacter` is nine explicit fields on top of `...character`; every field a prompt block reads that is NOT in the explicit list (today: `traits`, `features`, `speed`) is a raw save value. The same holds for `migrateLegacyNpc`'s `...npc` (`relationshipHistory` behind the `arcDisposition` gate) and the session sub-object (`premise`). A cheap standing check: diff the fields each builder renders against the fields each heal names.

### vector-memory-rag (`engine/vectorMemory.js` end to end; the ChatPanel seed effect `ChatPanel.jsx:358-413`; `turnOrchestrator.js` retrieval `:246-258` and live adds `:130-133,475,611`; `embedTexts`/`embedText` in `providers/gemini.js` as the batch boundary; `loadPersistedEmbeddings` as the cache boundary) — Lap 2
- **Scope examined:** every seed/live-add input against non-string, oversized, and junk-subject values; the campaign key against a non-string id; the batch against a per-request rejection; the cache rows against junk fields. **Verified sound:** `addMemory`'s non-string text guard; `normalizeSubjects` (80-char, cap 4, `String()`-typed); `findSubjectsInText` on junk names; the presence gate treating an unjudgeable subject as present; a non-string `session.id` re-minted at load (so the cache re-keys once instead of never caching); `deleteCampaignMemories` with a non-key id rejecting into its own catch; embed vectors element-typed (09-16); `enforceCampaignCap` evicting transient rows only; the `onblocked`/`onversionchange`/`onabort` handles.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — one rejected text nulls its whole 100-item embed chunk, on every mount.** `embedTexts` sends 100 texts per `batchEmbedContents` call and `continue`s past a non-OK response with all 100 slots null; `seedMemoriesInner` stores nothing for a null slot and rebuilds the same missing set in the same order next mount; nothing bounds a text before the request. Reproduced with the real provider + seed under a fetch stub that 400s any request carrying a >20k text: 150 seed items with one 100k journal summary at #10 → 2 calls, **50 rows stored, the 100-row chunk lost**; mount 2 → the same 2 calls, the same 50. A permanent hole of up to 99 healthy neighbours around every bad text, plus one wasted call per Continue, console-only. Sources that reach the seed unbounded: a loaded journal `summary` (the live write clamps at 2,000, LOAD_GAME leaves the field untyped) and any world-fact / story-card `knownBy` / `linkedNpcNames` element (above).   - **Test depth:** `gemini.test.js:139` pins the provider-level all-null on a batch 500 and `vectorMemory.test.js:377` a per-slot null; nothing pins the seed-level consequence (neighbours lost, same chunk lost again next mount) or an over-long text through the seed/live add.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) bound the embed input at the seed/live-add boundary (skip-and-warn, or truncate the EMBED text while keeping the full text as the row key); (2) on a chunk-level failure retry that chunk per item (or bisect) so one bad text costs one row; (3) type the cache row's text fields at load; (4) a one-line system notice when retrieval fails for a narrative turn; (5) the pins.

### Process notes
- Queue had ZERO open items at run start (the 09-16 sweep cleared it); eleven lines added (3 P1). Coverage snapshot refreshed (7 days old; overall 78.85 → 80.45, suite 2296 → 2710).
- **New Lap-2 sub-pattern: `null` is not `undefined`.** A default parameter (`card = {}`) is a presence heal for `undefined` only — `null` walks straight past it into the first property read, and a single null element takes down a whole array `.map` (LOAD_GAME) or a whole dispatch loop (the Scribe turn). The 09-08 fronts fix, the 09-11 turn-order fix, and today's cards are the same bug three times. Rule for the lens: grep every `function x(payload = {})` at a lane or load boundary and feed it `null`.
- **Second: a list element is a text field too.** `normalizeTextArray`-style helpers cap the COUNT and forget the element length, and a scalar where a list was expected reads as "no list" — for `knownBy` that is the difference between a secret and common knowledge. Check every list-typed lane field for (a) per-element clamps and (b) scalar-to-list folding.
- **Third: a batch is a blast radius.** Any per-request rejection inside a batched call must degrade per ITEM, and the retry loop (here: "the next mount re-embeds what's missing") must not re-form the same failing batch. `embedTexts` is the one batched provider call today; the rule applies to any future one.

`npm test`: 2580 passing / 141 files (green; the hosted container shipped without `node_modules` again — `npm install` first).

### scribe (`llm/scribe.js` extraction + reflection lanes, `tryParseDirectorJson` as the parse boundary, `llm/scribeAudits.js`, and every reducer the Scribe dispatches into — `UPDATE_NPC`/`upsertNpc`, `UPDATE_CHARACTER`, `ADD_STORY_MEMORY_CARDS`, `ADD_ITEM` via the loot audit, `UPDATE_LOCATION_PROFILE`, `ADD_TRAVEL_LINK`) — Lap 2
- **Scope examined:** every field of the Scribe and reflection schemas against absent / object / oversized / stamp-carrying values, through the dispatch and into the prompt, the save, and LOAD_GAME. **Verified sound:** `ADD_WORLD_FACTS` (whitelist + 400 clamp, object fact dropped); `ADD_TRAVEL_LINK` (typed, clamped, evidence-gated); `UPDATE_LOCATION_PROFILE` (junk type → null, `DEADLY` folds, object region → null); bond moments (`normalizeBondMoments` types text/kind/salience/voice); `openThread`/`trust` clamps; a string `callbackHooks` → `[]`; the reflection's `front_advances`/`tempo_directive`/`front_proposals` (the 09-08 typing holds); the audits' amount clamps and stand-down rules.

  - **P1 — the parser anchors on `world_facts`, and the prompt tells the model to omit empty fields.** `tryParseDirectorJson` returns null when the anchor key is absent — no "the response IS the object" fallback like `parseJsonObjectLoose` has — while rule `scribe.js:120` reads "Only include fields you have actual information for — omit empty/unknown fields", which licenses exactly that shape on every ordinary turn where something happened but no durable fact did. One fragment and the hero is painted as a different person; the prompt's "emit the COMPLETE description" is the only guard, the exact position the 09-06 P1 found indefensible for NPCs.
  - **P1 — `UPDATE_NPC` has no key whitelist and no clamp on its current-state fields.** `upsertNpc` DELETES six known-dangerous keys and spreads the rest; `normalizeNpcRecord` keeps unknown keys; both lanes reach it (the DM's `npc_updates` is an untyped `guardedList`, the Scribe dispatches `{ ...candidate }`). ### providers-adapter (`llm/adapter.js`, `providers/sse.js`, `providers/gemini.js`, `providers/openaiCompatible.js` + `openai.js`/`xai.js`/`xaiKey.js`, `llm/machinery.js`, `loadSettings` + the GameContext merge as the settings boundary, the orchestrator's stream call as the DM consumer) — Lap 2
- **Scope examined:** every provider response against null / non-object / non-string bodies, junk SSE events, headers; the settings blob as persisted input; the stream's lifetime. **Verified sound:** `Retry-After` parsing (junk/negative/huge → null/cap); symbolic + numeric stream error codes; a non-string `finishReason` → "stopped early (…)"; refusals on both factory lanes; `promptFeedback` with and without a candidate; embed HTTP/shape failures → null inside try; `GameContext` resets a model id not in the catalog, so a junk `settings.model` never reaches the raw URL interpolation; the adapter's per-attempt abort + external-signal precedence.
- **Findings:**
  - **P2 — a `null` JSON body defeats the retry classifier.** `makeHttpError` does `response.json().catch(() => ({}))` then `error.error?.message` — a body that parses to `null` (a proxy's `null`, an empty-JSON gateway) THROWS `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'error')` out of the helper (reproduced): `.status` and `.retryAfterMs` never stamp, a 429/503 shaped this way is not retried by `sendMessage`, and the player sees the TypeError instead of "Gemini API error (429)". The 200-with-`null` twin throws the same from both non-streaming lanes (`data.candidates` / `data.choices`, reproduced).
  - **P2 — one junk SSE event kills the stream.** `readSseStream` parses `data: null` to `null`, guards only its own in-band error check, and calls `onEvent(null)`; both consumers dereference it and the whole DM turn dies as a TypeError (reproduced on both providers); a `body: null` response throws from `getReader`.
  - **P2 — non-string content rides the OpenAI-compatible lanes.** The stream does `choice?.delta?.content || ''` then `fullText += text` — an object `content` (a content-parts array from a compat proxy) becomes **"[object Object]"** streamed to the player AND committed to the transcript (reproduced: `"[object Object] there"`); the non-stream lane returns an array `message.content` as-is (reproduced), which every machinery caller `String()`s into an anchor miss → silent extraction loss. Gemini's `extractCandidateText` is string-gated; the factory is not.
  - **P2 — the settings blob is the one persisted input without a field heal.** `loadSettings` types the container only and `GameContext` spreads the fields over the defaults. Reproduced: `geminiApiKey: 123` throws `?.trim is not a function` from `getMachineryGeminiKey` — `AppShell` calls `isMachineryReady` in RENDER whenever `apiKey` is set, so a corrupted settings row takes the shell down at boot behind the app-level boundary (unreachable until the row is cleared by hand); `normalizeXaiApiKey(123)` throws at the first xAI/scene-art call. The save got its field heals on 09-10/11; settings never did.
  - **P2 — `embedText`/`embedTexts` validate vector LENGTH, not elements.** A 768-slot vector of strings returns as a vector (reproduced); `addMemory` stores and persists it, cosine goes NaN so the row never retrieves this session, and only the next mount's `every(Number.isFinite)` load filter drops it.
  - **P2 (read-only) — the DM stream has no stall guard.** `sendMessage` aborts a non-streaming call at 90s; `streamMessage` has only the Stop button's `AbortController`. A proxy that accepts the POST and never sends a byte, or stops mid-reply without closing, parks the turn in "waiting" until the player notices — the 2026-08-08 stall class, one lane over.
  - **Test depth:** none of the six shapes is pinned — the provider suites feed well-formed bodies and `data: {…}` events only, `machinery.test.js` never passes a non-string key, no embed test returns non-numeric elements.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) object-guard the parsed body in `makeHttpError` and both `send`s; (2) `onEvent` object gate + null-body check in `readSseStream`; (3) string-typed content on both factory lanes; (4) type-strict key helpers + a typed `loadSettings`; (5) element validation in the embed helpers; (6) a first-byte/idle timer inside `streamMessage` (~60s without a chunk → abort with the retry message, reset on progress); (7) the pins.

### Process notes
- Queue had ZERO open items at run start (the 09-15 sweep cleared it); fourteen lines added (3 P1, all on the Scribe side). Coverage snapshot not refreshed (6 days).
- **New Lap-2 sub-pattern: the machinery is a trust boundary too.** Every earlier Lap-2 pass hardened the DM wire and the save; the Scribe's JSON is dispatched WHOLESALE into the same reducers (`{ ...candidate }` → `UPDATE_NPC`, the raw card payload, the audit's item entries) with "the reducer is the field boundary" as the stated contract — and the reducer projects nothing. Rule for the lens: a reducer fed by ANY LLM lane projects to known keys and clamps every text it stores; "the prompt says to omit it" is not a guard, and the DM/Scribe/reflection/Deepen-memory lanes should each be walked into every reducer they dispatch.
- **Second: an anchor is a schema assumption the prompt must honor.** `tryParseDirectorJson` requires a key the same module's prompt tells the model to omit when empty. Check every director/Scribe anchor list against its prompt's omit rules (the front directors anchor on required lists — fine; the Scribe and the reflection do not).
