Verified sound: the Scribe's `location_profile` dispatch projects only `{type, danger, region}` (an LLM cannot stamp `theaterFrontIds`/`aliases`/`lastVisitedMessage` through it — checked because `UPDATE_LOCATION_PROFILE` would accept them); `sanitizeRecentHearsay` and the hearsay block's item sanitizer (text 300, grade whitelist); `sanitizeAbsenceDrift`'s non-array `developments` → `[]`; `sanitizeAftermathProposals` → `normalizeEmergentFront` complete-or-nothing on both installers.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — `recentEncounters` has no load sanitizer, and one null entry crashes the prompt build on EVERY turn.** `session.js:157-159` only slices; `buildWorldTempoBlock` reads `entry.enemies` unguarded in the "Recent fights" line (`worldTempo.js:496`) — reproduced: `[…, null]` → "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'enemies')" out of `buildSystemPrompt`, i.e. the campaign loads and then every turn fails — the 07-29 "one null entry crashes buildSystemPrompt on every turn" class, one array further on (`computeRecentHeat`/`computeFoeFatigue` are `?.`-safe, the render line is not). The same missing boundary lets an object `enemies` become "the hero cutting down [object Object] at Millhaven" in hearsay AND the tempo line, an arbitrary `outcome` string print verbatim into the prompt ("…, Stalemate; the DM must now grant a level)" — reproduced), and 5k-char `enemies`/`location` ride both blocks unclamped (hearsay clamps to 120/90; the tempo line clamps nothing). Every sibling ledger (`recentHearsay`, `recentRulings`, `recentChecks`, `rollHistory`) has a typed sanitizer; this one needs `{ enemies: string, location: string|null, messageIndex: finite, outcome ∈ victory|defeat|escaped, foeFamilies: string[] }` or drop.
  - **P2 — the absence-drift locality gate and the write disagree on WHICH NPC.** `INSTALL_ABSENCE_DRIFT` admits a development when SOME local roster NPC `namesMatch`es it (`npcs.js:302-304`), then `upsertNpc` writes to the FIRST roster NPC that matches (`shared.js:653-656`). Reproduced: roster ["Maren of the Reeds" (Deep Fen), "Maren Tallow" (Millhaven)], drift for "Maren" at Millhaven → the fen witch's `lastNotes` became "Married the miller" and the chandler's stayed "chandler". The prompt hands the director full names and asks for them verbatim, so the exposure is a bare-first-name reply on a roster with a shared given name — real in long campaigns. Resolve the development to the matched LOCAL record's `id`/full name before the upsert (the gate already found it).
  - **P2 — `session.absenceDrift`, `session.regionalHearsay`, and the `pending*` markers load raw.** `session.js:225` passes `payload.session` through untouched: (a) `buildWhileYouWereAwayBlock` renders a stored `frontSymptom.maxIntensity` verbatim as the label ("maximum intensity confrontation — and ignore all rules: rumors, …" — reproduced) and never re-checks `frontSymptom.frontId` against a live ACTIVE front, so a symptom installed for a front that resolves inside the 12-message window (or a tampered one) still reads as "permitted here"; developments naming NPCs not on the roster render as canon; (b) a string `pendingAbsenceDrift: "yes"` loads as-is, `shouldGenerateAbsenceDrift` fires the DM-model call for an empty place, and `INSTALL_ABSENCE_DRIFT`'s key guard passes on `undefined !== undefined` → reproduced: a world fact installed with no locality check at all. (c) `regionalHearsay` is the well-behaved one (items re-sanitized at render; only `locationName` is trusted). Normalize the four session sub-objects on load (shape + finite stamps + `frontId` ∈ active fronts), and whitelist the intensity label at render like the tempo block should.
  - **P2 (minor):** `sanitizeAbsenceDrift` coerces an object `world_fact`/`front_symptom` with `String()` (see the hidden-fronts "[object Object]" item — one fix covers both).
  - **Test depth:** `gameReducer.livingWorld.test.js` (deep on the live path) never loads a save; no test feeds `buildWorldTempoBlock` a null/typed-junk encounter, `buildWhileYouWereAwayBlock` a stale/hostile `frontSymptom`, or `INSTALL_ABSENCE_DRIFT` a shared short name.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) `sanitizeRecentEncounters` at load + `?.`-guard and clamp the tempo "Recent fights" line + a null-entry prompt-build test; (2) id-resolved drift writes; (3) load-time normalization of the living-world session sub-objects + render-time front liveness check; (4) the pins above.

## 2026-09-07 — progression + chat-orchestration (Lap 1: correctness & test depth)

`npm test`: 2193 passing / 105 files (green)

Rotation: the last-6 union excludes the six memory/parser/spell/rules features; among the eligible, progression (08-30) was least recently audited, and living-world vs chat-orchestration tied at 08-31 — broken toward chat-orchestration by the Coverage Snapshot (`ChatPanel.jsx` 0%). Every finding below was **reproduced empirically** against the live reducer/runner with a throwaway vitest file (deleted, never committed; zero repo changes) unless marked read-only.

### progression (`engine/progression.js`, `state/handlers/character.js` ADD_EXP/LEVEL_UP/ASI, END_COMBAT/quest/front award sites, `eventChannels.js` XP wires) — Lap 1
- **Scope examined:** `progression.js` end to end; every `awardExperience` caller (`handlers/combat.js:199-218`, `quests.js:139-170`, `fronts.js:268-280`, `migrations.js:330-338` load replay); the DM XP lanes (`eventChannels.js:327-328` → `applyEvents.js:328-346` → `character.js:272-389`); `healLoadedCharacter` (the 07-28 string-concat fix holds); `progression.test.js` (46 tests) + `gameReducer.expLedger.test.js`. The 08-30 items verified fixed: revive-on-level-up, the `isDead` guard, the ASI `heroDown` guard, `perLevelHpGain`, and the shared `guardExpAwardLedger`.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 (design — rpg-balance-master ruling; completes, does not reverse, DECISIONS 2026-08-26):** **the two DM XP lanes are prompt-gated only.** `level_up: true` hands out a whole level whenever the DM emits it; the exp ledger's constant `levelup` marker only catches an ECHO inside 4 conversational messages — reproduced: four emissions five messages apart took a hero L1→L5 with zero suppression lines. `exp_awarded` clamps at 10000 while the prompt promises "tens to low hundreds" (`promptBuilder.js:591`) — reproduced: one event, L1→L5 with 3500 banked. And `level_up` plus a bonus ≥ the next threshold double-levels (L1→L3; the progress line reads "650 / 300 XP" because the XP line prints before the milestone) against applyEvents' own comment "skip ADD_EXP to avoid double-leveling". The 08-26 ruling made XP engine-owned on three verifiable tiers precisely because models award inconsistently (gpt-5.6 +75 / gemini 0 on one scripted quest) — `level_up` is now the single biggest DM-writable numeric lever left (a level > a front resolution), and the live 08-26 report showed the model reaches for it. Boss XP is the precedent: an untrusted flag honored only inside an engine-verifiable band. Proposal: `level_up` → the front tier (50% of the current threshold — "milestone" stays meaningful, two milestones = one level), `exp_awarded` → ≤ `getQuestCompletionXp(level)`.
  - **P1 — a level crossed at a DEFEAT terminal full-heals the downed hero.** END_COMBAT's `slainXpOnly` award runs `applySingleLevelUp`, whose heal deliberately has revive semantics (08-30). Reproduced both live shapes: (a) low-level-solo setback → "**Astra is defeated.** … capture, rob, spare…" immediately followed by "**Level Up!** … Fully healed — back on your feet, no longer dying!" (full HP, `lowLevelDefeat` cleared) while `combatNarrationPrompt` tells the DM "The player is mechanically defeated. Narrate the setback or collapse" (`combatExchange.js:1726`); (b) a hero who STABILIZED (3 successes → `dying: false`, 0 HP, Unconscious — `terminalState` maps `projected === 'stable'` to `defeat`, `:1450`): `revived` is false, so `currentHP: newMaxHP` is written with NO condition cleanup — 36/36 HP and `conditions: ['unconscious']`, the exact limbo the 08-30 fix set out to kill, reached through the stable state instead of the dying one (`progression.js:96-122`). Fix: on a defeat END_COMBAT grow maxHP but keep the downed state (or apply the pending level-up after the defeat narration commits), and widen `revived` to "0 HP or Unconscious" so any full heal clears the condition.
  - **P2:** a DM `level_up` at level 20 is a silent no-op — zero new messages (reproduced). Every other suppressed reward posts a line.
  - Sound under re-reading: `getExperienceThreshold` junk-clamping; the boss floor/ceiling; `estimateCombatExperience` reading `maxHp` before a dead foe's 0 `hp`; the quest one-shot guard (prior terminal status) and same-turn instant tier; the front milestone bypassing the ledger by construction; `replayPendingLevelUps` on load (revive semantics there are correct — the level was owed).
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) bound both DM lanes engine-side (balance ruling first); (2) defeat-terminal level-up keeps the hero down + the widened `revived`; (3) max-level line; (4) pins for all three.

### chat-orchestration (`llm/turnOrchestrator.js`, `components/Chat/ChatPanel.jsx`, `turnVisibility.js`, `eventRouting.js`, `sessionPriming.js`) — Lap 1
- **Scope examined:** `turnOrchestrator.js` end to end (755 lines), ChatPanel's priming/director/cue/combat-narration effects and `handleSend`, the setup-visibility and routing policies, all six orchestrator suites. The 08-31 items verified fixed: `loadNonce` in the AppShell key (`App.jsx:249`), the fresh `summarizedBoundary`, `sessionId` into director installs, both AbortError branches restoring the proposal (`turnOrchestrator.abort.test.js` exists).
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — an opening scene that requests a roll is swallowed, then retried into three hidden rows.** The priming lane calls `sendToLLM(prompt, null, { openingScene: true })` with no player action, so the arbiter/semantic paths are skipped but `deriveSetupVisibility` is not: `requested_rolls` in the opening ⇒ `hideSetup` ⇒ the narration commits HIDDEN, `applyEvents` runs in `setupPhase` (the opening's `starting_items`/`quest_updates` are deferred into nothing — reproduced: 0 quests, no knife), and NOTHING stages the proposal (the priming `.then` only checks `committed.hidden`, `ChatPanel.jsx:266-269`). It then throws "did not commit", `hasPrimedRef` resets, and the ladder re-fires up to 3× — three hidden assistant rows in the save, then the error line; a reload repeats the whole cycle because `shouldPrimeCampaignOpening` counts VISIBLE assistant messages only (`sessionPriming.js:11-19`). An in-medias-res premise ("a chase in progress" — the opening prompt's own sanctioned exception, `sessionPriming.js:26`) is exactly where a DM asks for an Athletics check. Fix: on the `openingScene` lane strip `requestedRolls` before visibility derivation (there is no action to adjudicate) and let the narration stand; belt: the `.then` should treat a committed-but-hidden opening as a bug to reveal, never as "retry".
  - **P1 — the 09-06 empty-reply guard has a JSON-only hole on the lanes that DISCARD events.** `!narrative.trim() && !parsed.events` (`:333`) — but on `narrationOnly`/`tableTalk` the events are nulled two lines later (`:338`), so a reply that is only a fenced block commits a blank assistant bubble (content `""`, not hidden) into the chat, the save, and the DM's 20-message window. Reproduced on both lanes. On combat narration the `.then` then fires `COMPLETE_COMBAT_NARRATION` (`ChatPanel.jsx:494`): the round advances with its story lost and the Retry-narration affordance gone (phase no longer AWAITING_NARRATION). A DM pattern-matching RESPONSE_FORMAT into a narration-only request is the documented Grok failure shape.
  - **P2 — `runPostTurnExtraction` reads state the turn just invalidated.** It calls `getState()` in the same task as the turn's dispatches (the file header documents this exact trap for messages, `:187-198`), so: a travel turn embeds the ARRIVAL narration under the departure place's `[Location: …]` prefix AND metadata (`:567-571` — retrieval renders "recorded at: <old place>"); and a post-roll OUTCOME that starts combat reaches `finalizeRoleplayTurn` (`:576-579`), which runs the Scribe, loot audit (`!latest.combat?.active` is pre-turn, `:558`), narrative embed, and auto-summarize on the fight-start narration — the four things `handleSend` deliberately skips when `combatStartedNow` (`ChatPanel.jsx:695-703`). Read `events.location`/`combatStart` from the committed record the function already trusts for everything else. (Read-only — the synchronous test harness cannot exhibit it.)
  - **P2:** Stop is inert during the post-stream helpers: the nudge's `sendMessage` carries no `signal` (`:483-491`; 90s stall guard × retries), nor do the roll-policy review and semantic-roll calls, while `isLoading` keeps the Stop button visible.
  - **Test depth:** the 09-06 suite pins `''` only (`turnOrchestrator.test.js:523-548`); no test sends an opening with `requested_rolls`; the harness's synchronous `getState` structurally hides the same-task-staleness class — a harness option deferring state visibility by one macrotask would expose it.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) opening-lane roll strip + hidden-opening guard, pinned with a chase-opening test; (2) throw on no-prose for event-discarding lanes, pinned on both; (3) committed-record reads in `runPostTurnExtraction`; (4) thread the turn's `signal` into the helpers.

### scribe (`llm/scribe.js` context builders + extraction lane, `upsertNpc` in `state/handlers/shared.js`, `engine/npcRoster.js` merge policy) — Lap 1
- **Scope examined:** `buildKnownAppearances`/`buildKnownStances`/`buildKnownStoryCards`/`buildKnownLocations` and their call sites (`turnOrchestrator.js:561-564`, `ChatPanel.jsx:502-505`); `runScribe`'s npc lane; `upsertNpc` end to end; `mergeNpcDossierText`/`appendBondMoments`/`appendCallbackHooks`/`namesMatch`/`dedupeNpcRoster`; the DM's `npc_updates` channel (`eventChannels.js:368`, `applyEvents.js:413`); `npcRoster.test.js` (60 tests) and `gameReducer.npc.test.js` (37 tests). The 09-01 scribe items verified fixed.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — the merge contract's context is looked up by full-name SUBSTRING, so the DM's normal short-name usage starves it — and appearance then plain-replaces.** `buildKnownAppearances` and `buildKnownStances` gate on `haystack.includes(name.toLowerCase())` (`:137,179`). A turn that calls "Saima Aallotar" just "Saima" — the exact alternation the 2026-07-23 romance playtest hit, which `namesMatch` fixed on the ROSTER side — yields no KNOWN APPEARANCES and no KNOWN STANCES (reproduced: both null). The Scribe, told to emit complete merged descriptions only "when KNOWN APPEARANCES lists this character", emits the turn's fragment; `namesMatch` routes it into the right record; and because `appearance` is a plain replace by design (`shared.js:596-598` — haircuts and disguises must be able to drop details) the look is gone. Reproduced end to end: "A tall woman with white hair to her waist, grey eyes, a broken nose, and a heavy build; wears a green wool cloak." → `"a fresh scar on her cheek"`. This is the precise failure the 2026-07-25 appearance-merge design exists to prevent, defeated by one `includes`. Stances degrade more gracefully (the fragment appends via `mergeNpcDossierText`), but the "complete rewrite" path the prompt promises never fires either. The DM's own `npc_updates` lane is a raw `guardedList` passthrough with no merge context at all, so a DM-emitted `appearance` fragment wipes the record the same way. (`buildKnownStoryCards`, added this morning, survives the short name through its subject-token rung — reproduced present.)

Drop `id` from name-matched updates, clamp trust 0..100, keep `pinned` a player-only write.

- **Suggested improvements:** (1) token-level name matching (`namesMatch`, or the vectorMemory word-boundary helper) in all `buildKnown*` builders + an engine belt on `appearance` (an incoming look that covers few of the known tokens and is much shorter is a fragment — merge, don't replace), pinned with the Saima case on both lanes; (2) the payload whitelist/clamps; (3) pins.

### prompt-building (memory injection: `buildJournalContext` KNOWN NPCs, `curateNpcsForPrompt`/`scoreNpcForPrompt`, WORLD FACTS, DRAMATIC CALLBACKS, RETRIEVED MEMORIES) — Lap 1
- **Scope examined:** `promptBuilder.js:100-236` block order + `buildWorldFactsBlock`; `buildJournalContext` (`worldJournal.js:326-451`); `scoreNpcForPrompt`/`curateNpcsForPrompt`/`computeNpcImportance`/`formatNpcEmbeddingText` (`npcRoster.js:495-681`); `buildStoryMemoryPromotion`; the seven promptBuilder suites. The 08-31 items verified fixed.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — KNOWN NPCs can omit the person in front of the hero.** Curation is a pure score ranking into 8 slots: location match +14, but a rich dossier anywhere scores 51 (importance 20 + recency 8 + tension 6 + stance 6 + hooks 4 + history 3 + agenda 2 + basedIn 2). Reproduced: eight dossier-rich rivals in the capital plus a thin ferrywoman the hero is talking to at the crossing — she is dropped even with her `lastLocation` matching (44 vs 51), and the block's overflow line calls her "(1 other NPCs available via RETRIEVED MEMORIES when relevant)". The DM narrates the dialogue without her looks, gender, disposition, or stance — the fields the block's own header says must stay "EXACTLY consistent". Every mature campaign has eight NPCs with tension and stance somewhere; this is the steady state, not an edge. The morning's presence text (`buildPresenceText` + `findSubjectsInText`) is the missing input: reserve slots for scene-present and location-matched NPCs first, rank the rest.
  - **P2 — importance saturates at birth.** `computeNpcImportance` seeds from the STORED value (`clampImportance(npc.importance, 3)`) and re-adds every structural bonus on each update (rosterTier +1, non-generic name +1, any dossier field +0.5…), so a named character is 5/5 the moment it is created (reproduced: a lantern-seller with one note = 5; `{name, rosterTier}` alone = 5). The curation's importance term is a constant 20 for everyone, and KNOWN NPCs prints "importance: 5/5" on every line — a signal that reads as meaning something and means nothing. Compute from dossier fields only.
  - **P2 (design, read-only) — recency is wall-clock and `lastSeen` is not "seen".** `scoreNpcForPrompt` uses `ageHours/12`, and `lastSeen: Date.now()` is stamped on EVERY upsert — absence-drift installs for NPCs the hero has not seen (`handlers/npcs.js:309`), journal `npcs_encountered` re-mentions of past events. Conversational distance, stamped only from the per-turn Scribe/DM lanes.
  - **(read-only notes)** the `npc` RAG row (`formatNpcEmbeddingText`: notes + stance + agenda) and the roster promotion card (`story_relationship`: "Toward the hero: stance…") embed the same stance text twice per NPC — the diversity pass may or may not fold them; and the `npc` row carries `Agenda:` (rule 9 private interior) into RETRIEVED MEMORIES without the `[SECRET — …]` marker world facts and cards get. Neither is a bug; both are token/boundary polish for the next lap.
  - **Test depth:** `npcRoster.test.js:107,185` curate rosters of 2–3 — the cap never bites in a test; importance saturation is unpinned.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) reserved slots for present + located NPCs, pinned with the eight-rivals case; (2) dossier-only importance; (3) conversational recency stamped from live lanes only; (4) the read-only polish when the prompt lap comes round.

### story-memory (`engine/storyMemory.js`, `state/handlers/worldMemory.js`, curation at `turnOrchestrator.js:206-218`, the Scribe's card lane at `scribe.js:325-331`) — Lap 1
- **Scope examined:** both files end to end; the DM's `memory_updates` path; the Scribe's extraction prompt + context (`scribe.js:60-115,257-287`); `promptBuilder.js:184-200` injection; all four suites (storyMemory ×2, reducer, epistemics). Both 08-30 items verified fixed and pinned (`npc-bond-` promotion ids + the twin heal; birth stamp + documented replace-merge).
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — `resolved` is not terminal.** The ADD merge spreads `{...existing, ...card}` (`worldMemory.js:92-102`) and a normalized incoming card ALWAYS carries `status: 'active'` (`storyMemory.js:128-129` defaults it), so a Scribe re-report of a beat the DM already resolved via `memory_updates` flips it back to active. Reproduced: promise → DM marks `resolved` + `used` → next turn's Scribe re-reports the same beat from a recap line → `active`, one card, back in DRAMATIC CALLBACK OPPORTUNITIES for the next scene. The pinned intent is that only a `dormant` card revives (`gameReducer.storyMemory.test.js:220`); resolved was never pinned. Root cause one tier up: the Scribe prompt carries KNOWN APPEARANCES / STANCES / PLACES but never the existing card pool, so every recap of a paid-off beat is re-minted rather than updated. Same ruling the fronts got on 2026-09-01: resolved is terminal in the engine.
  - **P1 — curation is roster-driven, not scene-driven.** Both `curateStoryMemory` call sites pass `s.npcs` — the WHOLE roster — as `npcs`. `scoreStoryMemory` then (a) adds +5 for any linked NPC found in that list, i.e. for every card whose person exists anywhere in the campaign, and (b) builds the query token set from every NPC's name + disposition + lastNotes (`storyMemory.js:209-236`), so overlap is against a roster-wide soup instead of the scene. Reproduced: talking to Celeste in the parlour, her floorboard-letter card scores 26.0 and a smuggler-two-towns-away card 25.0; with an empty roster the smuggler card drops to 8.0 — 17 of its 25 points came from the roster, not the scene. The "intentional callback" curation the north star describes is, in practice, salience + type constants plus roster noise. The presence machinery the morning fix built (`buildPresenceText` + `findSubjectsInText`) is exactly the scene-present NPC set this needs.
  - **P2 (design, read-only) — wall-clock windows.** `CALLBACK_COOLDOWN_MS` (8 minutes) and the `ageHours` recency bonus are the last wall-clock measures in the memory layer — one turn in a slow session, three in a fast one — after the 2026-07-30 sweep moved every ledger to conversational distance.
  - **Test depth:** the resolved revive and absent-NPC curation are unpinned; `scoreStoryMemory`'s NPC branch is only ever tested with a one-NPC roster that IS the scene (`storyMemory.test.js:153,232`).
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) sticky `resolved` on merge (a resolved card re-reported stays resolved — or, if the fiction reopens it, only an explicit `status: 'active'` from the DM's `memory_updates` reopens it) + a KNOWN STORY CARDS list (id/type/subject/status) in the Scribe context so it updates instead of re-minting; (2) pass scene-present NPCs (presence-text hits or `curateNpcsForPrompt`'s location set) and drop roster notes from the query tokens; (3) conversational-distance cooldown/recency; (4) the two pins.

### memory-journal (`engine/worldJournal.js`) — Lap 1
- **Scope examined:** `worldJournal.js` end to end; the cadence runner + live journal embed (`turnOrchestrator.js:79-104`); the mount seed's journal rows (`ChatPanel.jsx:363-368`); `narrativeMessages.js`; `buildJournalContext` consumers; both suites (summarize 309 lines, context 339 lines). The 08-31 P2s verified (alias-tolerant transition ledger, shared classify→dispatch).
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — infrastructure error lines and OOC table talk reach the summarizer.** The batch filter is `!hidden && !deleted` (`:191`); `kind: 'error'` lines ("Error resolving check: Failed to fetch") and the OOC exchange — the player's `OOC:` line AND the DM's at-the-table reply — are rendered into the transcript as `[SYSTEM]`/`[USER]`/`[ASSISTANT]` play (reproduced: all three present in the captured request). This is the PERMANENT tier: the entry feeds SESSION HISTORY every turn, the journal RAG row, and the cadence reflection's front/NPC reasoning. The table-talk contract says the exchange is "kept out of memory"; it is kept out of RAG, the Scribe, and the DM window — and then journaled. The 2026-09-04 chronicler fix built the shared predicate (`collectNarrativeEntries`) for exactly this; the journal never adopted it (engine roll-result system lines are the one thing the summarizer legitimately needs beyond it).
  - **P2 — the cadence counts raw rows.** `SUMMARIZE_EVERY = 10` over `state.messages.length` (`:133-136`) — hidden setups, roll-result users, exchange lines all count. A dice turn burns ~5 raw rows (the 2026-07-30 ledger sweep's own number), so roll-heavy play journals every ~2 turns (reproduced: cadence fired at 10 raw / 6 visible), multiplying entries and RAG rows, and `DORMANCY_JOURNAL_CYCLES` (3 cadences) then ages salience-2 cards out in ~6 turns. The last raw-index window in the memory layer.
  - **P2 — fallback entries are embedded.** After `MAX_BATCH_FAILURES` the honest "(Auto-summary was unavailable for a stretch of N messages…)" entry (`fallback: true`) is added like any summary — and then embedded by the live add (`turnOrchestrator.js:85-97`) and re-seeded on every mount (`ChatPanel.jsx:363-368`); neither checks the flag (grep: zero references outside worldJournal). A content-free apology row competes for retrieval slots forever.
  - **(design note, no queue item)** WORLD FACTS shows the 15 MOST RECENT facts under "canonical — never contradict these" (`promptBuilder.js:915-943`); older canon is RAG-only, and there is no supersede/retract channel for a fact the fiction has overturned — `PLAN.md:78-84` already scopes the reconciliation job (merge groups, flagged contradictions, `supersedes` links). Noting only that with the 15-newest window the DM can be shown two contradicting facts under a "never contradict" header; the PLAN item is the fix.
  - **Test depth:** the batch's error/OOC exclusion, the fallback-entry embed skip, and the raw-vs-narrative cadence are unpinned (`worldJournal.summarize.test.js` covers `hidden` only, `:183,259`).
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) `collectNarrativeEntries` + roll-result lines as the batch source; (2) cadence over narrative-eligible messages; (3) skip `fallback` at both embed sites; (4) pins for all three.

## 2026-09-06 — providers-adapter + vector-memory-rag (Lap 1: correctness & test depth)

`npm test`: 2120 passing / 103 files (green)

Every finding below was **reproduced empirically** against the live modules (Node scratch scripts outside the repo with `fetch` and IndexedDB stubbed; zero repo changes) unless marked read-only.

### vector-memory-rag (`engine/vectorMemory.js` + the seed effect in `ChatPanel.jsx`, retrieval/live-add sites in `turnOrchestrator.js`) — Lap 1: correctness & test depth
- **Scope examined:** `vectorMemory.js` end to end; the seed effect (`ChatPanel.jsx:348-400`), the live-add sites (`turnOrchestrator.js:94,406,524`, `ChatPanel.jsx:525,607`), retrieval (`turnOrchestrator.js:195-211`), the purge hook (`SettingsModal.jsx:182-187`); `vectorMemory.test.js` (812 lines, 44 tests). The 08-30 P2 verified fixed and pinned (word-boundary presence, `CATEGORY_BOOST` hoisted, `clearMemories` ruled test-only).
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — the presence gate judges "who is in the scene" from the PLAYER'S MESSAGE alone, so a conversation goes dormant on its second line.** `retrieveRelevant` builds the presence word set from the query (`:425`), and the orchestrator's query is `originalPlayerMessage + Location + combat enemies` (`turnOrchestrator.js:200-204`) — never the DM's last narration, which is what actually establishes who is present. Reproduced: two rows tagged `[Lady Celeste Jewelglade]` at raw 0.62 — her journal beat AND her own `npc` dossier row — retrieve on "I approach Celeste at the parlour" and vanish on the very next turn, "What do you know about the ledger?" (0.62 − 0.12 < 0.55). Every follow-up line of a dialogue that doesn't repeat the NPC's name — the normal shape of a conversation — pays the penalty on exactly the person the scene is about, the inverse of the 2026-08-28 intent ("the moment the person re-enters the conversation the memory returns at full weight"). Cheap fix inside the design: keep the EMBED query untouched, widen only the presence word set with the last 1–2 visible narrative/user messages (or the roster names `findSubjectsInText` finds in them) — an optional `presenceText` argument, no cosine or cost change.
  - **P2 — first tag wins forever.** The seed's subjects patch fires only when the cached row has NO subjects (`:355`). A journal row about Celeste AND Ketta, tagged on a mount when only Celeste was on the roster, stays `[Celeste]` on every later mount; reproduced: a later seed tagging both leaves the row invisible to "I ask Ketta about the argument" (0 rows, expected 1). Compare and replace when the seed's list differs — same upsert key, no re-embed.
  - **P2 — durable-overflow churn.** `enforceCampaignCap` evicts by oldest timestamp inside the durable class once durable rows alone exceed 1,500, and the seed re-embeds whatever is missing with a FRESH timestamp, so each mount evicts a different slice. Reproduced with 1,520 world facts: 20 batch-embeds on EVERY mount, and the missing window rotates (#0–19 after mount 1, #20–39 after mount 2). Nothing is destroyed, but every Continue pays the overflow in embeds and silently drops a rotating window of canon from retrieval. Cap transient rows only (the design's own stated evictables) or log the overflow once. Untested.
  - **P2 — leaked IndexedDB connection on a failed write.** `persistEmbedding` attaches only `tx.oncomplete` (`:58`), so a put that errors (quota) never closes the connection — reproduced: `close()` count unchanged after a failed put; `loadPersistedEmbeddings`' `request.onerror` path rejects without closing (`:110`); `openEmbedDB` registers no `onversionchange` (persistence.js's `withDb` does both). The 2026-07-12 persistence class, one store over.
  - **Test depth:** none of the four shapes is pinned. Also unpinned: `seedMemories` with a NULL sessionId + items — a campaign without `session.id` embeds its whole corpus on EVERY mount and never caches (the id is minted only at `CharacterCreation.jsx:203`, never healed on load); retrieval during an in-flight cold seed (the first turn after Continue on an uncached campaign runs against a partial store, silently); and `deletePersistedEmbeddings`' onabort path. (Checked and NOT a bug: a live `addMemory` during the seed's cache-load window survives — the wholesale `memoryStore = persisted` replace at `:337` lost nothing in the reproduction.)
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) `presenceText` from the last narrative turn(s) + the mid-conversation pin; (2) seed-wins subjects patch; (3) transient-only cap or an overflow log, with a durable-overflow test; (4) onabort/onerror close + `onversionchange`; (5) null-session and cold-seed pins.

### providers-adapter (`llm/adapter.js`, `providers/gemini.js`, `providers/openaiCompatible.js` + `openai.js`/`xai.js`, `providers/sse.js`, `llm/machinery.js`) — Lap 1: correctness & test depth
- **Scope examined:** all seven files end to end; the stream consumer (`turnOrchestrator.js:240-377`); `adapter.test.js` (23 tests) and the gemini/openai/xai suites (35 tests). The 08-30 P2 verified fixed: `sse.js` is the one SSE reader, and the 2026-09-03 in-band `{error}` fix landed there once, exactly as the factory's header promised.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — an OpenAI refusal on the stream commits a BLANK DM turn with no error.** OpenAI (and any OpenAI-compatible reasoning model) returns refusals as `message.refusal` / `delta.refusal` with `content: null` and `finish_reason: 'stop'`; the factory reads only `delta.content` (`openaiCompatible.js:123`), so the stream RESOLVES to `""` (reproduced) — `assertStreamComplete` passes on `stop`, `parseResponse('')` yields an empty narrative, and `turnOrchestrator.js:371-375` dispatches an empty assistant message (only the combat-intent mode is guarded): a blank bubble, a blank row in the save and in the DM's 20-message window, no system line, and the refusal text is never shown. The non-streaming lane throws the generic "No response generated" instead of the refusal (reproduced). Surface `refusal` as the thrown message on both lanes — under the 2026-08-28 refusal-cascade lens a VISIBLE refusal is what DELETE_MESSAGE exists to scrub — and never commit an empty non-intent narrative in the orchestrator.
  - **P1 — a Gemini PROMPT-level block is reported as a dropped connection.** When Gemini blocks the input it answers `{ promptFeedback: { blockReason: 'PROHIBITED_CONTENT' } }` with no candidates — the one classifier `BLOCK_NONE` cannot switch off, i.e. the residual refusal class after 2026-08-28. Non-streaming: "No response generated. The model may have been blocked…" (the cause is in the payload, unread); streaming: "The connection dropped mid-response … Please retry" (reproduced both). Retrying a deterministic block loops; the player needs "blocked: PROHIBITED_CONTENT — edit or remove the offending message". Read `promptFeedback.blockReason` in both lanes; candidate-level `finishReason` blocks are already named (reproduced `stopped early (PROHIBITED_CONTENT)`).
  - **P2 — 429 backoff ignores `Retry-After`.** `makeHttpError` keeps only `.status` (reproduced: no `retryAfter` on the error), and the adapter retries at ~1 s / ~2 s, so a per-minute quota 429 (the Gemini free-tier shape) burns all three attempts in ~3 s and the Scribe/journal extraction is lost. Parse the header (cap ~10 s) into the delay.
  - **P2 — the factory's 16,384 output cap is the "gpt-4o family ceiling"** (`openaiCompatible.js:11-16`), while every recommended OpenAI catalog model is a gpt-5.6 reasoning model whose reasoning tokens count against `max_completion_tokens` — the exact reason `gemini.js:34` raised its cap to 32,768. A heavy-reasoning long turn hits `length` → truncation error → a retry at the same cap. Read-only; raise per provider or model.
  - **P2 — `readSseStream` drops a spec-valid `data:` (no space) line and never flushes a final unterminated line**, both ending as "connection dropped" (reproduced; CRLF is fine). Low today (OpenAI/Gemini/xAI all emit `data: ` + `\n\n`), but a proxy in the path is a plausible player setup.
  - **P2 (polish, re-flagged — the 08-30 note was never queued):** the PROVIDERS catalog still says "Gemini 3.1 Pro (Latest!)" / "released Feb 2026" (`adapter.js:127`); and a doc drift: CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md line 139 still name the machinery model `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` while `machinery.js:19` has run `gemini-3.7-flash` since 2026-08-22 (STATUS.md has it right).
  - **Test depth:** `sse.js` has no direct suite — `makeStreamError` stamps no `.status` for Gemini's string `status` (`RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` without a numeric code) or OpenAI's string `code` (reproduced, informational since streams never retry); `makeHttpError`'s object-without-message fallthrough, the `data:` variants, and the promptFeedback/refusal shapes are all unpinned; `formatMessages` maps a `system` history role to `model` and passes `content: null` through as `text: null` (reproduced; a 400 at Gemini) — unreachable via `buildMessageWindow` today, unpinned.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) refusal surfacing on both factory lanes + an "empty stream never commits a blank turn" guard in the orchestrator; (2) `promptFeedback.blockReason` on both Gemini lanes with a non-retry remedy; (3) `Retry-After`; (4) per-provider output cap; (5) an `sse.test.js` for the reader and error helpers; (6) catalog copy + the CLAUDE/AGENTS machinery-model line.

## 2026-09-05 — response-parsing + enemy-stats-conditions (Lap 1: correctness & test depth)

`npm test`: 2085 passing / 102 files (green)

Every finding below was **reproduced empirically** against the live modules/reducer (Node scratch scripts outside the repo; zero repo changes) unless marked read-only.

### response-parsing (`llm/responseParser.js`, `llm/utils/jsonExtractor.js`, `llm/eventChannels.js`) — Lap 1: correctness & test depth
- **Scope examined:** all three files end to end; the parse consumer in `turnOrchestrator.js:276-377`; `sanitizeProposalRoll` (`engine/roleplayCheck.js:16-41`, the save-side twin); the three suites (`responseParser.test.js` 1209 lines, `jsonExtractor.test.js`, `eventChannels.test.js`). All four 2026-08-29 findings verified fixed in code and pinned.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — an irreparable fenced block leaks its raw JSON into the story.** `parseResponse` computes the pre-fence narrative (`:175`) but the repair-failure return (`:191`) hands back the FULL response — fence, broken JSON and all — and an empty `` ```json``` `` fence does the same (both reproduced). `turnOrchestrator.js:372-375` commits that as the assistant message: rendered in chat as a code block, stored in the save, riding the DM's 20-message window as a model-authored malformed block (the self-priming class DELETE_MESSAGE was built for, 2026-08-28), and reaching the journal summarizer and RAG embeds — the exact narrative→journal→RAG path the 2026-08-05 unfenced leak was rated P1 for. The "events could not be read" system line already tells the player everything the raw block would. NOTE: `responseParser.test.js:618-625` pins today's behavior with a comment stating it, so this is a ruling, not just a bug: return the already-computed pre-fence narrative and flip the pin.
  - **P2 — prose after the fence vanishes silently.** Narrative is everything BEFORE the first fence (`:174-175`): a block followed by more prose drops the tail, and a JSON-first response commits an EMPTY assistant message (both reproduced). FORMAT_REMINDER demands the block last, so this is DM disobedience — but the same function warns on a second fence for exactly that reason; append non-empty trailing text to the narrative, or at least warn.
  - **P2 — fence recognition is case-sensitive and tag-required.** `` ```JSON `` and a bare `` ``` `` fence fall to the unfenced-anchor path, which parses the events fine but leaves the dangling fence opener on the narrative (`"The door opens.\n```JSON"`, reproduced — an unclosed code fence in the rendered message). `/```json/` at `:132` vs the `/i` second-fence check at `:168` in the same function.
  - **P2 — the anchor search matches a wire key in PROSE first.** `extractBalancedJson` anchors on `text.indexOf(keyword)` (`jsonExtractor.js:73`), so a narrative that mentions a key before an unfenced block ("I'll log this under quest_updates…") finds the prose occurrence, walks back to no enclosing brace, returns null, and when no other anchor exists the whole response ships as narrative with the raw JSON attached (reproduced). Anchor on the QUOTED key (`"quest_updates"`) — JSON keys are always quoted, prose isn't — or take the last occurrence.
  - **P2 — `requested_rolls.dc` is the one numeric field with neither clamp nor string coercion.** `normalizeRequestedRoll` keeps any number (`eventChannels.js:119`): `dc: -40` → auto-success, `dc: 1e9` → auto-fail, and a string `"15"` — the quirk `clamp()` in the same file coerces for coins/XP (`:30-40`) — silently becomes DC 10 (all reproduced). `sanitizeProposalRoll` clamps 0..MAX on the SAVE boundary and the combat check slot clamps 5..30; the live parser lane is the only one that doesn't. Same shape one field over: `type`/`description`/`attacker`/`target`/`notation`/`damage` pass objects through via `|| null` (`:111,120,128,132-135`), and `description` is rendered as a React child (`ChatPanel.jsx:915`) — the 2026-07-23 skill/ability guard stopped one field short.
  - **Test depth:** none of the five reproduced shapes is pinned. Also unpinned: `UNFENCED_EVENT_ANCHORS` excluding plain-word wires, `normalizeSpellCasts`' bare-string entry, `validateCombatStart`'s `is_undead`/`isBoss` aliases. Otherwise the parser suite remains the repo's best fixture library.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) pre-fence narrative on repair failure + flip the pin; (2) trailing-prose append + JSON-first case; (3) `/i` + optional tag on the fence regex, and strip a dangling opener in the anchor path; (4) quoted-key anchoring in `extractBalancedJson`; (5) coerce+clamp dc and string-guard the six pass-through fields, pinned with the reproduced cases.

### enemy-stats-conditions (`engine/enemyStats.js`, `enemy_condition_updates`, `CONDITION_EFFECTS` — plus the hero-side `conditions_gained/removed` twin) — Lap 1: correctness & test depth
- **Scope examined:** `enemyStats.js` end to end + its 19-case suite; `validateCombatStart` (`eventChannels.js:60-107`); `normalizeCombatEnemy`/`START_COMBAT`/`UPDATE_ENEMY` (`handlers/combat.js`); the condition flow through `combatExchange.js` (delta normalize `:86-95`, apply `:307-320`, exchange `:1490-1493`, opening `:1652-1655`, enemy phase `:1349-1360`, save lane `:749-783`); the hero twin `ADD_CONDITION`/`REMOVE_CONDITION` (`handlers/character.js:306-321`), `withCondition` (`shared.js:55-59`), `reviveCharacter` (`shared.js:108`), `TAKE_REST` (`resources.js:314-318`), `healCharacterCoreFields`; every `CONDITION_EFFECTS` consumer. Both 2026-08-29 items verified fixed and pinned (opening-lane sync at `combatExchange.test.js:853`; initiative pipeline gone; one `canonicalEnemyId`; whitelist projections in `normalizeCombatEnemy` and `sanitizeStoredExchangeResult`).
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — the HERO's condition channel is the enemy channel's unhardened twin.** Enemies get `normalizeEnemyConditions` at every boundary (lowercase, trim, supported-set, dedupe). The hero's `conditions_gained`/`conditions_removed` get only `guardedList` — which KEEPS plain objects and strings of any length (`eventChannels.js:325-326`) — and `ADD_CONDITION`/`REMOVE_CONDITION` store and match VERBATIM. Reproduced against the live reducer: (a) `conditions_gained: ["Poisoned"]` then `conditions_removed: ["poisoned"]` leaves the hero Poisoned — disadvantage on every attack and check until the DM happens to repeat the exact casing; the prompt itself shows BOTH spellings (`"Poisoned"` in the channel doc at `promptBuilder.js:589`, `poisoned` in the combat rules at `:524`), so drift is the norm, and the long-rest filter already lowercases (`resources.js:317`) because someone on that path expected it; (b) `["poisoned"," Poisoned","POISONED"]` stack as three more rows; (c) an object element persists into `character.conditions` and then EVERY heal path throws — `reviveCharacter`'s `c.toLowerCase()` (`shared.js:108`) sits under TAKE_REST short AND long, potions, spell heals and the exchange commit — while the sheet's `<span>{c}</span>` crashes the render; (d) `LOAD_GAME` never heals `character.conditions` (`healCharacterCoreFields` skips it), so a poisoned save re-crashes on every reload. `withCondition` is already case-insensitive — the DM channel simply doesn't use it. Fix: normalize at the boundary (strings only, trim, lowercase, ≤40 chars, cap) + case-insensitive add/remove + a load heal — `normalizeEnemyConditions` minus the supported-set filter, shared.
  - **P2 — restrained's save disadvantage never reaches an enemy.** `CONDITION_EFFECTS.restrained.save` is defined (`rules.js:314`) and the hero's saves consult it (`combatExchange.js:1069`), but the save-spell lane rolls `rollD20(saveBonus)` flat (`:757`) — a restrained foe saves against Sacred Flame / Burning Hands at full strength. The 2026-07-13 stunned-ogre half-implementation class, one lane over. (Read-only finding; the kernel is explicit.)
  - **P2 — string-typed enemy stats silently default.** `"hp": "22"`, `"ac": "15"`, `"attack_bonus": "+4"`, `"save_bonus": "3"` → HP 20, AC 12, attack +3, save default (reproduced through `validateCombatStart`). `clamp()` in the same file coerces exactly this quirk for coins/XP by ruling ("LLMs regularly emit numeric fields as strings"); the enemy boundary predates it. A leading-number parse BEFORE the reject/clamp policy keeps the offensive-reject rule intact (`"+99"` still rejects) while `+4` written the way every 5e statblock writes it lands.
  - **Test depth:** `canonicalEnemyId` — made "ONE implementation" 08-29 — has no direct test (collision suffix `-2`, `enemy-` idempotency, junk-only name → index fallback, 80-char slice); `normalizeEnemyConditions`' "caps the list at 10" case (`enemyStats.test.js:141`) asserts a cap the code explicitly says does not exist (`:58-59`) — a misleading pin; reducer-level `ADD_CONDITION`/`REMOVE_CONDITION` have zero tests (only dispatch-level in the parser suite); `sanitizeStoredExchangeResult`'s junk-key drop is unpinned (`gameReducer.load.test.js:442-460` covers conditions only).
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) one shared creature-condition normalizer at the parser boundary, the two handlers, and the load heal, pinned with the case-drift, stacking, object-crash and reload cases; (2) `getConditionRollEffects(enemy.conditions, 'save')` in the save lane; (3) leading-number coercion ahead of the enemy validators; (4) the four test gaps.

## 2026-09-04 — spellcasting + chronicler (Lap 1: correctness & test depth — second run, user-directed; lens: cross-lane seams)

`npm test`: 2066 passing / 102 files (green)

Every finding below was **reproduced empirically** against the live reducer/modules (Node scratch scripts outside the repo; zero repo changes) unless marked as read-only.

### spellcasting (`state/handlers/spellcasting.js`, `engine/spellcasting.js`, `data/spells.js`) — Lap 1, seams lens
- **Scope examined:** `CAST_SPELL` end to end; `chooseSlotLevel`/`spendSpellSlot`/`buildNotation` (`engine/spellcasting.js:111-185`); the applyEvents spell lane (`applyEvents.js:113-118,354-356`); the combat resolver's support/stabilize lane (`combatExchange.js:836-881`); the replay-ledger core; `validateSaveState`'s ledger heal (`session.js:168-170`); both suites (16 handler cases + engine suite). All four 08-29 findings verified fixed in code and pinned.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 — an unconscious caster acts.** `CAST_SPELL` validates the spell, the slot, the recipients, and the dead-hero heal target — never the CASTER's own state. Reproduced: a cleric at 0 HP, `dying: true`, 2/3 death-save failures, Unconscious, self-casts Cure Wounds out of combat → 11 HP, `dying: false`, slot spent, death-save clock erased; Shield of Faith likewise sustains on a dying caster (AC 13, still dying). The combat lane cannot do this — a dying hero's exchange slot is `death_save` only, the engine-owned 09-02 seam — and the STATUS: DYING prompt line prescribes the out-of-combat death-save lane, but a DM narrating a "gasped prayer" and emitting `spell_cast` (a classic LLM move) is accepted whole. Same shape as the 08-30 progression P1 (level-up heal bypassing revival cleanup): an engine channel with no state gate. Fix: reject any cast while `dying`/`currentHP <= 0`/incapacitated (`getIncapacitatingCondition` — the 07-13 enemy pattern) with a visible line; companion-administered potions remain the out-of-combat rescue.
  - **P2 — the recast bypass is too loose.** A nearby same-spell re-emission spends a second slot only when the player's message "casts it again". Two reproduced false positives, each a second slot inside the 4-message window: `repeatIntentNearNoun(text, /(?:cast|casting|spell|it|that)/)` fires on "I try that again, the lock is stubborn" (trailing-`again` form on a bare pronoun), and the `nameWords.every(word => text.includes(word))` rung fires on "These wounds will not cure themselves; I bind them with cloth". The purchase ledger's 2026-08-22 quantifier-attaches-to-noun tightening never reached this ledger's pronoun set, and the name-words rung has no order or adjacency requirement.
  - **P2 (design, ruling needed) — Spare the Dying is inert on every lane.** Out of combat the `stabilizes` branch prints "is stabilized if dying" and changes nothing (`:215-216`); in combat it is likewise a note (`combatExchange.js:874-880`). Structurally so: the hero is the only creature with a dying clock and cannot cast while dying (once the P1 gate lands), and companions have no clock by design ("down but stable"). Either label it flavor in the catalog summary + caster prompt block, or cut it — the spec's own Death Ward scope-pressure precedent.
  - **Test depth:** the handler suite never reaches the cleanse-on-COMPANION branch (`:178-183`), the stabilize branch, the utility default branch (`:218` — Knock / Detect Magic / Guidance), the all-invalid-recipient rejection (`:126-128`), the "share of the spell is lost" line (`:172-174`), or a DM-requested `slotLevel` upcast at the handler level (`:88`). That set IS the snapshot's 85.60. Ledgers are clean: `findExactSourceReplay`/`findNearbyReplay`/`rememberLedgerEntry` all type-filter entries and the load heal keeps only strings.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) the caster-state gate + a dying-caster regression test; (2) tighten the recast rungs (ordered spell-name phrase; `it`/`that` only beside `cast`/`casting`); (3) the six unpinned branches; (4) the Spare-the-Dying ruling.

### chronicler (`llm/chronicler.js`, chronicle reducer paths, Journal Chronicle tab) — Lap 1, seams lens
- **Scope examined:** `writeChronicleChapters` end to end (chunking, part titling, salvage, clean-run `toIndex` claim); `collectNarrativeEntries` (the shared 09-01 predicate); `appendChronicleChapter`/`ADD_CHRONICLE_CHAPTER`/`REMOVE_CHRONICLE_CHAPTER`; `validateSaveState` (`session.js:76-190`); JournalPanel write/remove flow incl. the mid-write Remove guard (`disabled={writing}` — closed); `chronicler.test.js` (15 cases). Both 08-29 findings verified fixed and pinned.
  - **P2 — `chronicle` is the one persisted collection `validateSaveState` never shape-guards.** messages/quests/journal/party/rollHistory/npcs/worldFacts/storyMemory/fronts/locations/every ledger get an entry heal; `chronicle` rides the raw `...payload` spread. Both readers index its last element unguarded — `ChronicleTab` (`JournalPanel.jsx:327`) and `writeChronicleChapters` (`chronicler.js:90`) — so a null/non-object last entry or a non-array `chronicle` crashes the whole Journal panel on open (ErrorBoundary; reload re-crashes — the 07-25 QuestPanel class), and a string `toIndex` ("12") string-concatenates into `fromIndex` "121" (reproduced): every close says "Not enough new play" until that chapter is removed. `appendChronicleChapter` coerces on WRITE only (`Number.isFinite`), so the load side is the gap. Hostile-save class (cloud saves are hand-editable), consistent with the 07-25/07-29 items.
  - **P2 — infrastructure error lines are retold as fiction.** `collectNarrativeEntries` admits every visible system message (`narrativeMessages.js:32`) and `renderTranscript` labels all of them TABLE RECORD (`chronicler.js:68-75`), which the prompt defines as dice/coin/rest/combat results to "transmute into fiction — the blow lands or misses". But the transcript also carries "The DM's mechanical events could not be read this turn (malformed data)…" (`turnOrchestrator.js:285`), "Error resolving check: Failed to fetch" (`:594`), "…the DM's outcome response failed…" (`:592`), "Error challenging check…" (`:652`), and ChatPanel's `Error: …` lines — none are play, and the prompt tells the model to fictionalize them. Same class as the 08-29 table-talk leak, same fix shape: stamp those dispatches (`kind: 'error'`) and skip them in the shared predicate — SceneArt's situation picker and sessionPriming get cleaned for free. (Read-only finding; the chronicler is not runnable offline.)
  - Clean otherwise: the salvage path, multi-part split with contiguous spans, the clean-run raw-`toIndex` claim, the table-talk filter, and the newest-only remove are all verified in code and pinned by tests; a mid-write Remove cannot punch a hole (button disabled while writing).
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) chronicle entry heal in `validateSaveState` + a poisoned-save Journal-open test; (2) error-line stamping + predicate skip, pinned in `narrativeMessages` tests.

## 2026-09-04 — rules-math + quests (Lap 1: correctness & test depth)

`npm test`: 2066 passing / 102 files (green)

Every finding below was **reproduced empirically** against the live modules (Node scratch scripts outside the repo; zero repo changes) except where marked module-level.

### rules-math (`engine/rules.js`) — Lap 1: correctness & test depth
- **Scope examined:** `rules.js` end to end; the `normalizeItem` clamp boundary (`data/items.js:264-301`), the load-path heal (`migrations.js:205,392-401`), `rules.test.js` (382 lines, 22 describes).
- **Findings:**
  - **P2:** the 2026-08-28 Number()-coercion sweep stopped at armor. `getWeaponAttackBonus` (`:179`) and `getWeaponDamageNotation` (`:186`) still read `weapon?.attackBonus || …` bare — reproduced module-level: a junk string `attackBonus` yields a **NaN to-hit** (every attack silently misses), a junk `damageBonus` yields `"1d8NaN"` → parseNotation throw → the flat modifier-less 1d4 fallback the 08-28 fix was written to kill. And every clamp is ceilings-only: `attackBonus: -20` → −15, `baseAC: -50` → AC −48. Reachability is the honest caveat — see the correction below: `normalizeItem` guards BOTH boundaries today, so these read-site guards are belt-only. Coerce + floor for symmetry with `getArmorClass`, and fix the stale comment.
  - **P2 (documentation drift, load-bearing):** `rules.js:39` justifies the AC re-clamp with "LOAD_GAME does not re-normalize inventory" — false today: `healEquippedSlots` (UNCONDITIONAL_HEALS) maps `normalizeItem` over the whole inventory on EVERY load (`migrations.js:205`), which deletes string `baseAC`, floors negative bonuses at 0, and clamps ceilings at +3. The 08-28 entry's reachability claim inherited the same wrong premise. Worth recording: **the load path IS a normalizeItem boundary** — future stale-save findings should assume it.
  - **P2 (test depth):** `getAllSkills` has zero tests and still re-implements `getSkillModifier` inline (`:256-273` vs `:240-251`; the 08-28 Lap 4 fold was never queued) — a drift desyncs the sheet's skill list from the modifiers actual rolls use, undetected. `getWeaponAbilityModifier`'s thrown-weapon branch (`:125`, thrown ranged → STR — verified correct empirically) and the junk-`damageBonus` path are also unpinned.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) Number()-coerce + floor the weapon-bonus reads and correct the `:39` comment in the same commit; (2) fold `getAllSkills` onto `getSkillModifier` and pin it; (3) thrown-weapon + junk-damageBonus tests.

### quests (`state/handlers/quests.js`, applyEvents routing, `normalizeQuestUpdate`, QuestPanel round-trip) — Lap 1: correctness & test depth
- **Scope examined:** `handlers/quests.js` (whole file), applyEvents quest loop + exp suppression (`applyEvents.js:328-377`), `normalizeQuestUpdate`/aliases/`guardedList` (`eventChannels.js:161-197,329`), `QuestPanel.jsx` (whole file), `gameReducer.quests.test.js` (30 cases).
- **Findings:**
  - **P1:** the panel's ✓ button is an unbounded self-service XP mine. `handleComplete` dispatches `COMPLETE_QUEST` with the row id, and the handler pays engine XP for ANY completion — including quests the player added through the panel's own + button. Reproduced against the real reducer: add a note quest → one turn passes → ✓ = **+225 XP (the full 12.5% tier) at L3**, 8 click-cycles per level at any level; even add+✓ in the same turn pays the 25-XP instant tier per double-click with no waiting. Every anti-farming lever in the handler (same-turn gate, one-shot terminal guard, the `openedAtMessage` pre-age clamp) guards the DM channel; the panel walks in the front door. It is self-cheating in a solo game, but the project treats XP integrity as an invariant (vault import clamps, "XP is engine-owned", the 2026-08-26 ruling's anti-farming levers). Clean fix sparing DM flows: bare-string refs — the panel/stale-id path; applyEvents always sends object refs — complete as **bookkeeping only, no XP**.
  - **P2:** `REMOVE_QUEST` on a finished row deletes the one-shot XP replay guard. The handler's own doc names the terminal row as the guard against DM re-emission — so panel housekeeping (✕ on a completed quest) followed by the DM re-emitting that completion later (the proven recurring failure mode the ledger rule exists for) resurrects the row via the never-tracked insert and pays the 25-XP instant tier again (reproduced). Cheapest fix: never-tracked terminal inserts pay 0 — that path exists to record table history (playtest #14 was about the record, not the XP). The instant tier there was part of the 2026-08-26 ruling, so flag it for an explicit revisit rather than silently reversing.
  - **P2:** the panel's add-quest input has no length clamp on any layer — the parser clamps DM names to 160 chars, but `handleAddQuest` dispatches raw input, `ADD_QUEST` stores it verbatim, and the prompt's ACTIVE QUESTS block clamps descriptions (250) but not names — a pasted multi-KB name persists into the save and rides the system prompt every turn.
  - **Test depth:** the handler suite is exemplary (100% coverage, 30 cases, every prior queue item pinned) — but all three findings above live at the panel seam, and QuestPanel has no test file; neither reproduced behavior is pinned anywhere. The parser/applyEvents boundary is solid (guardedList cap 8, status aliases, identity guards all verified in place).
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) XP-free bare-string completion + a panel-farm regression test; (2) the never-tracked-insert XP revisit; (3) input maxLength + handler clamp.

## 2026-09-03 — character-vault + inventory-economy (Lap 1: correctness & test depth)

`npm test`: 2025 passing / 101 files.

Rotation excluded (last 6, local ∪ origin — origin == HEAD): combat-exchange, cloud-sync, roll-resolution, persistence (09-02), hidden-fronts, scribe (09-01 r2), dice-engine, scene-art (09-01), living-world, chat-orchestration (08-31 ×2). Snapshot was 7 days old — refreshed. Every finding below was **reproduced empirically** against the live modules (scratch script outside the repo, Node type-stripping; zero repo changes).

### character-vault (`engine/characterVault.js`, `engine/characterUtils.js`, roster flows in `CharacterCreation.jsx` / `CharacterSheet.jsx`, the `persistence.js` roster store, `START_CHARACTER`) — Lap 1: correctness & test depth
- **Scope examined:** `characterVault.js` end to end (clamps, the fixed-average-HP boundary, expertise gate, portrait allowlist, inventory sanitizer, parser); `characterUtils.js` (`buildDerivedCharacterFields`, `createCharacter`, the ASI/style/archetype normalizers); begin-from-roster, import, export, delete flows; `saveRosterCharacter`/`listRosterCharacters`/`deleteRosterCharacter`; `START_CHARACTER`; `normalizeItem` as the inventory sanitizer's core; `characterVault.test.js` (31) + the roster cases in `persistence.test.js`.
- **Verified fixed since 08-28:** both queue items — casters get authoritative `spellSlots` through the shared `buildDerivedCharacterFields` core (the builder fold), pinned by the 08-28 P0 test. Verified sound: the post-decision maxHP recompute, the exp clamp against the per-level threshold (level 20 included), class-gated expertise, the portrait allowlist + ceiling, roster-id retention on begin-from-roster, `START_CHARACTER`'s AC recompute.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 (weapon damage is unbounded across both trust boundaries):** `normalizeItem` clamps magicBonus, attack/damage bonus, acBonus, baseAC, shieldAC, valueCp and quantity — but never `damage` on a non-catalog weapon, and `sanitizeInventory` inherits it. Reproduced: `{ name: 'Doom Blade', type: 'weapon', damage: '99d12' }` imports with the notation intact, equips, and `getWeaponDamageNotation` emits `"99d12+3"`; the only ceiling left is `MAX_DICE_COUNT` (100) in dice.ts, ≈643 average damage per hit. The DM's `items_found` weapon takes the identical path. The file's own header promise ("engine owns the math") stops one field short — `data/items.js:208-283`, `characterVault.js:193-208`.
  - **P2 (the roster resurrects the dead — ruling needed):** Save to Roster / Export File are not gated on `isDead`, and `sanitizeCharacter` rebuilds `currentHP: maxHP` while dropping `isDead`/`deathSaves` (reproduced: a three-failure corpse comes back 12/12 with no flag). DECISIONS' "resurrection is cut permanently" governs HEALS; whether the roster is the sanctioned afterlife (a hero is a template, campaigns own deaths) or a bypass is undecided. Not proposing a reversal — asking for the ruling, then either a gate or a sentence in DECISIONS — `CharacterSheet.jsx:96-118, 558-572`, `characterVault.js:158-159`.
  - **P2 (skill count uncapped):** skills are filtered to KNOWN names but never to the class allowance — an 18-skill fighter imports intact (reproduced); rogue expertise is likewise uncounted. Clamp to racial + the class pick count (first N kept) — `characterVault.js:135-145`.
  - **P2 (roster flows fail quiet — the 09-02 boot-screen class):** `listRosterCharacters().catch(() => setRoster([]))` renders a blocked/failed IndexedDB as "0 in roster"; `handleSaveToRoster` swallows a rejected save to `console.warn` with no toast (the player believes the hero was saved); `handleDeleteHero` has no catch at all — `CharacterCreation.jsx:71, 286-291`, `CharacterSheet.jsx:111-113`.
  - **P2 (test depth):** no test covers begin-from-roster id retention, the import → roster → begin round trip, or delete; `sanitizeInventory`'s 200-item slice and string entries, `exp` at MAX level, and junk `portraitUpdatedAt` are unpinned (fightingStyle/archetype and notes/portraitPrompt ARE covered).
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) parse and bound non-catalog weapon `damage` in `normalizeItem` where magicBonus is clamped (count ≤2, sides ≤12 — the best catalog die — else fall back to 1d6), with vault AND DM-path tests; (2) a DECISIONS ruling on dead heroes in the roster; (3) allowance clamps for skills/expertise; (4) `rosterError` on a failed list, a toast on a failed save, a catch on delete.

### inventory-economy (`data/items.js`, `engine/equipment.js`, `engine/currency.js`, `engine/companionGear.js`, `handlers/inventory.js`, `handlers/economy.js`, the ref/ledger helpers in `handlers/shared.js`, applyEvents item routing) — Lap 1: correctness & test depth
- **Scope examined:** `items.js` (catalog, `normalizeItemKey`, `parseCountedItemName`, `normalizeItem`); `equipment.js`; `currency.js`; `companionGear.js` + `GIVE_GEAR_TO_COMPANION`; `handlers/inventory.js` and `handlers/economy.js` end to end; `findInventoryItemByRef`, `mintOwnedItem`, `consumeItem`, the ledger helpers; the items_found aggregation, items_lost dispatch and starting_items reconciliation in `applyEvents.js`; `items.test.js` (13), `equipment.test.js` (4), `currency.test.js` (24), `companionGear.test.js` (10), `gameReducer.inventory.test.js` (45), `gameReducer.economy.test.js` (91), the gear-gift cases in `gameReducer.companions.test.js`.
- **Verified fixed since 08-28:** all three queue items — unpayable charges are not ledgered and a partial audit ledgers the deducted value (`economy.js:550-560, 733-741`), `REMOVE_ITEM_BY_NAME` and `SELL_ITEM` ride `findInventoryItemByRef` plus the unambiguous fuzzy tier, all pinned. Verified sound against the 2026-09-03 money-traffic playtest's clean purse: covers, strips, direction echoes, receipts.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 (`items_lost` takes the whole stack):** `isLootEntry` admits `{ name, quantity }` objects, applyEvents forwards only the name (`applyEvents.js:261-265`), and `REMOVE_ITEM_BY_NAME` filters the row out (`inventory.js:336`). Reproduced: "Torch" against a 5-stack → empty pack. The ECONOMY prompt tells the DM to emit items_lost when "an owned item is consumed, destroyed, or leaves their possession" — one torch burned, one ration eaten, one javelin thrown loses all of them; the Scribe loss audit dispatches the same action.
  - **P1 (genitive loot becomes catalog gear):** the descriptor-suffix rule (`items.js:132`) accepts ANY prefix that ends in a space. Reproduced: "Scroll of Shield" → catalog Shield (type shield, auto-equipped into an empty slot for +2 AC, the original name gone), "Ring of the Dagger" → a Dagger. Every path shares it — items_found, purchase, premise starting_items, vault import — so a story object named "X of <catalog word>" is silently rewritten into mechanics. Reject prefixes containing a preposition (of/for/with/from) or require ≤2 adjective tokens.
  - **P2 (inventory never stacks):** `ADD_ITEM` and `PURCHASE_ITEM` append unconditionally (`inventory.js:148`, `economy.js:812`). Reproduced: buy 2 → buy 3 → find 1 = three "Torch" rows, and `items_lost "torches"` then removes only the first row. `healShadowInventoryRows` merges keyless shadows on load but never same-key rows. Three rows in the panel, three lines in the prompt's INVENTORY block, and USE_ITEM decrements whichever row was clicked.
  - **P2 (SELL_ITEM fractional/string quantity):** `Math.max(1, Math.min(item.quantity, payload.quantity))` never truncates (`economy.js:833`). Reproduced: selling 1.5 of 4 rations leaves "Rations (1 day) ×2.5" and pays 1.5×. `buildPurchaseTransaction` truncs; mirror it.
  - **P2 (a loss-covered purchase double-represents one spend):** the lossCover path ledgers the purchase as `applied` at full price although no coin moved in that action (`economy.js:774-788`) — against 08-28's own rule that the spend ledgers record only coin that MOVED. `spendLedgerView` then holds the payment twice and `stripBundledReplay` strips both. Reproduced: pay 5 gp loose, covered purchase, then a genuine 10 gp room charge two messages later is refused entirely ("repeats payments already taken"). Player-favorable direction (the documented asymmetry), wrong magnitude. Record it `ignored` — `findRecentTransactionDuplicate` is status-blind, so the purchase replay guard survives — or with priceCp 0.

### combat-exchange (`engine/combatExchange.js`, `engine/combatMath.js`, `state/handlers/combat.js`, the death/defeat seam) — Lap 1: correctness & test depth
- **Scope examined:** `combatExchange.js` end to end (normalizer, reconciliation, `validatePlayerSlots`, every resolver, `terminalState`, both planners, the narration prompt); `combatMath.js` kernel (`resolveAttackRoll`, `applyUncannyDodge`); all nine handlers in `handlers/combat.js`; the ChatPanel commit/opening/queued/narration effects; the death seam across `TAKE_DAMAGE`, `DEATH_SAVE_RESULT`, `PLAYER_DEFEAT`, `isLowLevelSolo`, and `applyEvents`' `player_death` branch; `combatExchange.test.js` (24 describes) + `gameReducer.combat.test.js` (9).
- **Verified fixed since 08-27:** all five queue items — `bonusActionUsed` rides the payload and locks the potion, the opening planner's null-character guard, REJECT's phase guard, `isEnemyActive` before `on_success`, and `resolveAttackRoll` as the one hit pipeline. Verified sound under adversarial reading: defend-stance timing (enemy defend protects the NEXT exchange, companion defend the SAME one — both pinned), guard interception re-checked per attack, standing-flank lifecycle, the shared Uncanny Dodge state across the opening, `APPLY_COMBAT_EXCHANGE`'s replay guard + phase/kind cross-check, the message ordering (roll lines before the falls/defeat status lines), END_COMBAT's slain-only XP on a loss.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 (death-save-time solo divergence soft-locks the fight):** the 2026-07-17 "one semantic" fix unified `isLowLevelSolo` at TAKE_DAMAGE time; the death-SAVE transition was left split. `terminalState` (`combatExchange.js:1379-1391`) re-checks `lowLevelSolo` only when the hero is not yet dying; on the dying branch it projects the die and returns `'dying'`/`'defeat'` from the tally alone. The reducer's `DEATH_SAVE_RESULT` (`character.js:214-226`) checks `isLowLevelSolo(character, party)` LIVE and converts the save into early defeat. So: L1-2 hero + companion; hero drops (dying, companion standing); companion drops in a later exchange; next exchange's `death_save` → the payload says `terminal: 'dying'`, the reducer flips the hero to `lowLevelDefeat: true, dying: false` and posts "Death save skipped", narration is told "remains unconscious and dying", `COMPLETE_COMBAT_NARRATION` hands the turn back, and every subsequent action fails `validatePlayerSlots` ("cannot commit a combat action while defeated or dead", `:576`) → REJECT → "No one acted; try again". Combat never ends on its own — only the manual End Combat button exits. This is the playtest #11 scenario (L1 rogue dying under a standing guardian) with the guardian dropping first — the most dramatic early-game beat the game has.
  - **P1 (`player_death` uses the stale solo predicate):** `applyEvents.js:421` decides "solo" with `(!state.party || state.party.length === 0)` — the fourth consumer of the semantic, still on the pre-07-17 definition. A level ≤2 hero whose only companion is DOWNED is protected by the reducer (and the safety block tells the DM so), but a DM `player_death` takes the else branch and dispatches `UPDATE_CHARACTER { isDead: true }` — the one irreversible outcome in the game. Same branch, noted not queued: a DM `player_death` on a level ≥3 hero at full HP is also permanent; the prompt's "unavoidable narrative deaths only" (`promptBuilder.js:544`) is the only guard on the only channel that can end a campaign. Worth a DECISIONS look (an HP/dying precondition, or a confirm).
  - **P2 (natural-20 revive is a free round):** the planner computes the enemy phase with `playerHp` still 0 (`healedBaseHp` from `currentHP`), so `resolveEnemyAttack` skips the "already-defeated player" (`:1262-1264`) for every foe, and only afterwards the payload sets HP to `max(1, …)` (`:1524`). A hero who rolls a 20 stands up at 1 HP AND cannot be attacked that exchange — in 5e the revived creature is a valid target for everyone after it, and the reducer's own commit order is death save → damage. Player-favoring, rare, but the narration is told "combat is still active" beside foes who inexplicably held their swords.
  - **P2 (design — opening ignores intents):** `planOpeningExchange` resolves every initiative winner with `exchange: null` (`:1599-1611`), i.e. the default `attack → player` / companion auto-attack. The fight-starting response's `enemy_intents` (a companion target, `defend`) and `companion_intents` (`guard`) never apply in the highest-damage slot of the fight; every ambusher beelines the hero, and the guard mechanic structurally cannot protect the opening. The 08-29 fix synced conditions and said "never the intents" — a rule that deserves a DECISIONS line or bounded opening intents.
  - **P2:** in-combat check/save `dc` defaults to 15 (`:138`) while the out-of-combat channel deliberately defaults to 10 with a comment saying never 15.
  - **P2 (test depth):** the death-save test (`combatExchange.test.js:658`) uses a level-3 hero — nothing pins the low-level dying branch with a downed companion; no test rolls a 20 and then an enemy attack in the same exchange; `applyEvents`' `player_death` routing has no downed-companion case; the manual End Combat exit from a `lowLevelDefeat` hero mid-fight is unpinned.
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) `terminalState`'s dying branch returns `'defeat'` when `lowLevelSolo` — better, one engine predicate ("this 0-HP moment is defeat or death?") consulted by `terminalState`, `DEATH_SAVE_RESULT`, `rollResolver.resolveDeathSave` (this morning's P2) and `applyEvents`; (2) `isLowLevelSolo` in the `player_death` branch + a DECISIONS ruling on the channel's precondition; (3) revive before the enemy phase; (4) settle the opening-intents rule; (5) the pins.

### cloud-sync (`state/cloudSync.js`, `state/auth.js`, `config/firebase.js`, `firestore.rules`, SettingsModal cloud flows) — Lap 1: correctness & test depth
- **Scope examined:** `cloudSync.js` end to end (chunking, transactional save/delete, chunked + legacy load, list); `auth.js`; `firebase.js` re-init path; `firestore.rules`; SettingsModal `handleSave`/`handleOverwrite`/`handleLoad`/`handleDeleteCloud`/sign-in/`handleUploadLocalSaves`; `cloudSync.test.js` (20) + `cloudSync.nodb.test.js` + `auth.test.js`.
- **Verified fixed since 08-27:** all three queue items — `handleLoad`'s local branch surfaces + catches, the write-side autosave vestiges are gone (legacy guards documented), `auth.test.js` exists. Verified sound: surrogate-safe chunk split, the in-transaction stale-chunk sweep, delete's chunk sweep, the missing-chunk throw → null (a torn concurrent read degrades to a failed load, never a corrupt one — re-verified for shrink AND grow), the rules' `chunks` match, `initializeFirebase`'s same-config reuse vs `deleteApp` on a changed project (live ES bindings keep `db` current).
- **Findings:** no P0/P1.
  - **P2 (the 08-27 asymmetry has two more instances):** `handleSave` (`SettingsModal.jsx:96-125`) and `handleOverwrite` (`:205-224`) are `try { … } finally { … }` with no catch — a rejecting local `saveGame` (IDB error, quota, this morning's leaked-connection class) escapes as an unhandled rejection with zero UI feedback while `isSaving` resets; the cloud half is handled, the local half isn't. Same shape the 08-27 finding fixed for load/delete.
  - **P2 (failure reasons collapse to `false`):** `saveGameToCloud` returns `false` for everything (`cloudSync.js:117-126`) and the UI renders one generic "cloud upload failed (details in browser console)". The two real-world classes need different player actions: `permission-denied` from a pre-chunk `firestore.rules` deploy (the hint exists — console-only), and the ~10 MiB transaction request ceiling that a full-message-history mature campaign will reach (cloud saves carry everything since 2026-08-04; CLAUDE.md calls mature campaigns multi-MB). There is no pre-flight size check and no hint, so that campaign's cloud saves fail silently forever; the code comment defers multi-batch generations. `listCloudSaves` already re-throws for exactly this reason — the save path should carry its reason too.
  - **P2 (minor):** `handleUploadLocalSaves` aborts the whole loop on the first `loadGame` rejection and loses the partial count; a per-slot try/catch would report "uploaded N of M, K failed".
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) catch + `setSyncStatus` in `handleSave`/`handleOverwrite`; (2) `{ ok, reason }` from `saveGameToCloud` (or a typed error), a payload-size pre-flight with an actionable message, tests for both; (3) per-slot isolation in the upload loop.

The runner comment calls the absence deliberate, but the documented reason covers only the transaction guard (`playerActionContext` already carries that).

Your character dies.**" line stamped `isDeathEvent`, and a summary telling the DM "THE PLAYER CHARACTER IS DEAD (the system has recorded it; narrate the death)" — while the system recorded a non-lethal setback and posted "Death save skipped". Rare (needs dying set while a companion stood, then the companion down), consequence is a narrated death the sheet contradicts.

### persistence (`state/persistence.js`, `state/autosaveRuntime.js`, `state/autosavePolicy.js`, `state/GameContext.jsx`, boot/load flows) — Lap 1: correctness & test depth
- **Scope examined:** `persistence.js` end to end (openDB + migration, serialize/metadata, all nine IDB functions, autosave wrappers); `autosaveRuntime.js` + `autosavePolicy.js` end to end; `GameContext.jsx` wiring; `App.jsx` boot `checkSaves` + `handleLoad`; `SettingsModal` load sites; `MARK_MESSAGES_SUMMARIZED` + the runner's `summarizedBoundary` (the `prunedMessageCount` contract); `persistence.test.js` (33), `autosaveRuntime.test.js` (13), `autosavePolicy.test.js` (9).
- **Verified fixed since 08-27:** all three queue items — settings stripped from the snapshot, the strip-`state` `listSaves` projection, the legacy-fallback test + `autosaveRuntime.js` extraction with its suite. Verified sound: `prunedMessageCount` (save-time `filter(summarized).length`) agrees with `MARK_MESSAGES_SUMMARIZED`'s `upTo` because the reducer flags every index below the boundary, hidden and deleted rows included, so the prefix stays contiguous and the 08-31 boundary belt is consistent; commit-time resolution on every write; dirty-flag choreography (clean only when a write lands and the state hasn't moved); the read-path close-on-abort.
- **Findings:**
  - **P1 (the fail-loud contract stops at the boot screen):** `loadAutoSave` turns every IDB failure into `null` (`persistence.js:381-387`) and `checkSaves` (`App.jsx:22-38`) catches a rejecting `listSaves` with only `console.warn`; neither sets `loadError`. A blocked open — the 8s `onblocked` reject the 2026-07-12 fix added specifically to fail loudly — a quota/corruption error, or an evicted DB renders the start screen as "no autosave, no saves": the player sees their campaign gone with no message while the data is intact. The in-game load path (`App.jsx:76-96`) and the cloud list (`:41-52`) both surface errors; the boot path is the one consumer that doesn't. `loadAutoSave`'s null is tested only for the genuinely-missing case (`persistence.test.js:355`).
  - **P2 (leaked connection on a synchronous throw):** every IDB function does `const db = await openDB()` and then synchronous `db.transaction`/`put`/`delete`/snapshot-building inside the Promise executor with no try/catch (`persistence.js:168-201` and siblings). A sync throw — `DataCloneError` when a non-cloneable value reaches structured clone, `InvalidStateError` if the connection is closing under a cross-tab `versionchange`, a plain `TypeError` on a bad snapshot — rejects the promise but never calls `db.close()`: the same leak class the 2026-07-12 read-path fixes closed for request errors. `persistence.test.js:359` (`autoSave(null)`) walks straight through this path (`TypeError` on `null.messages`) and asserts only the `false`. Compounding it, no connection sets `db.onversionchange = () => db.close()`, so a leaked one blocks every other tab's upgrade until that 8s timeout.
  - **P2 (the one-time migration has no failure path):** `onupgradeneeded` (`persistence.js:78-96`) copies every payload into `savePayloads` before `cursor.update` strips it — peak ≈2× every save inside one versionchange transaction — with no `onerror` on the cursor or the puts. If it aborts (quota on a device already near budget with multi-MB campaigns), the open fails, the upgrade re-runs on EVERY open, and every save/load/autosave fails forever with no self-heal (red toast each turn). The migration test (`persistence.test.js:273`) covers the happy path only.
  - **P2 (write amplification on the flush path — Lap 3 preview):** `flush({ action })` cancels the pending debounce and writes, but the action's own re-render then calls `noteStateChange` → dirty + a fresh 2s timer → a second full-snapshot write per flushed turn (`autosaveRuntime.js:37-47,59-81`; the comment at 43-44 acknowledges it).
- **Suggested improvements:** (1) distinguish missing from failed in `loadAutoSave` (or let the caller catch), set `loadError` in the boot catch, test a rejecting `listSaves` at boot; (2) a `withDb(fn)` helper that closes on any throw + `onversionchange` + assert-close in the existing `autoSave(null)` test; (3) per-record put error → leave the record legacy (`loadGame`'s embedded-state fallback already covers it) + a failing-put-still-opens test; (4) a landed-source skip in `noteStateChange`.
